decls.statement: theorem isFiniteMeasure_bind_withDensity (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∫⁻ x, f x ∂ν ≠ ⊤) : IsFiniteMeasure ((ν.withDensity f).bind ⇑κ)
decls.doc: `(f ν) π⋆` is a finite measure as soon as `f` has finite `ν`-integral.

decls.name: bindDensity
decls.statement: noncomputable def bindDensity (κ : Kernel α α) (ν : Measure α) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : α → ℝ≥0∞
decls.doc: **The density action `T f := d((f ν) π⋆)/dν`** of the main text (`universality.tex:26–27`), on non-negative densities.

decls.name: bindDensity_congr
decls.statement: theorem bindDensity_congr (κ : Kernel α α) (ν : Measure α) {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h : f =ᵐ[ν] g) : bindDensity κ ν f = bindDensity κ ν g
decls.doc: `T` depends on `f` only through its `ν`-a.e.

decls.name: measurable_bindDensity
decls.statement: theorem measurable_bindDensity (κ : Kernel α α) (ν : Measure α) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : Measurable (bindDensity κ ν f)
decls.doc: `T f` is measurable, with no hypothesis on `f`: a Radon–Nikodym derivative always is.

decls.name: withDensity_bindDensity
decls.statement: theorem withDensity_bindDensity (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ν.withDensity (bindDensity κ ν f) = (ν.withDensity f).bind ⇑κ
decls.doc: **`T f` is a genuine density for `(f ν) π⋆`.** This is the well-definedness assertion of `universality.tex:26–27`.

decls.name: lintegral_bindDensity
decls.statement: theorem lintegral_bindDensity (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ x, bindDensity κ ν f x ∂ν = ∫⁻ x, f x ∂ν
decls.doc: **`∫ T f dν = ∫ f dν`** — the non-negative half of `hint`.

decls.name: bindDensity_one
decls.statement: theorem bindDensity_one (κ : Kernel α α) {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) : bindDensity κ ν 1 =ᵐ[ν] 1
decls.doc: **`T 𝟏 = 𝟏`** — the non-negative half of `hone`, and pure invariance: `𝟏 ν = ν`, so `(𝟏 ν) π⋆ = ν π⋆ = ν` and `dν/dν = 𝟏`.

decls.name: bindDensity_zero
decls.statement: theorem bindDensity_zero (κ : Kernel α α) (ν : Measure α) : bindDensity κ ν 0 =ᵐ[ν] 0
decls.doc: `T 0 = 0`: the zero density pushes to the zero measure.

decls.name: bindDensity_add
decls.statement: theorem bindDensity_add (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f ν) (hfi : ∫⁻ x, f x ∂ν ≠ ⊤) (hgi : ∫⁻ x, g x ∂ν ≠ ⊤) : bindDensity κ ν (f + g) =ᵐ[ν] bindDensity κ ν f + bindDensity κ ν g
decls.doc: **`T` is additive**, `ν`-a.e., on densities of finite integral.

decls.name: bindDensity_smul
decls.statement: theorem bindDensity_smul (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] {c : ℝ≥0∞} (hc : c ≠ ⊤) {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f ν) (hfi : ∫⁻ x, f x ∂ν ≠ ⊤) : bindDensity κ ν (c • f) =ᵐ[ν] c • bindDensity κ ν f
decls.doc: **`T` is positively homogeneous**, `ν`-a.e., for a finite scalar.

decls.name: densityAction
decls.statement: noncomputable def densityAction (κ : Kernel α α) (ν : Measure α) (f : α → ℝ) : α → ℝ
decls.doc: **The density action `P⋆ f := d((f ν) π⋆)/dν` on signed densities.** A signed density is split into its positive and negative parts, each pushed by `T = bindDensity`, and the two densities subtracted.

decls.name: densityAction_congr
decls.statement: theorem densityAction_congr (κ : Kernel α α) (ν : Measure α) {f g : α → ℝ} (h : f =ᵐ[ν] g) : densityAction κ ν f = densityAction κ ν g
decls.doc: `P⋆` depends on `f` only through its `ν`-a.e.

decls.name: measurable_densityAction
decls.statement: theorem measurable_densityAction (κ : Kernel α α) (ν : Measure α) (f : α → ℝ) : Measurable (densityAction κ ν f)
decls.doc: `P⋆ f` is measurable, with no hypothesis on `f`.

decls.name: lintegral_ofReal_ne_top
decls.statement: theorem lintegral_ofReal_ne_top {ν : Measure α} {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) : ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (f x) ∂ν ≠ ⊤
decls.doc: The positive part of an integrable function has finite `ν`-integral.

decls.name: bindDensity_ofReal_lt_top
decls.statement: theorem bindDensity_ofReal_lt_top (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) : ∀ᵐ x ∂ν, bindDensity κ ν (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) x < ⊤
decls.doc: `T f⁺` has finite `ν`-integral, hence is a.e.

decls.name: integrable_toReal_bindDensity
decls.statement: theorem integrable_toReal_bindDensity (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) : Integrable (fun x => (bindDensity κ ν (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) x).toReal) ν
decls.doc: `(T f⁺).toReal` is `ν`-integrable, with `∫ (T f⁺).toReal dν = ∫ f⁺ dν`.

decls.name: integral_toReal_bindDensity
decls.statement: theorem integral_toReal_bindDensity (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) : ∫ x, (bindDensity κ ν (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) x).toReal ∂ν = (∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (f x) ∂ν).toReal

decls.name: integral_densityAction
decls.statement: theorem integral_densityAction (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) : ∫ x, densityAction κ ν f x ∂ν = ∫ x, f x ∂ν
decls.doc: **`hint`, in the paper's own terms**: `∫ P⋆ f dν = ∫ f dν` for every `ν`-integrable `f`.

decls.name: densityAction_one
decls.statement: theorem densityAction_one (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) : densityAction κ ν 1 =ᵐ[ν] 1

decls.name: max_add_aux
decls.statement: theorem max_add_aux (u v : ℝ) : max (u + v) 0 + max (-u) 0 + max (-v) 0 = max (-(u + v)) 0 + max u 0 + max v 0
decls.doc: The real identity behind additivity of `P⋆`: `(u+v)⁺ + u⁻ + v⁻ = (u+v)⁻ + u⁺ + v⁺`.

decls.name: ofReal_add_aux
decls.statement: theorem ofReal_add_aux (u v : ℝ) : ENNReal.ofReal (u + v) + ENNReal.ofReal (-u) + ENNReal.ofReal (-v) = ENNReal.ofReal (-(u + v)) + ENNReal.ofReal u + ENNReal.ofReal v
decls.doc: The same identity in `ℝ≥0∞`, which is where `T` consumes it.

decls.name: lintegral_add_ne_top
decls.statement: theorem lintegral_add_ne_top {ν : Measure α} {u v : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hu : AEMeasurable u ν) (hun : ∫⁻ x, u x ∂ν ≠ ⊤) (hvn : ∫⁻ x, v x ∂ν ≠ ⊤) : ∫⁻ x, (u + v) x ∂ν ≠ ⊤
decls.doc: `∫ (u + v) dν` is finite when both summands are.

decls.name: bindDensity_add₃
decls.statement: theorem bindDensity_add₃ (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] {u v w : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hu : AEMeasurable u ν) (hv : AEMeasurable v ν) (hun : ∫⁻ x, u x ∂ν ≠ ⊤) (hvn : ∫⁻ x, v x ∂ν ≠ ⊤) (hwn : ∫⁻ x, w x ∂ν ≠ ⊤) : bindDensity κ ν (u + v + w) =ᵐ[ν] bindDensity κ ν u + bindDensity κ ν v + bindDensity κ ν w
decls.doc: `T` on a sum of three densities of finite integral.

decls.name: aemeasurable_ofReal
decls.statement: theorem aemeasurable_ofReal {ν : Measure α} {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) : AEMeasurable (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) ν
decls.doc: The positive part of an integrable function is `ν`-a.e.

decls.name: densityAction_add
decls.statement: theorem densityAction_add (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) {f g : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) (hg : Integrable g ν) : densityAction κ ν (fun x => f x + g x) =ᵐ[ν] fun x => densityAction κ ν f x + densityAction κ ν g x
decls.doc: **`P⋆` is additive**, `ν`-a.e., on `ν`-integrable densities.

decls.name: densityAction_neg
decls.statement: theorem densityAction_neg (κ : Kernel α α) (ν : Measure α) (f : α → ℝ) : densityAction κ ν (fun x => -f x) = fun x => -densityAction κ ν f x
decls.doc: `P⋆(-f) = -P⋆ f`, by definition: negation swaps the positive and negative parts.

decls.name: densityAction_smul_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem densityAction_smul_nonneg (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) : densityAction κ ν (fun x => r * f x) =ᵐ[ν] fun x => r * densityAction κ ν f x
decls.doc: `P⋆` is homogeneous under a non-negative scalar.

decls.name: densityAction_smul
decls.statement: theorem densityAction_smul (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] {ν : Measure α} [SigmaFinite ν] (r : ℝ) {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) : densityAction κ ν (fun x => r * f x) =ᵐ[ν] fun x => r * densityAction κ ν f x
decls.doc: **`P⋆` is homogeneous**, `ν`-a.e., under every real scalar.

decls.name: IsBoundedDensityAction
decls.statement: structure IsBoundedDensityAction (κ : Kernel α α) (ν : Measure α) (p : ℝ≥0∞) (C : ℝ) : Prop
decls.doc: **The paper's boundedness hypothesis on the parameterization**, and the only hypothesis of `theo:universality_L2_full` that this file assumes rather than derives.

decls.name: densityActionLM
decls.statement: noncomputable def densityActionLM (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) : Lp ℝ p ν →ₗ[ℝ] Lp ℝ p ν
decls.doc: `P⋆` as a linear map on `L^p(ν)`.

decls.name: densityActionCLM
decls.statement: noncomputable def densityActionCLM (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) : Lp ℝ p ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ p ν
decls.doc: **`P⋆` as a `ContinuousLinearMap` on `L^p(ν)`**, with the paper's own operator-norm bound `C` as the continuity constant.

decls.name: norm_densityActionCLM_le
decls.statement: theorem norm_densityActionCLM_le (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) : ‖densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb‖ ≤ C
decls.doc: `‖P⋆‖_{L^p→L^p} ≤ C`: the paper's constant bounds the operator norm, as rule 3 asks.

decls.name: coeFn_densityActionCLM
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_densityActionCLM (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) (F : Lp ℝ p ν) : ⇑(densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb F) =ᵐ[ν] densityAction κ ν ⇑F
decls.doc: The `L^p` operator applied to `F` is represented by `P⋆` applied to any representative.

decls.name: densityActionCLM_constOne
decls.statement: theorem densityActionCLM_constOne (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) : densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb (constOne ν p) = constOne ν p
decls.doc: **`hone` on `L^p(ν)`**: `P⋆ 𝟏 = 𝟏`, the paper's `(Id − P⋆) 𝟏 = 0` (`proofs.tex:100`).

decls.name: integral_densityActionCLM
decls.statement: theorem integral_densityActionCLM (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) (F : Lp ℝ p ν) : ∫ x, (densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb F) x ∂ν = ∫ x, F x ∂ν
decls.doc: **`hint` on `L^p(ν)`**: `∫ P⋆ f dν = ∫ f dν`.

decls.name: weaklyUniversal_of_kernel
decls.statement: theorem weaklyUniversal_of_kernel (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) (hsum : Summable fun n : ℕ => ‖(densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb) ^ n - meanProj ν p‖) (hp : p ≠ ⊤) : WeaklyUniversal (densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb) (meanProj ν p)
decls.doc: **`theo:universality_L2_full`'s weak half, from the paper's own hypotheses about the kernel.** `π⋆` is a Markov kernel, `ν` is finite and `π⋆`-invariant, `P⋆` is bounded on `L^p(ν)` with constant `C` — the paper's requirement on the parameterization — and the mixing coefficients `β_n = ‖P⋆^n − Π‖` are summable.

decls.name: weaklyUniversalAt_of_kernel
decls.statement: theorem weaklyUniversalAt_of_kernel (κ : Kernel α α) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) (hsum : Summable fun n : ℕ => ‖(densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb) ^ n - meanProj ν p‖) (hp : p ≠ ⊤) {f_init f_term : Lp ℝ p ν} (hmass : ∫ x, f_init x ∂ν = ∫ x, f_term x ∂ν) : WeaklyUniversalAt (densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb) (f_term - f_init)
decls.doc: **The same, at one admissible pair**: two densities in `L^p(ν)` of equal total mass are joined to arbitrary accuracy by a non-negative outflow against the kernel `π⋆`.

decls.name: bind_id
decls.statement: theorem bind_id (ν : Measure α) : ν.bind ⇑(Kernel.id : Kernel α α) = ν
decls.doc: Every measure is invariant under the identity kernel.

decls.name: bindDensity_id
decls.statement: theorem bindDensity_id (ν : Measure α) [SigmaFinite ν] {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f ν) : bindDensity (Kernel.id : Kernel α α) ν f =ᵐ[ν] f
decls.doc: The identity kernel has the identity density action on non-negative densities.

decls.name: densityAction_id
decls.statement: theorem densityAction_id (ν : Measure α) [SigmaFinite ν] {f : α → ℝ} (hf : AEMeasurable f ν) : densityAction (Kernel.id : Kernel α α) ν f =ᵐ[ν] f
decls.doc: The identity kernel has the identity density action.

decls.name: isBoundedDensityAction_id
decls.statement: theorem isBoundedDensityAction_id (ν : Measure α) [SigmaFinite ν] (p : ℝ≥0∞) : IsBoundedDensityAction (Kernel.id : Kernel α α) ν p 1
decls.doc: **`IsBoundedDensityAction` is satisfiable**, so `weaklyUniversal_of_kernel` is not vacuous: the identity kernel is Markov, every measure is invariant under it (`bind_id`), and its density action is the identity, of operator norm `1`.

files.title: The mixing sum, and the Poisson equation it solves
variables: variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E}

decls.name: Mixing
decls.statement: structure Mixing {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) : Prop
decls.doc: The hypothesis shared by `lem:sigma_mixing` and Step 1 of `theo:universality_L2_full`: a bounded operator `P` and a projection `Pi` onto its invariant vectors, whose mixing coefficients `n ↦ ‖P ^ n - Pi‖` are summable.

decls.name: beta
decls.statement: noncomputable def beta (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The mixing coefficients `β_n = ‖P ^ n - Pi‖` of `equ:mixing_coefficients`.

decls.name: B
decls.statement: noncomputable def B (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) : ℝ
decls.doc: The mixing sum `B = ∑_{n ≥ 0} β_n` of `equ:mixing_coefficients`; the appendix writes it `B̂` at `p = 2`.

decls.name: summable_beta
decls.statement: theorem summable_beta (h : Mixing P Pi) : Summable (beta P Pi)

decls.name: beta_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem beta_nonneg (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ beta P Pi n

decls.name: B_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem B_nonneg (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) : 0 ≤ B P Pi

decls.name: summable_terms
decls.statement: theorem summable_terms [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) : Summable fun n : ℕ => P ^ n - Pi
decls.doc: The family `n ↦ P ^ n - Pi` is summable: absolutely so, by hypothesis.

decls.name: S
decls.statement: noncomputable def S (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) : E →L[ℝ] E
decls.doc: The **mixing sum operator** `S = ∑_{n ≥ 0} (P^n - Pi)` of `equ:poisson`.

decls.name: tendsto_partialSum
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_partialSum [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) : Tendsto (partialSum P Pi) atTop (𝓝 (S P Pi))
decls.doc: `S` is the limit of `GFNBounds.Doubling.partialSum`, which is the hypothesis every result of `Doubling/Operator.lean` consumes.

decls.name: tendsto_pow
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_pow [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => P ^ n) atTop (𝓝 Pi)
decls.doc: Summable mixing forces `P ^ n → Pi` in operator norm — the appendix's `‖P^{N+1} - Π‖ = β_{N+1} → 0`.

decls.name: proj_idem
decls.statement: theorem proj_idem [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) : Pi * Pi = Pi
decls.doc: `Pi` is idempotent: `P ^ n → Pi` while `P ^ (n+1) Pi = Pi` throughout.

decls.name: norm_S_le
decls.statement: theorem norm_S_le [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) : ‖S P Pi‖ ≤ B P Pi
decls.doc: `‖S‖ ≤ B`: the operator-norm bound behind `theo:universality_L2_full`'s `‖Sθ‖ ≤ B_p ‖θ‖`.

decls.name: norm_S_apply_le
decls.statement: theorem norm_S_apply_le [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) (θ : E) : ‖S P Pi θ‖ ≤ B P Pi * ‖θ‖
decls.doc: `‖S θ‖ ≤ B ‖θ‖`, which is how `theo:universality_L2_full` states the bound.

decls.name: poisson_right
decls.statement: theorem poisson_right [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) : S P Pi * (1 - P) = 1 - Pi
decls.doc: **The Poisson equation, right form**: `S (1 - P) = 1 - Pi`.

decls.name: poisson_left
decls.statement: theorem poisson_left [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) : (1 - P) * S P Pi = 1 - Pi
decls.doc: **The Poisson equation, left form**: `(1 - P) S = 1 - Pi`.

decls.name: poisson_right_apply
decls.statement: theorem poisson_right_apply [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) (θ : E) : S P Pi ((1 - P) θ) = θ - Pi θ
decls.doc: The Poisson equation, applied: `S ((1 - P) θ) = θ - Pi θ`.

decls.name: poisson_left_apply
decls.statement: theorem poisson_left_apply [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) (θ : E) : (1 - P) (S P Pi θ) = θ - Pi θ
decls.doc: The Poisson equation, applied on the other side: `(1 - P) (S θ) = θ - Pi θ`.

decls.name: poisson_solved
decls.statement: theorem poisson_solved [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) {θ : E} (hθ : Pi θ = 0) : (1 - P) (S P Pi θ) = θ
decls.doc: **The Poisson equation solves exactly on mean-zero data**, the form Step 2 consumes: if `Pi θ = 0` then `(1 - P) (S θ) = θ`.

decls.name: coercivity
decls.statement: theorem coercivity [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) (x : E) : ‖x - Pi x‖ ≤ B P Pi * ‖(1 - P) x‖
decls.doc: **Mixing controls coercivity** — the "consequently" of `lem:sigma_mixing`, and the only part of it the paper's downstream consumers use (`proofs.tex:872`).

decls.name: coercivity_div
decls.statement: theorem coercivity_div [CompleteSpace E] (h : Mixing P Pi) (hB : 0 < B P Pi) (x : E) : ‖x - Pi x‖ / B P Pi ≤ ‖(1 - P) x‖
decls.doc: The quotient form of `lem:sigma_mixing`'s display.

files.title: A stable `L^q` flow-matching loss controls the sampling error and the initial-mass defect
variables: variable {ν : Measure α} {e k : α → ℝ}

decls.name: tvD
decls.statement: noncomputable def tvD (ν : Measure α) (f g : α → ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The ½-convention total variation of `app:notation`**, read between two densities against a common dominating measure: `TV(f·ν ‖ g·ν) = ½ ∫ |f − g| dν`.

decls.name: tvD_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem tvD_nonneg (ν : Measure α) (f g : α → ℝ) : 0 ≤ tvD ν f g

decls.name: tvD_comm
decls.statement: theorem tvD_comm (ν : Measure α) (f g : α → ℝ) : tvD ν f g = tvD ν g f

decls.name: tvD_triangle
decls.statement: theorem tvD_triangle {ν : Measure α} {f₁ f₂ f₃ : α → ℝ} (h₁ : Integrable (fun x => f₁ x - f₂ x) ν) (h₂ : Integrable (fun x => f₂ x - f₃ x) ν) : tvD ν f₁ f₃ ≤ tvD ν f₁ f₂ + tvD ν f₂ f₃
decls.doc: **The triangle inequality Step 2 opens with** (`proofs.tex:209–212`), for densities against a common measure.

decls.name: tvD_normalization
decls.statement: theorem tvD_normalization {ν : Measure α} {f g : α → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) (hg : Integrable g ν) (hg0 : 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] g) (hb : b = ∫ x, g x ∂ν) (ha0 : 0 < a) (hb0 : 0 < b) : tvD ν (fun x => f x / a) (fun x => g x / b) ≤ ((∫ x, |f x - g x| ∂ν) + |a - b|) / (2 * a)
decls.doc: **`equ:normalization_lemma`, first inequality** (`proofs.tex:217–220`): for `α = f·ν` and `β = g·ν` non-negative and finite with masses `a, b > 0`, `TV(α/a ‖ β/b) ≤ (‖α − β‖_{L¹} + |a − b|)/(2a)`, by the paper's own splitting `β/b − α/a = (β − α)/a + β(1/b − 1/a)`.

decls.name: tvD_normalization_le
decls.statement: theorem tvD_normalization_le {ν : Measure α} {f g : α → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hf : Integrable f ν) (hg : Integrable g ν) (hg0 : 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] g) (ha : a = ∫ x, f x ∂ν) (hb : b = ∫ x, g x ∂ν) (ha0 : 0 < a) (hb0 : 0 < b) : tvD ν (fun x => f x / a) (fun x => g x / b) ≤ (∫ x, |f x - g x| ∂ν) / a
decls.doc: **`equ:normalization_lemma`, second inequality** (`proofs.tex:217–220`): `TV(α/a ‖ β/b) ≤ ‖α − β‖_{L¹}/a`, by `|a − b| ≤ ‖α − β‖_{L¹}`.

decls.name: negPart_le_abs_sub
decls.statement: theorem negPart_le_abs_sub {x y : ℝ} (hy : 0 ≤ y) : max (-x) 0 ≤ |x - y|
decls.doc: **Step 1's first pointwise inequality** (`proofs.tex:204`): `k ≥ 0` gives `e⁻ ≤ |e − k|`, because on `{e < 0}` one has `|e − k| = k − e ≥ −e`.

decls.name: abs_sub_posPart_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_sub_posPart_le {x y : ℝ} (hy : 0 ≤ y) : |y - max x 0| ≤ |x - y|
decls.doc: **Step 1's second pointwise inequality** (`proofs.tex:204`): `x ↦ x⁺` is `1`-Lipschitz and `k⁺ = k`, so `|e⁺ − k| ≤ |e − k|`.

decls.name: posPart_mass
decls.statement: theorem posPart_mass (he : Integrable e ν) : ∫ x, max (e x) 0 ∂ν = (∫ x, e x ∂ν) + ∫ x, max (-e x) 0 ∂ν
decls.doc: **`equ:mass_identity`, Step 0** (`proofs.tex:200–202`): `E⁺` and `E⁻` having disjoint supports and `E(𝒮) = z`, the corrected terminal flow has mass `κ̂(𝒮) = z + E⁻(𝒮) ≥ z`.

decls.name: negMass_le
decls.statement: theorem negMass_le (he : Integrable e ν) (hk : Integrable k ν) (hk0 : 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k) : ∫ x, max (-e x) 0 ∂ν ≤ ∫ x, |e x - k x| ∂ν
decls.doc: **`equ:two_dominations`, first half** (`proofs.tex:205–207`): `δF_init(𝒮) = E⁻(𝒮) ≤ Δ`.

decls.name: hatDist_le
decls.statement: theorem hatDist_le (he : Integrable e ν) (hk : Integrable k ν) (hk0 : 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k) : ∫ x, |k x - max (e x) 0| ∂ν ≤ ∫ x, |e x - k x| ∂ν
decls.doc: **`equ:two_dominations`, second half** (`proofs.tex:205–207`): `‖κ̂ − κ‖_{L¹(ν_B)} ≤ Δ`.

decls.name: mass_defect_le
decls.statement: theorem mass_defect_le (he : Integrable e ν) (hk : Integrable k ν) : |(∫ x, e x ∂ν) - ∫ x, k x ∂ν| ≤ ∫ x, |e x - k x| ∂ν
decls.doc: **`equ:mass_defect`** (`proofs.tex:226–228`): `|z − t| = |∫(e − k) dν_B| ≤ Δ`.

decls.name: normalization_bound
decls.statement: theorem normalization_bound (he : Integrable e ν) (hk : Integrable k ν) (hk0 : 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k) {t zhat : ℝ} (ht : t = ∫ x, k x ∂ν) (hzh : zhat = ∫ x, max (e x) 0 ∂ν) (ht0 : 0 < t) (hzh0 : 0 < zhat) : tvD ν (fun x => k x / t) (fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) ≤ (∫ x, |e x - k x| ∂ν) / t
decls.doc: **Term (ii) of Step 2** (`proofs.tex:217–221`): `TV(κ/t ‖ κ̂/κ̂(𝒮)) ≤ Δ/t`, by `equ:normalization_lemma` at `α = κ`, `β = κ̂` and `equ:two_dominations`.

decls.name: tv_le_two_fmL1
decls.statement: theorem tv_le_two_fmL1 (he : Integrable e ν) (hk : Integrable k ν) (hk0 : 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k) {z t zhat tv tvNC : ℝ} (hz : z = ∫ x, e x ∂ν) (ht : t = ∫ x, k x ∂ν) (hzh : zhat = ∫ x, max (e x) 0 ∂ν) (hz0 : 0 < z) (ht0 : 0 < t) (hNC : tvNC ≤ (∫ x, max (-e x) 0 ∂ν) / zhat) (htri : tv ≤ tvNC + tvD ν (fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) (fun x => k x / t)) : tv ≤ 2 * (∫ x, |e x - k x| ∂ν) / t
decls.doc: **`equ:tv_chain` closed at `2Δ/t`, Step 2 in full** (`proofs.tex:209–232`): `TV(s_τ ‖ κ/t) ≤ Δ/(z + Δ) + Δ/t ≤ 2Δ/t`, with `Δ := ‖e − k‖_{L¹(ν_B)}`.

decls.name: integral_le_measure_rpow_mul
decls.statement: theorem integral_le_measure_rpow_mul {q : ℝ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {h : α → ℝ} (hh0 : 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] h) (hmem : MemLp h (ENNReal.ofReal q) ν) : ∫ x, h x ∂ν ≤ ν.real Set.univ ^ (1 - 1 / q) * (∫ x, h x ^ q ∂ν) ^ (1 / q)
decls.doc: **Step 3, first Hölder** (`proofs.tex:236`): on a finite measure, `∫ h dν ≤ ν(𝒮)^{1−1/q} ‖h‖_{L^q(ν)}` for `h ≥ 0` and `1 ≤ q < ∞`, by Hölder against the constant `1` with the conjugate exponents `q` and `q/(q−1)`.

decls.name: integral_le_of_le_smul
decls.statement: theorem integral_le_of_le_smul {νT : Measure α} {M : ℝ≥0} (hdom : ν ≤ (M : ℝ≥0∞) • νT) {f : α → ℝ} (hf0 : 0 ≤ᵐ[νT] f) (hint : Integrable f νT) : ∫ x, f x ∂ν ≤ (M : ℝ) * ∫ x, f x ∂νT
decls.doc: **Step 3, the change of measure** (`proofs.tex:237`): with `ν_B ≤ M ν_T`, an integral of a non-negative function against `ν_B` is at most `M` times its integral against `ν_T`.

decls.name: holderConst
decls.statement: noncomputable def holderConst (ν : Measure α) (M : ℝ≥0) (q : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`equ:stable_constants`, `C₀`** (`proofs.tex:152–156`): `C₀ = ν_B(𝒮)^{1−1/q} ‖dν_B/dν_T‖^{1/q}_{L^∞(ν_T)}`, with the `L^∞` norm carried by `M`.

decls.name: stableConst
decls.statement: noncomputable def stableConst (ν : Measure α) (M : ℝ≥0) (q t : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`equ:stable_constants`, `C`** (`proofs.tex:152–156`): `C = 2C₀/κ(𝒮)`.

decls.name: stableLoss
decls.statement: noncomputable def stableLoss (νT : Measure α) (q : ℝ) (e k : α → ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The stable loss `𝓛` of `equ:FMloss`** as `proofs.tex:193` reads it, `𝓛 = ‖e − k‖_{L^q(ν_T)}`, at `q < ∞`.

decls.name: fmL1_le_holderConst_mul_loss
decls.statement: theorem fmL1_le_holderConst_mul_loss {νT : Measure α} {M : ℝ≥0} {q : ℝ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (hdom : ν ≤ (M : ℝ≥0∞) • νT) (hmem : MemLp (fun x => e x - k x) (ENNReal.ofReal q) νT) : ∫ x, |e x - k x| ∂ν ≤ holderConst ν M q * stableLoss νT q e k
decls.doc: **Step 3 in full** (`proofs.tex:234–239`): `Δ ≤ C₀ 𝓛`, the two Hölder applications composed.

decls.name: mass_floor
decls.statement: theorem mass_floor {νT : Measure α} {M : ℝ≥0} {q z t : ℝ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (hdom : ν ≤ (M : ℝ≥0∞) • νT) (hmem : MemLp (fun x => e x - k x) (ENNReal.ofReal q) νT) (he : Integrable e ν) (hk : Integrable k ν) (hz : z = ∫ x, e x ∂ν) (ht : t = ∫ x, k x ∂ν) : |z - t| ≤ holderConst ν M q * stableLoss νT q e k
decls.doc: **`equ:mass_floor`** (`proofs.tex:164–166`), the second display of item (1) of **`theo:RL_CV_bound_full`**: `|F_init(𝒮) − κ(𝒮)| ≤ C₀ 𝓛` .

decls.name: stable_bound
decls.statement: theorem stable_bound {νT : Measure α} {M : ℝ≥0} {q z t zhat tv tvNC : ℝ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (hdom : ν ≤ (M : ℝ≥0∞) • νT) (hmem : MemLp (fun x => e x - k x) (ENNReal.ofReal q) νT) (he : Integrable e ν) (hk : Integrable k ν) (hk0 : 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k) (hz : z = ∫ x, e x ∂ν) (ht : t = ∫ x, k x ∂ν) (hzh : zhat = ∫ x, max (e x) 0 ∂ν) (hz0 : 0 < z) (ht0 : 0 < t) (hNC : tvNC ≤ (∫ x, max (-e x) 0 ∂ν) / zhat) (htri : tv ≤ tvNC + tvD ν (fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) (fun x => k x / t)) : tv ≤ stableConst ν M q t * stableLoss νT q e k
decls.doc: **`equ:stable_bound`** (`proofs.tex:160–162`), the first display of item (1) of **`theo:RL_CV_bound_full`**: `TV(s_τ ‖ κ/t) ≤ C 𝓛`, `C = 2C₀/t` .

files.title: Strong universality at `p = +∞`, and the transfer of the realized outflow to every `L^r`
variables: variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [Lattice E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
variable {r : ℝ≥0∞} [Fact (1 ≤ r)] {P : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ ⊤ ν}

decls.name: ae_le_norm_top
decls.statement: theorem ae_le_norm_top (g : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) : ∀ᵐ x ∂ν, g x ≤ ‖g‖
decls.doc: **`g ≤ ‖g‖` a.e., on `L^∞(ν)`.** The essential supremum dominates a.e., and on `L^∞` it is finite, so the `ℝ≥0∞` inequality `‖g x‖ₑ ≤ eLpNormEssSup g ν` may be read in `ℝ`.

decls.name: le_norm_smul_constOne
decls.statement: theorem le_norm_smul_constOne (g : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) : g ≤ ‖g‖ • constOne ν ⊤
decls.doc: **The order hypothesis of `stronglyUniversalAt_of_le`, discharged at `p = +∞`**: `g ≤ ‖g‖ • 𝟏` in the `L^∞(ν)` order.

decls.name: stronglyUniversalAt_top
decls.statement: theorem stronglyUniversalAt_top {P Pi : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} {θ : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} (h : Mixing P Pi) (hone : P (constOne ν ⊤) = constOne ν ⊤) (hθ : Pi θ = 0) : StronglyUniversalAt P θ
decls.doc: **`theo:universality_L2_full`'s `p = +∞` clause, at one admissible pair.** "Taking `η := ‖Sθ‖_{L^∞(ν_B)}` gives `δf_init = δf_term = 0`, and the flow-matching constraint holds exactly" (`proofs.tex:73`).

decls.name: StronglyUniversal
decls.statement: def StronglyUniversal (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) : Prop
decls.doc: **`def:universality`, strong form, with its pair quantifier closed**: the family `Θ = {P} × E⁺` is strongly universal when *every* admissible pair is realized exactly — not merely approached.

decls.name: StronglyUniversal.weaklyUniversal
decls.statement: theorem StronglyUniversal.weaklyUniversal [HasSolidNorm E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} (h : StronglyUniversal P Pi) : WeaklyUniversal P Pi

decls.name: stronglyUniversal_top
decls.statement: theorem stronglyUniversal_top {P Pi : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} (h : Mixing P Pi) (hone : P (constOne ν ⊤) = constOne ν ⊤) : StronglyUniversal P Pi
decls.doc: **`theo:universality_L2_full`'s `p = +∞` clause, for the family**: under summable `L^∞`-mixing and with `P` fixing the constants, `Θ = {P} × L^∞_+(ν)` is strongly universal.

decls.name: stronglyUniversal_of_kernel_top
decls.statement: theorem stronglyUniversal_of_kernel_top (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν ⊤ C) (hsum : Summable fun n : ℕ => ‖(densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb) ^ n - meanProj ν ⊤‖) : StronglyUniversal (densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb) (meanProj ν ⊤)
decls.doc: **Strong universality at `p = +∞`, from the paper's hypotheses on the kernel.** `π⋆` a Markov kernel, `ν` finite and `π⋆`-invariant, the density action bounded on `L^∞(ν)`, the mixing coefficients summable there.

decls.name: stronglyUniversalAt_of_kernel_top
decls.statement: theorem stronglyUniversalAt_of_kernel_top (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν ⊤ C) (hsum : Summable fun n : ℕ => ‖(densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb) ^ n - meanProj ν ⊤‖) {f_init f_term : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} (hmass : ∫ x, f_init x ∂ν = ∫ x, f_term x ∂ν) : StronglyUniversalAt (densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb) (f_term - f_init)
decls.doc: **The same at one admissible pair**, in the paper's own terms: two densities in `L^∞(ν)` of equal total mass are joined *exactly* — not approximately — by a non-negative outflow.

decls.name: inclTop
decls.statement: noncomputable def inclTop (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (r : ℝ≥0∞) (f : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) : Lp ℝ r ν
decls.doc: **The inclusion `L^∞(ν) ↪ L^r(ν)`**, `ν` finite.

decls.name: memLp_of_top
decls.statement: theorem memLp_of_top (r : ℝ≥0∞) (f : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) : MemLp (⇑f) r ν
decls.doc: An `L^∞(ν)` function is in every `L^r(ν)`: finiteness of `ν` and nothing else.

decls.name: coeFn_inclTop
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_inclTop (r : ℝ≥0∞) (f : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) : ⇑(inclTop ν r f) =ᵐ[ν] ⇑f

decls.name: inclTop_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem inclTop_nonneg {r : ℝ≥0∞} {f : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} (hf : 0 ≤ f) : 0 ≤ inclTop ν r f
decls.doc: The inclusion is order-preserving, the `Lp` order being the a.e.

decls.name: coeFn_defect
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_defect {p : ℝ≥0∞} [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (P : Lp ℝ p ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ p ν) (θ fout : Lp ℝ p ν) : ⇑(defect P θ fout) =ᵐ[ν] fun x => (P fout) x - fout x - θ x
decls.doc: The defect, read pointwise: `D = P f_out − f_out − θ` a.e.

decls.name: exists_outflow_memLp_of_top
decls.statement: theorem exists_outflow_memLp_of_top {P Pi : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} {θ : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} (h : Mixing P Pi) (hone : P (constOne ν ⊤) = constOne ν ⊤) (hθ : Pi θ = 0) : ∃ fout : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν, 0 ≤ fout ∧ (∀ r : ℝ≥0∞, MemLp (⇑fout) r ν) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂ν, (P fout) x = fout x + θ x
decls.doc: **The transfer, in the form that assumes nothing at `r`.** The `p = +∞` construction produces a non-negative outflow that lies in *every* `L^r(ν)` and satisfies the flow-matching constraint as an a.e.

decls.name: CompatibleAcrossTop
decls.statement: def CompatibleAcrossTop (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (r : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ r)] (P : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) (Q : Lp ℝ r ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ r ν) : Prop
decls.doc: **The compatibility an operator-level transfer consumes**: `Q` on `L^r(ν)` and `P` on `L^∞(ν)` agree a.e.

decls.name: coeFn_defect_inclTop
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_defect_inclTop (hc : CompatibleAcrossTop ν r P Q) (θ fout : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) : ⇑(defect Q (inclTop ν r θ) (inclTop ν r fout)) =ᵐ[ν] ⇑(defect P θ fout)
decls.doc: The two defects are the same function: `D` at `r` computed on the included data agrees a.e.

decls.name: defect_inclTop_eq_zero
decls.statement: theorem defect_inclTop_eq_zero (hc : CompatibleAcrossTop ν r P Q) {θ fout : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} (h : defect P θ fout = 0) : defect Q (inclTop ν r θ) (inclTop ν r fout) = 0
decls.doc: An exactly flow-matching outflow at `p = +∞` is exactly flow-matching at `r`.

decls.name: stronglyUniversalAt_inclTop
decls.statement: theorem stronglyUniversalAt_inclTop (hc : CompatibleAcrossTop ν r P Q) {θ : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} (h : StronglyUniversalAt P θ) : StronglyUniversalAt Q (inclTop ν r θ)
decls.doc: **The cross-`p` transfer**, `def:universality`'s "realization at one `p` implies it at every `p ≥ 1`": a pair realized exactly in `L^∞(ν)` is realized exactly in `L^r(ν)`, by the same outflow.

decls.name: compatibleAcrossTop_densityActionCLM
decls.statement: theorem compatibleAcrossTop_densityActionCLM (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (r : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ r)] {C C' : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν ⊤ C) (hb' : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν r C') : CompatibleAcrossTop ν r (densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb) (densityActionCLM κ ν r hinv hb')
decls.doc: **The compatibility, discharged for a Markov kernel.** `densityAction κ ν` is a map on functions `α → ℝ` and knows nothing about `p`; `coeFn_densityActionCLM` says the operator at either exponent is represented by it, and `densityAction_congr` says it only sees the a.e.

decls.name: stronglyUniversalAt_of_kernel_Lr
decls.statement: theorem stronglyUniversalAt_of_kernel_Lr (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (r : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ r)] {C C' : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν ⊤ C) (hb' : IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν r C') (hsum : Summable fun n : ℕ => ‖(densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb) ^ n - meanProj ν ⊤‖) {θ : Lp ℝ ⊤ ν} (hθ : meanProj ν ⊤ θ = 0) : StronglyUniversalAt (densityActionCLM κ ν r hinv hb') (inclTop ν r θ)
decls.doc: **`proofs.tex:114`'s last sentence, inside `defect`**: the outflow constructed at `p = +∞` realizes the infimum in `L^r(ν)` as well.

files.title: Universality: the lifted outflow, its defect, and the quantitative bound
variables: variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [Lattice F] [HasSolidNorm F] [IsOrderedAddMonoid F]
variable {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} {one θ : E}

decls.name: norm_posPart_le
decls.statement: theorem norm_posPart_le (a : F) : ‖a⁺‖ ≤ ‖a‖
decls.doc: `‖a⁺‖ ≤ ‖a‖` in a normed lattice: `a⁺ ≤ |a|` and both are non-negative, so the solid axiom applies.

decls.name: norm_negPart_le
decls.statement: theorem norm_negPart_le (a : F) : ‖a⁻‖ ≤ ‖a‖

decls.name: norm_le_norm_posPart_add_norm_negPart
decls.statement: theorem norm_le_norm_posPart_add_norm_negPart (a : F) : ‖a‖ ≤ ‖a⁺‖ + ‖a⁻‖

decls.name: defect
decls.statement: noncomputable def defect (P : E →L[ℝ] E) (θ fout : E) : E
decls.doc: The **flow-matching defect** of an outflow `fout` against the pair `(f_init, f_term)`, written as its density: `D = (P - 1) fout - θ` with `θ = f_term - f_init` (`theo:universality_L2_full`, `proofs.tex:78`).

decls.name: resInit
decls.statement: noncomputable def resInit (P : E →L[ℝ] E) (θ fout : E) : E
decls.doc: The residual against the initial flow, `δf_init = D⁻`.

decls.name: resTerm
decls.statement: noncomputable def resTerm (P : E →L[ℝ] E) (θ fout : E) : E
decls.doc: The residual against the target, `δf_term = D⁺`.

decls.name: norm_defect_le_residuals
decls.statement: theorem norm_defect_le_residuals (P : E →L[ℝ] E) (θ fout : E) : ‖defect P θ fout‖ ≤ ‖resInit P θ fout‖ + ‖resTerm P θ fout‖
decls.doc: `equ:defect_equivalence`, lower half: `‖D‖ ≤ ‖δf_init‖ + ‖δf_term‖`.

decls.name: residuals_le_two_norm_defect
decls.statement: theorem residuals_le_two_norm_defect (P : E →L[ℝ] E) (θ fout : E) : ‖resInit P θ fout‖ + ‖resTerm P θ fout‖ ≤ 2 * ‖defect P θ fout‖
decls.doc: `equ:defect_equivalence`, upper half: `‖δf_init‖ + ‖δf_term‖ ≤ 2 ‖D‖`.

decls.name: WeaklyUniversalAt
decls.statement: def WeaklyUniversalAt (P : E →L[ℝ] E) (θ : E) : Prop
decls.doc: **Weak `L^p`-universality** of `def:universality`, for the family `Θ = {P} × E⁺` that `theo:universality_L2_full` is about: the two residuals can be driven to `0` together by a non-negative outflow.

decls.name: StronglyUniversalAt
decls.statement: def StronglyUniversalAt (P : E →L[ℝ] E) (θ : E) : Prop
decls.doc: **Strong universality**: the infimum is realized — some non-negative outflow makes the flow-matching constraint hold exactly.

decls.name: WeaklyUniversal
decls.statement: def WeaklyUniversal (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) : Prop
decls.doc: **`def:universality`**, weak form, with its quantifier closed: the family `Θ = {P} × E⁺` is weakly `L^p`-universal when *every* admissible pair is reachable.

decls.name: StronglyUniversalAt.weaklyUniversalAt
decls.statement: theorem StronglyUniversalAt.weaklyUniversalAt {P : E →L[ℝ] E} {θ : E} (h : StronglyUniversalAt P θ) : WeaklyUniversalAt P θ

decls.name: liftedOutflow
decls.statement: noncomputable def liftedOutflow (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (one θ : E) (η : ℝ) : E
decls.doc: The **lifted outflow** `f_out^η := (η • 1 - Sθ)⁺` of `theo:universality_L2_full`'s Step 2.

decls.name: truncation
decls.statement: noncomputable def truncation (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (one θ : E) (η : ℝ) : E
decls.doc: The **truncation** `ψ_η := (η • 1 - Sθ)⁻`, which the appendix also writes `(Sθ - η)⁺`.

decls.name: liftedOutflow_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem liftedOutflow_nonneg (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (one θ : E) (η : ℝ) : 0 ≤ liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η

decls.name: truncation_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem truncation_nonneg (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (one θ : E) (η : ℝ) : 0 ≤ truncation P Pi one θ η

decls.name: liftedOutflow_eq
decls.statement: theorem liftedOutflow_eq (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (one θ : E) (η : ℝ) : liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η = (η • one - Mixing.S P Pi θ) + truncation P Pi one θ η
decls.doc: `f_out^η = η • 1 - Sθ + ψ_η`: the appendix's `f_out^η ν_B - ν_∞^η = ψ_η ν_B`.

decls.name: defect_eq_truncation
decls.statement: theorem defect_eq_truncation (h : Mixing P Pi) (hone : P one = one) (hθ : Pi θ = 0) (η : ℝ) : defect P θ (liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η) = P (truncation P Pi one θ η) - truncation P Pi one θ η
decls.doc: **`equ:defect_is_truncation`** — the exact part cancels and only the truncation survives: `D = (P - 1) ψ_η`.

decls.name: residuals_le
decls.statement: theorem residuals_le (h : Mixing P Pi) (hone : P one = one) (hθ : Pi θ = 0) (η : ℝ) : ‖resInit P θ (liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η)‖ + ‖resTerm P θ (liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η)‖ ≤ 2 * (1 + ‖P‖) * ‖truncation P Pi one θ η‖
decls.doc: **`equ:universality_quantitative`**, the bound of `theo:universality_L2_full`: `‖δf_init‖ + ‖δf_term‖ ≤ 2 (1 + ‖P‖) ‖ψ_η‖`.

decls.name: stronglyUniversalAt_of_le
decls.statement: theorem stronglyUniversalAt_of_le (h : Mixing P Pi) (hone : P one = one) (hθ : Pi θ = 0) {η : ℝ} (hle : Mixing.S P Pi θ ≤ η • one) : StronglyUniversalAt P θ
decls.doc: **Strong universality when the truncation vanishes.** If `Sθ ≤ η • 1` for some `η` — which at `p = +∞` is `η := ‖Sθ‖_∞`, the appendix's own choice — then `ψ_η = 0`, the defect is `0` and the flow-matching constraint `equ:FM_const` holds *exactly*.

decls.name: weaklyUniversalAt_of_tendsto
decls.statement: theorem weaklyUniversalAt_of_tendsto (h : Mixing P Pi) (hone : P one = one) (hθ : Pi θ = 0) (hlim : Filter.Tendsto (fun η : ℝ => ‖truncation P Pi one θ η‖) Filter.atTop (𝓝 0)) : WeaklyUniversalAt P θ
decls.doc: **Weak universality from a vanishing truncation.** Step 3 of `theo:universality_L2_full` for `p < ∞`, with the analytic half — `‖ψ_η‖ → 0` as `η → +∞`, which is dominated convergence on a concrete `L^p` — carried as the hypothesis it is.

files.title: The truncation vanishes on `L^p(ν)` for `p < ∞`, and weak universality follows
variables: variable {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] {ν : Measure α} [IsFiniteMeasure ν]

decls.name: constOne
decls.statement: noncomputable def constOne (ν : Measure α) (p : ℝ≥0∞) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] : Lp ℝ p ν
decls.doc: The constant `𝟏` of `L^p(ν)`.

decls.name: coeFn_constOne
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_constOne : ⇑(constOne ν p) =ᵐ[ν] fun _ => (1 : ℝ)

decls.name: coeFn_truncation
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_truncation (P Pi : Lp ℝ p ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ p ν) (θ : Lp ℝ p ν) (η : ℝ) : ⇑(truncation P Pi (constOne ν p) θ η) =ᵐ[ν] fun x => max (Mixing.S P Pi θ x - η) 0
decls.doc: The pointwise form of the truncation `ψ_η = (η • 𝟏 - Sθ)⁻`: its a.e.

decls.name: tendsto_truncation_norm
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_truncation_norm (hp : p ≠ ⊤) (P Pi : Lp ℝ p ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ p ν) (θ : Lp ℝ p ν) : Tendsto (fun η : ℝ => ‖truncation P Pi (constOne ν p) θ η‖) atTop (𝓝 0)
decls.doc: **Step 3 of `theo:universality_L2_full`, `p < +∞`**: the truncation vanishes in `L^p(ν)`.

decls.name: weaklyUniversalAt_Lp
decls.statement: theorem weaklyUniversalAt_Lp {P Pi : Lp ℝ p ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ p ν} {θ : Lp ℝ p ν} (h : Mixing P Pi) (hone : P (constOne ν p) = constOne ν p) (hθ : Pi θ = 0) (hp : p ≠ ⊤) : WeaklyUniversalAt P θ
decls.doc: **`theo:universality_L2_full`, its conclusion at `p < +∞`**: the family `Θ = {P} × L^p_+(ν)` is weakly `L^p`-universal.

decls.name: weaklyUniversal_Lp
decls.statement: theorem weaklyUniversal_Lp {P Pi : Lp ℝ p ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ p ν} (h : Mixing P Pi) (hone : P (constOne ν p) = constOne ν p) (hp : p ≠ ⊤) : WeaklyUniversal P Pi
decls.doc: **`theo:universality_L2_full`, weak half, with `def:universality`'s quantifier closed**: for `p ≠ ∞`, under summable mixing and with `P` fixing the constants, the family `Θ = {P} × L^p_+(ν)` is weakly `L^p`-universal — every pair of equal total mass is reachable, each by its own outflow.

files.title: The density action `P`, and `P⋆ = P*`

decls.name: abs_rpow_add3_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_rpow_add3_le {w₁ w₂ w₃ u₁ u₂ u₃ p : ℝ} (h1 : 0 ≤ w₁) (h2 : 0 ≤ w₂) (h3 : 0 ≤ w₃) (hw : w₁ + w₂ + w₃ = 1) (hp : 1 ≤ p) : |w₁ * u₁ + w₂ * u₂ + w₃ * u₃| ^ p ≤ w₁ * |u₁| ^ p + w₂ * |u₂| ^ p + w₃ * |u₃| ^ p
decls.doc: Jensen's inequality for a three-atom probability and the convex `t ↦ |t|^p`, `p ≥ 1`.

decls.name: mact_vanish_offChain
decls.statement: theorem mact_vanish_offChain (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {nu : St → ℝ} (hnu : ∀ x, ¬ OnChain cap x → nu x = 0) {y : St} (hy : ¬ OnChain cap y) : mact S cap nu y = 0
decls.doc: Off the chain the transported measure vanishes: no edge of the chain leaves it.

decls.name: dens
decls.statement: noncomputable def dens (u : St → ℝ) (y : St) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The density action** `Pu := d((uλ)T)/dλ`, in closed form: the transported measure `(uλ)T` of `Balance.mact`, divided by `λ`.

decls.name: w1
decls.statement: noncomputable def w1 (k : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The reversed one-step law: the decrement weight, read backwards.

decls.name: w2
decls.statement: noncomputable def w2 (k : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The reversed one-step law: the doubling weight, read backwards.

decls.name: w3
decls.statement: noncomputable def w3 (k : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The reversed one-step law: the target-row weight, read backwards.

decls.name: w1_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem w1_nonneg (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ L.w1 k

decls.name: w2_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem w2_nonneg (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ L.w2 k

decls.name: w3_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem w3_nonneg (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ L.w3 k

decls.name: w_sum
decls.statement: theorem w_sum {k : ℕ} (hk : OnChain cap (.lad k)) : L.w1 k + L.w2 k + L.w3 k = 1
decls.doc: **The reversed law is a probability at every state of the chain.** This is the balance equation `λT = λ` divided by `λ_k`, and it is the only place invariance enters.

decls.name: dens_sink
decls.statement: theorem dens_sink (u : St → ℝ) : L.dens u .sink = u (.lad 0)
decls.doc: `P` at the sink: the wrap is the only incoming edge, so `(Pu)(s_f) = u(s₀)`.

decls.name: dens_lad
decls.statement: theorem dens_lad (u : St → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : L.dens u (.lad k) = L.w1 k * u (.lad (k + 1)) + L.w2 k * u (.lad (k / 2)) + L.w3 k * u .sink
decls.doc: `P` at a ladder state, as a three-atom average.

decls.name: lam_mul_dens
decls.statement: theorem lam_mul_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (u : St → ℝ) (y : St) : L.lam y * L.dens u y = mact S cap (fun x => L.lam x * u x) y
decls.doc: **`λ·Pu = (uλ)T`.** On the chain this is the definition with the division cleared; off it both sides vanish, `λ` by `Stat.vanish` and the transported measure by `mact_vanish_offChain`.

decls.name: dens_const
decls.statement: theorem dens_const (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {y : St} (hy : OnChain cap y) : L.dens (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) y = 1
decls.doc: **`P` fixes the constants** on the chain: the reversed law is a probability.

decls.name: summable_abs_lad_mul
decls.statement: theorem summable_abs_lad_mul {g : St → ℝ} (hg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) (hs : Summable fun x => L.lam x * g x) : Summable fun k : ℕ => |L.lam (.lad k) * g (.lad k)|
decls.doc: `λ·g` is absolutely ladder-summable whenever `g` has finite `λ`-integral.

decls.name: tsum_lam_dens
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {g : St → ℝ} (hg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) (hs : Summable fun x => L.lam x * g x) : ∑' y, L.lam y * L.dens g y = ∑' x, L.lam x * g x
decls.doc: **`∫ Pg dλ = ∫ g dλ`** at every non-negative `g` with finite `λ`-integral: the transported measure has the same total mass.

decls.name: summable_lam_dens
decls.statement: theorem summable_lam_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {g : St → ℝ} (hg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) (hs : Summable fun x => L.lam x * g x) : Summable fun y => L.lam y * L.dens g y

decls.name: abs_rpow_dens_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_rpow_dens_le {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (u : St → ℝ) {y : St} (hy : OnChain cap y) : |L.dens u y| ^ p ≤ L.dens (fun z => |u z| ^ p) y
decls.doc: **Jensen for `P`**, at every state of the chain: `|Pu|^p ≤ P(|u|^p)` for `p ≥ 1`.

decls.name: mass_dens_le
decls.statement: theorem mass_dens_le (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) {u : St → ℝ} (hs : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ p * L.lam x) : L.mass p (L.dens u) ≤ L.mass p u
decls.doc: **`P` is a contraction of `L^p(λ)`**, `p ∈ [1,∞)` — the mirror of `Stat.mass_pstar_le`, and what makes `P` an operator of `L²(λ)`.

decls.name: tsum_dens_mul
decls.statement: theorem tsum_dens_mul (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {u : St → ℝ} (hu : Summable fun k : ℕ => |L.lam (.lad k) * u (.lad k)|) {v : St → ℝ} (hv : ∃ C, ∀ x, |v x| ≤ C) : ∑' y, L.lam y * L.dens u y * v y = ∑' x, L.lam x * u x * pstar S cap v x
decls.doc: **`⟨Pu,v⟩_λ = ⟨u,P⋆v⟩_λ` at bounded `v`.** This is `lem:doubling_operator`(1)'s adjoint clause on the plain-real layer, and it is also the characterisation of `Pu` as a Radon–Nikodym derivative: taking `v = 1_{\{y\}}` reads off `λ(y)(Pu)(y) = ((uλ)T)(\{y\})`.

decls.name: abs_rpow_two'
decls.statement: theorem abs_rpow_two' (t : ℝ) : |t| ^ (2 : ℝ) = t ^ 2
decls.doc: `|t|^{(2:ℝ)} = t^2`: the bridge between the `rpow` form of `Stat.mass` and the natural power the summability estimates are written in.

decls.name: abs_pstar_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_pstar_le (f : St → ℝ) (x : St) : |pstar S cap f x| ≤ pstar S cap (fun y => |f y|) x
decls.doc: `|P⋆f| ≤ P⋆|f|`: Jensen at `p = 1`.

decls.name: summable_mass_pstar
decls.statement: theorem summable_mass_pstar {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) {f : St → ℝ} (hs : Summable fun x => |f x| ^ p * L.lam x) : Summable fun x => |pstar S cap f x| ^ p * L.lam x
decls.doc: `P⋆` preserves the `L^p` summability of the mass — the summability half of `Stat.mass_pstar_le`.

decls.name: summable_mass_dens
decls.statement: theorem summable_mass_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) {u : St → ℝ} (hs : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ p * L.lam x) : Summable fun x => |L.dens u x| ^ p * L.lam x
decls.doc: `P` preserves the `L^p` summability of the mass — the summability half of `Stat.mass_dens_le`.

decls.name: summable_lam_mul_mul
decls.statement: theorem summable_lam_mul_mul {a b : St → ℝ} (ha : Summable fun x => |a x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) (hb : Summable fun x => |b x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) : Summable fun x => L.lam x * |a x| * |b x|
decls.doc: The Cauchy–Schwarz-free product bound: `2|a||b| ≤ a² + b²`, summed against `λ`.

decls.name: summable_abs_lad_of_sq
decls.statement: theorem summable_abs_lad_of_sq {u : St → ℝ} (hu : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) : Summable fun k : ℕ => |L.lam (.lad k) * u (.lad k)|
decls.doc: `λ·u` is absolutely ladder-summable whenever `u ∈ L²(λ)`.

decls.name: tsum_dens_mul_sq
decls.statement: theorem tsum_dens_mul_sq (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {u v : St → ℝ} (hu : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) (hv : Summable fun x => |v x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) : ∑' y, L.lam y * L.dens u y * v y = ∑' x, L.lam x * u x * pstar S cap v x
decls.doc: **`⟨Pu,v⟩_λ = ⟨u,P⋆v⟩_λ` at `u, v ∈ L²(λ)`** — `lem:doubling_operator`(1)'s adjoint clause, at the paper's own hypothesis.

decls.name: tsum_lam_pstar_sq
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_pstar_sq (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {v : St → ℝ} (hv : Summable fun x => |v x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) : ∑' x, L.lam x * pstar S cap v x = ∑' x, L.lam x * v x
decls.doc: **Invariance against a square-integrable test function.** `Stat.inv` is stated against bounded `f`; `u ≡ 1` in the adjoint identity, where `P1 = 1`, removes that restriction at `L²(λ)`.

decls.name: memLp_dens
decls.statement: theorem memLp_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {p : ℝ≥0∞} (hp1 : 1 ≤ p) (hpt : p ≠ ∞) {u : St → ℝ} (hu : MemLp u p L.mu) : MemLp (L.dens u) p L.mu
decls.doc: `P` maps `L^p(μ)` into itself, at every finite `p ≥ 1`.

decls.name: eLpNorm_dens_le
decls.statement: theorem eLpNorm_dens_le (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {p : ℝ≥0∞} (hp1 : 1 ≤ p) (hpt : p ≠ ∞) {u : St → ℝ} (hu : MemLp u p L.mu) : eLpNorm (L.dens u) p L.mu ≤ eLpNorm u p L.mu
decls.doc: **`P` is a contraction of `L^p(μ)`**, `p ∈ [1,∞)` — the `eLpNorm` form of `Stat.mass_dens_le`.

files.title: `P⋆ = P*` on `L²(λ)`, and `‖P⋆ⁿ − Π‖ = β̂ₙ`

decls.name: inner_eq_tsum
decls.statement: theorem inner_eq_tsum (F G : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⟪F, G⟫_ℝ = ∑' x, L.lam x * F x * G x
decls.doc: **The Bochner half of the `LpLayer` dictionary.** `⟪F,G⟫_{L²(μ)} = ∑' x, λ(x)F(x)G(x)`.

decls.name: inner_eq_tsum_of_ae
decls.statement: theorem inner_eq_tsum_of_ae {F G : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} {f g : St → ℝ} (hF : ⇑F =ᵐ[L.mu] f) (hG : ⇑G =ᵐ[L.mu] g) : ⟪F, G⟫_ℝ = ∑' x, L.lam x * f x * g x
decls.doc: The same, read against any representatives: off the chain `λ` vanishes, so a.e.

decls.name: dens_add
decls.statement: theorem dens_add (u v : St → ℝ) : L.dens (u + v) = L.dens u + L.dens v

decls.name: dens_smul
decls.statement: theorem dens_smul (c : ℝ) (u : St → ℝ) : L.dens (c • u) = c • L.dens u

decls.name: dens_congr_onChain
decls.statement: theorem dens_congr_onChain {u v : St → ℝ} (h : ∀ x, OnChain cap x → u x = v x) (y : St) : L.dens u y = L.dens v y
decls.doc: **`P` descends to `λ`-classes**, and unlike `P⋆` it needs no hypothesis to do so: each of its three weights carries the factor `λ` of the state it reads (`Stat.w1`, `Stat.w2`, `Stat.w3`), so a state off the chain is read with weight zero.

decls.name: densLp
decls.statement: noncomputable def densLp (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu
decls.doc: `P` acting on `L²(μ)`, as a map of the space into itself.

decls.name: coeFn_densLp
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_densLp (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⇑(L.densLp hrow F) =ᵐ[L.mu] L.dens ⇑F

decls.name: norm_densLp_le
decls.statement: theorem norm_densLp_le (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ‖L.densLp hrow F‖ ≤ ‖F‖

decls.name: densLp_add
decls.statement: theorem densLp_add (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F G : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.densLp hrow (F + G) = L.densLp hrow F + L.densLp hrow G

decls.name: densLp_smul
decls.statement: theorem densLp_smul (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (c : ℝ) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.densLp hrow (c • F) = c • L.densLp hrow F

decls.name: densL2
decls.statement: noncomputable def densL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu
decls.doc: **`P` as a bounded linear operator on `L²(μ)`**, of norm at most `1` — the mirror of `Stat.pstarL2`, and the operator the paper's `β̂ₙ` is measured on.

decls.name: densL2_apply
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem densL2_apply (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.densL2 hrow F = L.densLp hrow F

decls.name: coeFn_densL2
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_densL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⇑(L.densL2 hrow F) =ᵐ[L.mu] L.dens ⇑F

decls.name: norm_densL2_le
decls.statement: theorem norm_densL2_le (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : ‖L.densL2 hrow‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: inner_densL2_left
decls.statement: theorem inner_densL2_left (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (U V : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⟪L.densL2 hrow U, V⟫_ℝ = ⟪U, L.pstarL2 hrow V⟫_ℝ
decls.doc: **`⟪PU, V⟫ = ⟪U, P⋆V⟫` on `L²(μ)`** — `Stat.tsum_dens_mul_sq` read through the inner product.

decls.name: adjoint_pstarL2
decls.statement: theorem adjoint_pstarL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (L.pstarL2 hrow) = L.densL2 hrow
decls.doc: **The adjoint clause of `lem:doubling_operator`(1).** The density action is the `L²(λ)`-adjoint of the function action.

decls.name: adjoint_densL2
decls.statement: theorem adjoint_densL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (L.densL2 hrow) = L.pstarL2 hrow
decls.doc: The same identity read the other way: `P* = P⋆`.

decls.name: piL2
decls.statement: noncomputable def piL2 : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu
decls.doc: **`Π`, the `λ`-mean projection** of `L²(μ)`: `ΠF = (∫F dλ)·1`.

decls.name: piL2_apply
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem piL2_apply (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.piL2 F = ⟪L.oneLp, F⟫_ℝ • L.oneLp

decls.name: inner_oneLp_self
decls.statement: theorem inner_oneLp_self : ⟪L.oneLp, L.oneLp⟫_ℝ = 1
decls.doc: `⟪1,1⟫ = 1`: `λ` is a probability.

decls.name: piL2_mul_piL2
decls.statement: theorem piL2_mul_piL2 : L.piL2 * L.piL2 = L.piL2
decls.doc: **`Π` is idempotent.**

decls.name: adjoint_piL2
decls.statement: theorem adjoint_piL2 : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint L.piL2 = L.piL2
decls.doc: **`Π` is self-adjoint**, `λ` being a probability.

decls.name: piL2_mul_pstarL2
decls.statement: theorem piL2_mul_pstarL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : L.piL2 * L.pstarL2 hrow = L.piL2
decls.doc: `Π P⋆ = Π`: the function action preserves the `λ`-mean.

decls.name: pstarL2_mul_piL2
decls.statement: theorem pstarL2_mul_piL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : L.pstarL2 hrow * L.piL2 = L.piL2
decls.doc: `P⋆ Π = Π`: the function action fixes the constants.

decls.name: piL2_mul_densL2
decls.statement: theorem piL2_mul_densL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : L.piL2 * L.densL2 hrow = L.piL2
decls.doc: `Π P = Π`, read off the adjoint of `P Π = Π`.

decls.name: densL2_mul_piL2
decls.statement: theorem densL2_mul_piL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : L.densL2 hrow * L.piL2 = L.piL2
decls.doc: `P Π = Π`, read off the adjoint of `Π P⋆ = Π`.

decls.name: betaHat
decls.statement: noncomputable def betaHat (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`β̂ₙ := ‖Pⁿ − Π‖_{L²(λ)}`** — the mixing coefficient of `def:doubling_setting`, defined on the density action as the paper defines it.

decls.name: adjoint_densL2_pow_sub_piL2
decls.statement: theorem adjoint_densL2_pow_sub_piL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (n : ℕ) : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ((L.densL2 hrow) ^ n - L.piL2) = (L.pstarL2 hrow) ^ n - L.piL2
decls.doc: `P⋆ⁿ − Π` is the adjoint of `Pⁿ − Π`.

decls.name: norm_pstarL2_pow_sub_piL2
decls.statement: theorem norm_pstarL2_pow_sub_piL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (n : ℕ) : ‖(L.pstarL2 hrow) ^ n - L.piL2‖ = L.betaHat hrow n
decls.doc: **`‖P⋆ⁿ − Π‖_{L²(λ)} = β̂ₙ` for every `n ≥ 0`** — the trailing clause of `lem:doubling_operator`(1).

files.title: The measure action, its duality with `P⋆`, and the pointwise balance equations

decls.name: dblW
decls.statement: noncomputable def dblW (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The doubling weight out of the ladder state `j ≥ 1`: `ε(j)` when the edge `j → 2j` survives the truncation, `0` when it has been deleted.

decls.name: decW
decls.statement: noncomputable def decW (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The decrement weight out of the ladder state `j ≥ 1`: `1 − ε(j)` when the doubling edge survives, `1` when it has been deleted and the decrement carries the whole mass.

decls.name: dblW_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem dblW_nonneg {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 ≤ dblW S cap j

decls.name: decW_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem decW_nonneg {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 ≤ decW S cap j

decls.name: dblW_add_decW
decls.statement: theorem dblW_add_decW {j : ℕ} : dblW S cap j + decW S cap j = 1
decls.doc: The one-step law out of a ladder state is a probability.

decls.name: dblW_le_one
decls.statement: theorem dblW_le_one {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : dblW S cap j ≤ 1

decls.name: decW_le_one
decls.statement: theorem decW_le_one {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : decW S cap j ≤ 1

decls.name: pstar_lad_succ_weights
decls.statement: theorem pstar_lad_succ_weights {f : St → ℝ} (j : ℕ) : pstar S cap f (.lad (j + 1)) = dblW S cap (j + 1) * f (.lad (2 * (j + 1))) + decW S cap (j + 1) * f (.lad j)
decls.doc: `P⋆` at a ladder state, with the two weights named: this is `pstar_lad_succ` with the `if` pushed into `dblW` and `decW`.

decls.name: row_zero
decls.statement: theorem row_zero (S : Setting) : S.row 0 = 0
decls.doc: The target row vanishes at `0`: `row_supp` forces `1 ≤ j` at every non-zero entry.

decls.name: mact
decls.statement: noncomputable def mact (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (nu : St → ℝ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: **The transported measure `νT`**, in closed form: one summand per kind of incoming edge.

decls.name: mact_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem mact_sink (nu : St → ℝ) : mact S cap nu .sink = nu (.lad 0)

decls.name: mact_lad
decls.statement: theorem mact_lad (nu : St → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : mact S cap nu (.lad k) = nu (.lad (k + 1)) * decW S cap (k + 1) + (if 1 ≤ k ∧ 2 ∣ k then nu (.lad (k / 2)) * dblW S cap (k / 2) else 0) + nu .sink * S.row k

decls.name: hasSum_mact
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_mact (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {nu : St → ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun k : ℕ => |nu (.lad k)|) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : ∃ V : ℝ, HasSum (fun x => nu x * pstar S cap f x) V ∧ HasSum (fun y => mact S cap nu y * f y) V
decls.doc: **The duality identity, in `HasSum` form.** Both series converge, to the same value.

decls.name: tsum_mact
decls.statement: theorem tsum_mact (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {nu : St → ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun k : ℕ => |nu (.lad k)|) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : ∑' x, nu x * pstar S cap f x = ∑' y, mact S cap nu y * f y
decls.doc: **The duality identity.** `∫ v d(νT) = ∫ P⋆v dν`.

decls.name: summable_mact
decls.statement: theorem summable_mact (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {nu : St → ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun k : ℕ => |nu (.lad k)|) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : Summable fun y => mact S cap nu y * f y

decls.name: tsum_mact_eq
decls.statement: theorem tsum_mact_eq (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {nu : St → ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun k : ℕ => |nu (.lad k)|) : ∑' y, mact S cap nu y = ∑' x, nu x
decls.doc: The transported measure has the same total mass: `f = 1` in the duality, `P⋆1 = 1`.

decls.name: summable_abs_lad
decls.statement: theorem summable_abs_lad : Summable fun k : ℕ => |L.lam (.lad k)|
decls.doc: `λ` restricted to the ladder is absolutely summable — the hypothesis every use of the duality takes.

decls.name: mact_lam
decls.statement: theorem mact_lam (y : St) : mact S cap L.lam y = L.lam y
decls.doc: **`λT = λ`, pointwise.** The paper's invariance hypothesis is carried in `Stat` in the integral form against bounded test functions; testing it against the indicator of a single state and reading the duality identity on the other side gives the balance equation at that state.

decls.name: lam_sink
decls.statement: theorem lam_sink : L.lam .sink = L.lam (.lad 0)
decls.doc: The balance equation at the sink: `λ(s_f) = λ(s₀)`, the wrap being the only incoming edge.

decls.name: lam_lad
decls.statement: theorem lam_lad (k : ℕ) : L.lam (.lad k) = L.lam (.lad (k + 1)) * decW S cap (k + 1) + (if 1 ≤ k ∧ 2 ∣ k then L.lam (.lad (k / 2)) * dblW S cap (k / 2) else 0) + L.lam .sink * S.row k
decls.doc: The balance equation at a ladder state, written out.

files.title: The solutions of the cut balance form a `d`-dimensional space

decls.name: extend
decls.statement: noncomputable def extend (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) (b : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The solution of `eq:doubling_avg` with boundary data `b` on `{0,…,d}`.

decls.name: extend_of_le
decls.statement: theorem extend_of_le (b : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ} (h : m ≤ d) : D.extend d b m = b m

decls.name: extend_of_gt
decls.statement: theorem extend_of_gt (b : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ} (h : d < m) : D.extend d b m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.qm m j * D.extend d b j

decls.name: extend_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem extend_cutBal (b : ℕ → ℝ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) : D.CutBal d (D.extend d b) ⊤
decls.doc: `extend` solves the cut balance.

decls.name: extend_unique
decls.statement: theorem extend_unique {lam b : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hb : ∀ j ≤ d, lam j = b j) : ∀ m, lam m = D.extend d b m
decls.doc: Nothing else with the same boundary data solves it: the coordinate map is injective.

decls.name: extend_pos
decls.statement: theorem extend_pos (b : ℕ → ℝ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hb : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → 0 < b j) : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → 0 < D.extend d b m
decls.doc: Positivity of the sequence is positivity of the boundary data.

decls.name: extend_add
decls.statement: theorem extend_add (b₁ b₂ : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : D.extend d (fun j => b₁ j + b₂ j) m = D.extend d b₁ m + D.extend d b₂ m
decls.doc: The extension is additive in the boundary data.

decls.name: extend_smul
decls.statement: theorem extend_smul (t : ℝ) (b : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : D.extend d (fun j => t * b j) m = t * D.extend d b m
decls.doc: The extension is homogeneous in the boundary data.

decls.name: extend_congr_high
decls.statement: theorem extend_congr_high (b₁ b₂ : ℕ → ℝ) (hb : ∀ j, d < 2 * j → j ≤ d → b₁ j = b₂ j) : ∀ m : ℕ, d < m → D.extend d b₁ m = D.extend d b₂ m
decls.doc: **The mechanism behind `ν_j = 0` for `2j ≤ d`.** Above the cut `d`, the solution does not see the boundary data at an index `j` with `2j ≤ d`: every window of an `m > d` starts at `⌈m/2⌉ ≥ (d+1)/2 > d/2`.

files.title: The constant of the sharp asymptotic is a non-negative linear functional of the boundary data

decls.name: ind
decls.statement: def ind (j : ℕ) : ℕ → ℝ
decls.doc: The indicator `e_j` of the index `j`, as boundary data.

decls.name: ind_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem ind_nonneg (j i : ℕ) : 0 ≤ ind j i

decls.name: climit
decls.statement: noncomputable def climit (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) (b : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `C(b) := lim_m (extend d b)_m m^{p_*}`, the constant `theo:doubling_sharp` attaches to the solution of the cut balance with boundary data `b`.

decls.name: nu
decls.statement: noncomputable def nu (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The coefficients of `eq:doubling_constant`:** `ν_j := C(1 + e_j) − C(1)`, a difference of two limits that `theo:doubling_sharp` provides, both data being positive.

decls.name: extend_zero
decls.statement: theorem extend_zero (m : ℕ) : D.extend d (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)) m = 0

decls.name: extend_sum
decls.statement: theorem extend_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : D.extend d (fun i => ∑ j ∈ s, f j i) m = ∑ j ∈ s, D.extend d (f j) m
decls.doc: Linearity of `extend` in the data, over a finite sum.

decls.name: extend_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem extend_nonneg (b : ℕ → ℝ) (hb : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → 0 ≤ b j) : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → 0 ≤ D.extend d b m
decls.doc: Non-negative data give a non-negative solution at every `m ≥ 1` — the induction of `extend_pos` with `≤` in place of `<`.

decls.name: extend_eq_sum_ind
decls.statement: theorem extend_eq_sum_ind (hd : 1 ≤ d) (b : ℕ → ℝ) : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → D.extend d b m = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, b j * D.extend d (ind j) m
decls.doc: Above index `0`, the solution is the sum of its data on `1..d` against the solutions with indicator data: `(extend d b)_m = Σ_{j=1}^{d} b_j (extend d e_j)_m` for `m ≥ 1`.

decls.name: tendsto_climit_of_pos
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_climit_of_pos (hd : 1 ≤ d) (b : ℕ → ℝ) (hb : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → 0 < b j) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => D.extend d b m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 (D.climit d b)) ∧ 0 < D.climit d b
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_sharp` at the solution with positive data `b`:** the rescaled profile converges to `C(b)`, and `C(b) > 0`.

decls.name: tendsto_ind
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_ind (hd : 1 ≤ d) (j : ℕ) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => D.extend d (ind j) m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 (D.nu d j))
decls.doc: The rescaled profile of the solution with indicator data `e_j` converges to `ν_j`.

decls.name: tendsto_extend
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_extend (hd : 1 ≤ d) (b : ℕ → ℝ) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => D.extend d b m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j * b j))
decls.doc: **Step 2, `eq:doubling_constant` on the whole space of data:** for every boundary data `b`, `(extend d b)_m m^{p_*} → Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j b_j`.

decls.name: climit_eq_sum
decls.statement: theorem climit_eq_sum (hd : 1 ≤ d) (b : ℕ → ℝ) : D.climit d b = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j * b j
decls.doc: `C(b) = Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j b_j` for every data `b`: the `limUnder` is the linear functional.

decls.name: tendsto_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_of_cutBal (hd : 1 ≤ d) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j * lam j))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_constant`, for the sequence itself.** Every real solution of the cut balance at every `m > d` has `λ_m m^{p_*} → Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j λ_j`.

decls.name: constant_eq
decls.statement: theorem constant_eq (hd : 1 ≤ d) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) {C : ℝ} (hC : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C)) : C = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j * lam j
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_constant`, in the paper's words:** the constant `C` of `theo:doubling_sharp` at a positive solution is `Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j λ_j`.

decls.name: nu_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem nu_nonneg (hd : 1 ≤ d) (j : ℕ) : 0 ≤ D.nu d j
decls.doc: **Step 3, first clause: `ν_j ≥ 0`.** The solution with indicator data is non-negative, so its profile is, and so is the limit.

decls.name: sum_nu_pos
decls.statement: theorem sum_nu_pos (hd : 1 ≤ d) : 0 < ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j
decls.doc: **Step 3, second clause: `Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j > 0`.** At the data `λ_1 = … = λ_d = 1` the sum is `C(1)`, which `theo:doubling_sharp` puts above the `c₁ > 0` of `theo:doubling_decay`.

decls.name: nu_eq_zero
decls.statement: theorem nu_eq_zero (hd : 1 ≤ d) {j : ℕ} (h2j : 2 * j ≤ d) : D.nu d j = 0
decls.doc: **Step 3, third clause: `ν_j = 0` whenever `2j ≤ d`.** Above the cut the solutions with data `1 + e_j` and `1` coincide (`extend_congr_high`), so the profile of `e_j`'s solution is eventually `0`.

decls.name: constant_functional
decls.statement: theorem constant_functional (hd : 1 ≤ d) : ∃ ν : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ j, 0 ≤ ν j) ∧ 0 < ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, ν j ∧ (∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 2 * j ≤ d → ν j = 0) ∧ ∀ lam : ℕ → ℝ, D.CutBal d lam ⊤ → (∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) → Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, ν j * lam j))
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_constant`, Steps 2 and 3, packaged in the paper's shape.** There are `ν_1,…,ν_d ≥ 0` with `Σ ν_j > 0` and `ν_j = 0` for `2j ≤ d` such that every positive solution of the cut balance at every `m > d` has `λ_m m^{p_*} → Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j λ_j`, i.e.

files.title: `lem:doubling_coupling`: two descents from one block reach the base block with nearly the same law

decls.name: block_eq
decls.statement: theorem block_eq (i ℓ : ℕ) : block i ℓ = Finset.Ico (2 ^ i * ℓ) (2 * (2 ^ i * ℓ))
decls.doc: `I_i(ℓ) = [a, 2a)` with `a = 2^i ℓ`.

decls.name: le_pow_mul
decls.statement: theorem le_pow_mul (i ℓ : ℕ) : ℓ ≤ 2 ^ i * ℓ

decls.name: coupling
decls.statement: theorem coupling {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 20 ≤ ℓ) (hℓτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (ℓ : ℝ)) : ∀ i : ℕ, ∀ y ∈ block i ℓ, ∀ y' ∈ block i ℓ, tvOn (Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ)) (D.exitLaw ℓ y) (D.exitLaw ℓ y') ≤ (1 - D.omeg) ^ i
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_coupling`.** Two descents started in `I_i(ℓ)` reach the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)` with laws at total variation at most `(1−ω)^i`.

decls.name: coupling_above
decls.statement: theorem coupling_above {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 20 ≤ ℓ) (hℓτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (ℓ : ℝ)) (i : ℕ) {m m' : ℕ} (hm : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m) (hm' : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m') : tvOn (Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ)) (D.exitLaw ℓ m) (D.exitLaw ℓ m') ≤ (1 - D.omeg) ^ i
decls.doc: **The coupling bound above a block.** Two descents started anywhere above `2^i ℓ` — not necessarily in the same block — reach the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)` with laws at total variation at most `(1−ω)^i`.

files.title: The Cramér root

decls.name: psi
decls.statement: noncomputable def psi (c t : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `ψ(t) = c(2^t − 1) − t`, whose non-zero root is the Cramér exponent `p_*`.

decls.name: psi_zero
decls.statement: theorem psi_zero (c : ℝ) : psi c 0 = 0

decls.name: two_rpow_eq
decls.statement: theorem two_rpow_eq (t : ℝ) : (2 : ℝ) ^ t = exp (t * log 2)
decls.doc: `2^t = exp (t · ln 2)`.

decls.name: two_rpow_pos
decls.statement: theorem two_rpow_pos (t : ℝ) : (0 : ℝ) < (2 : ℝ) ^ t

decls.name: log_two_pos
decls.statement: theorem log_two_pos : (0 : ℝ) < log 2

decls.name: two_log_two_gt_one
decls.statement: theorem two_log_two_gt_one : (1 : ℝ) < 2 * log 2
decls.doc: `2 ln 2 > 1`, the one numeric fact behind `two_rpow_gt_add_one`.

decls.name: two_rpow_gt_add_one
decls.statement: theorem two_rpow_gt_add_one {t : ℝ} (ht : 1 < t) : t + 1 < (2 : ℝ) ^ t
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cramer_ineq`, the engine.** `2^t > t + 1` for every `t > 1`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_two_rpow
decls.statement: theorem hasDerivAt_two_rpow (t : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => (2 : ℝ) ^ x) ((2 : ℝ) ^ t * log 2) t

decls.name: hasDerivAt_psi
decls.statement: theorem hasDerivAt_psi (c t : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (psi c) (c * ((2 : ℝ) ^ t * log 2) - 1) t

decls.name: deriv_psi
decls.statement: theorem deriv_psi (c : ℝ) : deriv (psi c) = fun t => c * ((2 : ℝ) ^ t * log 2) - 1

decls.name: continuous_two_rpow
decls.statement: theorem continuous_two_rpow : Continuous fun t : ℝ => (2 : ℝ) ^ t

decls.name: continuous_psi
decls.statement: theorem continuous_psi (c : ℝ) : Continuous (psi c)

decls.name: psi_strictConvexOn
decls.statement: theorem psi_strictConvexOn {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) : StrictConvexOn ℝ univ (psi c)
decls.doc: `ψ` is strictly convex on `ℝ`, for every `c > 0`.

decls.name: psi_neg_of_mem_openSegment
decls.statement: theorem psi_neg_of_mem_openSegment {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {a b t : ℝ} (ha : psi c a = 0) (hb : psi c b = 0) (hab : a ≠ b) (ht : t ∈ openSegment ℝ a b) : psi c t < 0

decls.name: psi_neg_of_between
decls.statement: theorem psi_neg_of_between {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {a b t : ℝ} (ha : psi c a = 0) (hb : psi c b = 0) (hab : a < b) (h1 : a < t) (h2 : t < b) : psi c t < 0

decls.name: psi_pos_of_outside
decls.statement: theorem psi_pos_of_outside {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {a b t : ℝ} (ha : psi c a = 0) (hb : psi c b = 0) (hab : a < b) (ht : t < a ∨ b < t) : 0 < psi c t
decls.doc: Outside the closed interval spanned by two roots, `ψ` is strictly positive.

decls.name: psi_no_three_roots
decls.statement: theorem psi_no_three_roots {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {a b e : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hbe : b < e) (ha : psi c a = 0) (hb : psi c b = 0) (he : psi c e = 0) : False
decls.doc: `ψ` has no three distinct roots.

decls.name: cramer_root_unique
decls.statement: theorem cramer_root_unique {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {p q : ℝ} (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hq0 : q ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) (hq : psi c q = 0) : p = q
decls.doc: **Uniqueness.** `ψ` has at most one root other than `0`.

decls.name: psi_pos_of_log_eq
decls.statement: theorem psi_pos_of_log_eq {c : ℝ} (hc : c * log 2 = 1) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) : 0 < psi c t
decls.doc: At `c = 1/ln 2` the only root is `0`: `ψ(t) > 0` for `t ≠ 0`.

decls.name: psi_pos_atTop
decls.statement: theorem psi_pos_atTop {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) : ∃ T : ℝ, 0 < T ∧ ∀ t, T ≤ t → 0 < psi c t
decls.doc: `ψ(T) > 0` for `T` far enough to the right: the exponential beats the line.

decls.name: psi_pos_atBot
decls.statement: theorem psi_pos_atBot {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) : ∃ T : ℝ, T < 0 ∧ ∀ t, t ≤ T → 0 < psi c t
decls.doc: `ψ(T) > 0` for `T` far enough to the left, where `c(2^T − 1) > −c`.

decls.name: cramer_root_exists
decls.statement: theorem cramer_root_exists {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hne : c * log 2 ≠ 1) : ∃ p : ℝ, p ≠ 0 ∧ psi c p = 0 ∧ (0 < p ↔ c * log 2 < 1)
decls.doc: The root exists whenever `c ln 2 ≠ 1`, and its sign is that of `1 − c ln 2`.

decls.name: cramer_root_gt_one
decls.statement: theorem cramer_root_gt_one {c p : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : 1 < p
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(1), second equivalence, `⟸`.** `c < 1` forces `p_* > 1`.

decls.name: cramer_lt_one_of_root_gt_one
decls.statement: theorem cramer_lt_one_of_root_gt_one {c p : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hp : psi c p = 0) (hp1 : 1 < p) : c < 1
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(1), second equivalence, `⟹`.** `p_* > 1` forces `c < 1`.

decls.name: cramer_root_pos_iff
decls.statement: theorem cramer_root_pos_iff {c p : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hne : c * log 2 ≠ 1) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : 0 < p ↔ c * log 2 < 1
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(1), first equivalence.**

decls.name: cramer_form
decls.statement: theorem cramer_form {c p : ℝ} (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : c * (((2 : ℝ) ^ p - 1) / p) = 1
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cramer_form`.** `c(τ−1)/p_* = 1`.

decls.name: cramer_kernel_integral
decls.statement: theorem cramer_kernel_integral {c p : ℝ} (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : (∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, c * log 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (p * v)) = 1
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(2), the kernel.** `∫₀¹ c ln 2 · 2^{p v} dv = 1`.

decls.name: cramer_ineq
decls.statement: theorem cramer_ineq (hc : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : 2 < (2 : ℝ) ^ p ∧ p + 1 < (2 : ℝ) ^ p ∧ p + 2 < 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ p ∧ p + 3 < 4 * (2 : ℝ) ^ p
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cramer_ineq`.** At `0 < c < 1`, with `τ := 2^{p_*}`: `τ > 2`, `τ > p_*+1`, `2τ > p_*+2` and `4τ > p_*+3`.

files.title: Cut balance

decls.name: lam_mul_dirac_eq
decls.statement: theorem lam_mul_dirac_eq (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) : (fun x => L.lam x * dirac j x) = (fun x => if x = St.lad j then L.lam (St.lad j) else 0)
decls.doc: `λ` against a point mass is the mass of the point.

decls.name: hasSum_lam_mul_dirac
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_lam_mul_dirac (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) : HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * dirac j x) (L.lam (.lad j))

decls.name: summable_lam_mul_dirac
decls.statement: theorem summable_lam_mul_dirac (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) : Summable (fun x => L.lam x * dirac j x)

decls.name: tsum_lam_mul_dirac
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_mul_dirac (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) : ∑' x, L.lam x * dirac j x = L.lam (.lad j)

decls.name: tsum_lam_mul_cutFn
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_mul_cutFn (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) : ∑' x, L.lam x * cutFn S m x = 0
decls.doc: The `λ`-integral of the per-cut defect vanishes: this is invariance, tested against `1_A`.

decls.name: cut_balance
decls.statement: theorem cut_balance (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) : L.lam (.lad m) * (1 - S.eps m) = ∑ j ∈ window m, L.lam (.lad j) * S.eps j
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cut`.** The mass leaving the cut at `m` by decrement equals the mass entering it from the window below by doubling.

decls.name: CutBalanceSeq
decls.statement: def CutBalanceSeq (S : Setting) (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (M₁ : ℕ∞) : Prop
decls.doc: The recursion `eq:doubling_cut` as a predicate on a bare real sequence, with no invariance and no normalisation.

decls.name: cutBalanceSeq_of_stat
decls.statement: theorem cutBalanceSeq_of_stat (L : Stat S none) : CutBalanceSeq S (fun j => L.lam (.lad j)) ⊤
decls.doc: An invariant probability of the loop closure gives a sequence satisfying the recursion everywhere: the bridge from `Stat` to `CutBalanceSeq`.

files.title: Notation for the decay estimates, and the averaging form of the cut balance

decls.name: Decay
decls.statement: structure Decay
decls.doc: The decay parameters: `c` in the standing range at `s = 1`, and a non-zero root `p` of the Cramér equation `c(2^p − 1) = p`.

decls.name: p_gt_one
decls.statement: theorem p_gt_one : 1 < D.p
decls.doc: `p_* > 1` at `0 < c < 1` (`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(1)).

decls.name: p_pos
decls.statement: theorem p_pos : 0 < D.p

decls.name: tau
decls.statement: noncomputable def tau : ℝ

decls.name: tau_gt_two
decls.statement: theorem tau_gt_two : 2 < D.tau

decls.name: tau_pos
decls.statement: theorem tau_pos : 0 < D.tau

decls.name: cramer
decls.statement: theorem cramer : D.c * ((D.tau - 1) / D.p) = 1
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cramer_form`.** `c(τ−1)/p = 1`.

decls.name: eps
decls.statement: noncomputable def eps (j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `ε(j) = c/(j+1)`, the family at `s = 1`.

decls.name: eps_eq
decls.statement: theorem eps_eq (j : ℕ) : D.eps j = D.c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)

decls.name: eps_pos
decls.statement: theorem eps_pos (j : ℕ) : 0 < D.eps j

decls.name: eps_le_half
decls.statement: theorem eps_le_half {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : D.eps j ≤ D.c / 2

decls.name: one_sub_eps_pos
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_eps_pos {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 < 1 - D.eps j

decls.name: qm
decls.statement: noncomputable def qm (m j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `q_m(j) = c/((j+1)(1−ε(m)))`, the cut weights of `eq:doubling_window`.

decls.name: qm_eq
decls.statement: theorem qm_eq (m j : ℕ) : D.qm m j = D.c / (((j : ℝ) + 1) * (1 - D.eps m))

decls.name: qm_pos
decls.statement: theorem qm_pos {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (j : ℕ) : 0 < D.qm m j

decls.name: wm
decls.statement: noncomputable def wm (m j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `w_m(j) = q_m(j)(m/j)^p`, the rescaled cut weights.

decls.name: wm_pos
decls.statement: theorem wm_pos {m j : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 < D.wm m j

decls.name: wm_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem wm_nonneg {m j : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 ≤ D.wm m j

decls.name: R0
decls.statement: noncomputable def R0 (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `R_0(m) = Σ_{j ∈ W(m)} w_m(j)`, the total weight of the window — `eq:doubling_R` at `α = 0`.

decls.name: uu
decls.statement: noncomputable def uu (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The rescaled profile `u_m := λ_m m^p` of `def:doubling_decay_notation`.

decls.name: Phi
decls.statement: noncomputable def Phi (α : ℝ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ

decls.name: Ralpha
decls.statement: noncomputable def Ralpha (α : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `R_α(m)` of `eq:doubling_R`.

decls.name: delta
decls.statement: def delta (m : ℕ) : ℕ
decls.doc: The parity `δ(m) = m − 2⌊m/2⌋`.

decls.name: delta_lt_two
decls.statement: theorem delta_lt_two (m : ℕ) : delta m < 2

decls.name: block
decls.statement: def block (i ℓ : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
decls.doc: The dyadic block `I_i(ℓ) = [2^i ℓ, 2^{i+1} ℓ)`.

decls.name: mem_block
decls.statement: theorem mem_block {i ℓ n : ℕ} : n ∈ block i ℓ ↔ 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ n ∧ n < 2 ^ (i + 1) * ℓ

decls.name: CutBal
decls.statement: def CutBal (d : ℕ) (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (M₁ : ℕ∞) : Prop
decls.doc: `eq:doubling_cut` as a predicate on a bare sequence, with `ε` the family at `s = 1`.

decls.name: cutBal_of_setting
decls.statement: theorem cutBal_of_setting {S : Setting} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞} (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = D.eps j) (h : CutBalanceSeq S lam M₁) : D.CutBal S.d lam M₁
decls.doc: The bridge: a `Setting` whose `ε` is the family at `s = 1` gives `Decay.CutBal`.

decls.name: one_le_of_mem_window'
decls.statement: theorem one_le_of_mem_window' {m j : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hj : j ∈ window m) : 1 ≤ j
decls.doc: Every index of `W(m)` is a positive integer, `m` being positive.

decls.name: avg_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem avg_of_cutBal {d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞} (h : D.CutBal d lam M₁) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hdm : d < m) (hM : (m : ℕ∞) ≤ M₁) : lam m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.qm m j * lam j
