decls.statement: theorem main_constant_functional {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c 1 j) : ∃ p : ℝ, psi c p = 0 ∧ 1 < p ∧ ∃ ν : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ j, 0 ≤ ν j) ∧ 0 < ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d, ν j ∧ (∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 2 * j ≤ S.d → ν j = 0) ∧ ∀ L : Stat S none, Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => L.lam (.lad m) * (m : ℝ) ^ p) atTop (𝓝 (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d, ν j * L.lam (.lad j)))
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(2), "determined by `c`, `d` and `λ_1, …, λ_d`", in the form of `prop:doubling_constant`.** There are coefficients `ν_1, …, ν_d ≥ 0`, depending on `c` and `d` alone, with `Σ ν_j > 0` and `ν_j = 0` for `2j ≤ d`, such that for every invariant probability `λ` of the loop closure the constant of `main_invariant_measure` is `C = Σ_{j≤d} ν_j λ_j`.

decls.name: main_unbounded
decls.statement: theorem main_unbounded {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c s j) (L : Stat S none) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∃ m, S.d < m ∧ L.mass p (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S none (L.centredTail m) x) ≤ t * L.mass p (L.centredTail m)) ∧ ¬ ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ f : St → ℝ, (∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) → (∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) → L.mass p f ≤ B * L.mass p (fun x => f x - pstar S none f x)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(3), the finite exponents.** At every member of the family in the standing range, and at every positive recurrent `λ`, the flow-matching defect of the centred tail indicators drives the `L^p(λ)` Rayleigh quotient to zero, and no constant bounds a bounded mean-zero function by its defect.

decls.name: main_unbounded_infty
decls.statement: theorem main_unbounded_infty {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c s j) (L : Stat S none) : ¬ ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ (f : St → ℝ) (M Dd : ℝ), (∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) → (∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) → (∃ x, M ≤ |f x|) → (∀ x, |f x - pstar S none f x| ≤ Dd) → M ≤ B * Dd
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(3), the exponent `+∞`.** At every member of the family and every positive recurrent `λ`, no constant bounds the attained `L^∞` size of a bounded mean-zero function by the uniform size of its flow-matching defect.

decls.name: main_unbounded_two
decls.statement: theorem main_unbounded_two {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c s j) (L : Stat S none) : (¬ ∃ Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 (rowOnChain_none S)) = 1 - L.piL2) ∧ (¬ ∃ U : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, Tendsto (partialSum (L.pstarL2 (rowOnChain_none S)) L.piL2) atTop (𝓝 U)) ∧ ¬ Summable (L.betaHat (rowOnChain_none S))
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(3), the `p = 2` sentence.** On `L²(λ)`: no bounded `S` satisfies `S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π` — the convention `B̂ = +∞` of `def:doubling_setting` — the series `Σ_{n≥0}(P⋆ⁿ − Π)` does not converge in operator norm, and `Σ_{n≥0} β̂_n = +∞`.

decls.name: main_sigmaBar_eq
decls.statement: theorem main_sigmaBar_eq {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c 1 j) : ⨆ n, sbar S none n = S.jbar / (1 - c)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(3), the backward-length clause.** At `s = 1` and `0 < c < 1` the expected backward-trajectory length of the loop closure is `σ̄ = j̄/(1−c)` (`prop:doubling_length`).

decls.name: main_sigmaBar_le
decls.statement: theorem main_sigmaBar_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) {cap : Option ℕ} (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c 1 j) (n : ℕ) : sbar S cap n ≤ S.jbar / (1 - c)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(3), the backward-length clause, on every truncation as well.** The truncated expectations `σ̄⁽ⁿ⁾_K` are bounded by `j̄/(1−c)` uniformly in `n` and `K` (`lem:doubling_supersolution`).

decls.name: main_rate
decls.statement: theorem main_rate {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c 1 j) (L : Stat S none) : ∃ p : ℝ, psi c p = 0 ∧ 1 < p ∧ ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∃ m₂ : ℕ, S.d < m₂ ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m₂ ≤ m → c₁ * (m : ℝ) * L.mass 2 (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S none (L.centredTail m) x) ≤ 4 * c₂ * (p - 1) * L.mass 2 (L.centredTail m)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(3), the `c₇√m` clause, unconditional.** At `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1`, with `p_*` the Cramér root and `λ` an invariant probability, there are `0 < c₁ ≤ c₂` and `m₂ > d` with `c₁ m ‖(Id−P⋆)f_m‖² ≤ 4c₂(p_*−1) ‖f_m‖²` for every `m ≥ m₂`, i.e.

decls.name: main_unsolvable
decls.statement: theorem main_unsolvable {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c s j) (L : Stat S none) : (L.defectRange ≤ L.kerPi ∧ L.defectRange.topologicalClosure = L.kerPi ∧ L.defectRange ≠ L.kerPi) ∧ ∃ fi fe : St → ℝ, (∀ x, 0 ≤ fi x) ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ fe x) ∧ MemLp fi 2 L.mu ∧ MemLp fe 2 L.mu ∧ ∑' x, L.lam x * fi x = 1 ∧ ∑' x, L.lam x * fe x = 1 ∧ ¬ ∃ f : St → ℝ, MemLp f 2 L.mu ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂L.mu, f x - pstar S none f x = fi x - fe x
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(4).** At every member of the family in the standing range and every positive recurrent `λ`: `(Id − P⋆)L²(λ)` is a dense proper subspace of `ker Π`, and there are probability densities `f_init, f_term ∈ L²(λ)` such that no `f ∈ L²(λ)` satisfies the flow-matching equation `(Id − P⋆)f = f_init − f_term` (`prop:doubling_unsolvable`).

decls.name: main_truncation_irreducible
decls.statement: theorem main_truncation_irreducible {K : ℕ} (hK : Even K) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) (P : PreStat S (some K)) : (∀ x y : St, OnChain (some K) y → Reach S (some K) x y) ∧ (∀ ⦃y : St⦄, OnChain (some K) y → 0 < P.lam y)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(5), the irreducibility clause.** The truncation at an even cap `K ≥ d` is irreducible, and an invariant probability on it is positive at every state of it.

decls.name: main_truncation_bhat
decls.statement: theorem main_truncation_bhat {K : ℕ} (hK : Even K) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : Nonempty (Stat S (some K)) ∧ (∀ L L' : Stat S (some K), L.lam = L'.lam) ∧ ∀ L : Stat S (some K), ∃ Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, (1 - L.pstarL2 (rowOnChain_some hdK)) * Sop = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 (rowOnChain_some hdK)) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ L.piL2 * Sop = 0 ∧ Sop * L.piL2 = 0
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(5), `λ^K` and `B̂_K < +∞`.** At an even cap `K ≥ d` the truncation carries exactly one invariant probability, and on `L²(λ^K)` there is a diffusion operator `S` satisfying `eq:doubling_resolvent` — a bounded operator, so `B̂_K = ‖S‖ < +∞` (`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible`).

decls.name: main_truncation_sqrtK
decls.statement: theorem main_truncation_sqrtK {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c 1 j) : ∃ c₈ : ℝ, 0 < c₈ ∧ ∃ K₀ : ℕ, ∀ K : ℕ, K₀ ≤ K → ∀ (L : Stat S (some K)) (hrow : RowOnChain S (some K)) (Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu), Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2 → c₈ * (K : ℝ) ≤ ‖Sop‖ ^ 2
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_main`(5), the proved `√K`, squared.** At `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1`, there are `c₈ > 0` and `K₀` — depending on `c`, `d`, `j̄` and the `Setting`'s `ε_max` — such that for every `K ≥ K₀`, every invariant probability `λ^K` of the truncation and every bounded `S` on `L²(λ^K)` with `S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π`, `c₈ K ≤ ‖S‖²`; read at the `S` of `main_truncation_bhat` this is `B̂_K ≥ √c₈ · √K` (`cor:doubling_truncation`(3)).

files.title: The diffusion operator: the resolvent identities

decls.name: pi_mul_pow
decls.statement: theorem pi_mul_pow (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) : ∀ n : ℕ, Pi * P ^ n = Pi
decls.doc: `Π P⋆^n = Π` for every `n`.

decls.name: pow_mul_pi
decls.statement: theorem pow_mul_pi (hPPi : P * Pi = Pi) : ∀ n : ℕ, P ^ n * Pi = Pi
decls.doc: `P⋆^n Π = Π` for every `n`.

decls.name: partialSum
decls.statement: noncomputable def partialSum (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (N : ℕ) : E →L[ℝ] E
decls.doc: The partial sums of `Σ (P⋆^n − Π)`.

decls.name: one_sub_mul_partialSum
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_mul_partialSum (hPPi : P * Pi = Pi) (N : ℕ) : (1 - P) * partialSum P Pi N = 1 - P ^ N
decls.doc: **The telescoping identity, on the left.** `(Id − P⋆) S_N = Id − P⋆^N`.

decls.name: partialSum_mul_one_sub
decls.statement: theorem partialSum_mul_one_sub (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) (N : ℕ) : partialSum P Pi N * (1 - P) = 1 - P ^ N
decls.doc: **The telescoping identity, on the right.** `S_N (Id − P⋆) = Id − P⋆^N`.

decls.name: pi_mul_partialSum
decls.statement: theorem pi_mul_partialSum (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) (N : ℕ) : Pi * partialSum P Pi N = 0
decls.doc: `Π S_N = 0`: every term of the series is killed by `Π` on the left.

decls.name: partialSum_mul_pi
decls.statement: theorem partialSum_mul_pi (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPPi : P * Pi = Pi) (N : ℕ) : partialSum P Pi N * Pi = 0

decls.name: tendsto_pow
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_pow (hconv : Tendsto (partialSum P Pi) atTop (𝓝 U)) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => P ^ N) atTop (𝓝 Pi)
decls.doc: Convergence of the series makes `P⋆^N → Π`: the general term goes to zero.

decls.name: resolvent_identities
decls.statement: theorem resolvent_identities (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) (hPPi : P * Pi = Pi) (hconv : Tendsto (partialSum P Pi) atTop (𝓝 U)) : (1 - P) * U = 1 - Pi ∧ U * (1 - P) = 1 - Pi ∧ Pi * U = 0 ∧ U * Pi = 0
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_resolvent`, both halves.**

decls.name: resolvent_inverse
decls.statement: theorem resolvent_inverse (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) (hPPi : P * Pi = Pi) (hconv : Tendsto (partialSum P Pi) atTop (𝓝 U)) : (1 - P + Pi) * (Pi + U) = 1 ∧ (Pi + U) * (1 - P + Pi) = 1
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_operator`(3).** `Id − P⋆ + Π` is invertible with inverse `Π + U`, so the diffusion operator `S = (Id − P⋆ + Π)^{-1} − Π` is `U`.

decls.name: resolvent_norm_le
decls.statement: theorem resolvent_norm_le {B : ℝ} (hconv : Tendsto (partialSum P Pi) atTop (𝓝 U)) (hB : ∀ N : ℕ, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, ‖P ^ n - Pi‖ ≤ B) : ‖U‖ ≤ B
decls.doc: **`B̂ ≤ Σ_{n≥0} β̂_n`.** The norm of the diffusion operator is at most the mixing sum: the two constants written `B̂` in the appendix (`rem:doubling_two_constants`) are ordered, in this direction and not the other.

files.title: The diffusion operator on a finite chain: invertibility and the resolvent identities
variables: variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E}
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]

decls.name: pi_mul_resolventOp
decls.statement: theorem pi_mul_resolventOp (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) : Pi * (1 - P + Pi) = Pi
decls.doc: `Π(Id − P⋆ + Π) = Π`.

decls.name: resolventOp_mul_pi
decls.statement: theorem resolventOp_mul_pi (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPPi : P * Pi = Pi) : (1 - P + Pi) * Pi = Pi
decls.doc: `(Id − P⋆ + Π)Π = Π`.

decls.name: resolventOp_injective
decls.statement: theorem resolventOp_injective (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) (hker : ∀ f : E, P f = f → Pi f = f) : Function.Injective (1 - P + Pi : E →L[ℝ] E)
decls.doc: **`Id − P⋆ + Π` is injective.** `Πf = 0` follows by applying `Π`; then `P⋆f = f`, so `f` is a constant of zero mean, that is `0`.

decls.name: resolvent_identities_of_inverse
decls.statement: theorem resolvent_identities_of_inverse {R : E →L[ℝ] E} (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) (hPPi : P * Pi = Pi) (hMR : (1 - P + Pi) * R = 1) (hRM : R * (1 - P + Pi) = 1) : (1 - P) * (R - Pi) = 1 - Pi ∧ (R - Pi) * (1 - P) = 1 - Pi ∧ Pi * (R - Pi) = 0 ∧ (R - Pi) * Pi = 0
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_resolvent`, from a two-sided inverse.** Pure algebra: once `Id − P⋆ + Π` has an inverse `R`, the identities of the paper follow from `ΠR = RΠ = Π` and `Π(Id − P⋆) = (Id − P⋆)Π = 0`.

decls.name: exists_inverse
decls.statement: theorem exists_inverse (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) (hker : ∀ f : E, P f = f → Pi f = f) : ∃ R : E →L[ℝ] E, (1 - P + Pi) * R = 1 ∧ R * (1 - P + Pi) = 1
decls.doc: **`Id − P⋆ + Π` is invertible** on a finite-dimensional space: it is injective, hence surjective, and in finite dimensions the inverse is again bounded.

decls.name: exists_resolvent
decls.statement: theorem exists_resolvent (hPi2 : Pi * Pi = Pi) (hPiP : Pi * P = Pi) (hPPi : P * Pi = Pi) (hker : ∀ f : E, P f = f → Pi f = f) : ∃ R : E →L[ℝ] E, (1 - P + Pi) * R = 1 ∧ R * (1 - P + Pi) = 1 ∧ (1 - P) * (R - Pi) = 1 - Pi ∧ (R - Pi) * (1 - P) = 1 - Pi ∧ Pi * (R - Pi) = 0 ∧ (R - Pi) * Pi = 0
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_operator`(2), the algebra.** On a finite-dimensional space, `Id − P⋆ + Π` is invertible and the diffusion operator `S := (Id − P⋆ + Π)^{-1} − Π` satisfies `eq:doubling_resolvent`.

files.title: The diffusion operator of the truncation, and `B̂_K < +∞`

decls.name: finite_onChain
decls.statement: instance finite_onChain (K : ℕ) : Finite {x : St // OnChain (some K) x}
decls.doc: **The chain of the truncation at `K` is finite**: it is the `K + 2` states `{s₀, 1, …, K, s_f}` of `lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible`, injected here into `Option (Fin (K+1))`.

decls.name: eq_smul_oneLp_of_pstarL2_fixed
decls.statement: theorem eq_smul_oneLp_of_pstarL2_fixed (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} (hF : L.pstarL2 hrow F = F) : F = (F : St → ℝ) (.lad 0) • L.oneLp
decls.doc: A fixed point of `P⋆` in `L²(λ)` is a constant class — `lem:doubling_fixed_points`' `P⋆` half (`Stat.fixed_const_memLp`), transported to `Lp` at an arbitrary cap.

decls.name: piL2_fixed_of_pstarL2_fixed
decls.statement: theorem piL2_fixed_of_pstarL2_fixed (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} (hF : L.pstarL2 hrow F = F) : L.piL2 F = F
decls.doc: **`hker`**: `P⋆f = f` forces `Πf = f`.

decls.name: evalChain
decls.statement: noncomputable def evalChain : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →ₗ[ℝ] ({x : St // OnChain (some K) x} → ℝ)
decls.doc: **Evaluation at the states of the chain**, as a linear map into a finite product.

decls.name: evalChain_injective
decls.statement: theorem evalChain_injective : Function.Injective L.evalChain
decls.doc: Evaluation on the chain is injective: `λ` charges every state of the chain and vanishes off it, so a class vanishing there is the zero class.

decls.name: instFiniteDimensionalLp
decls.statement: instance instFiniteDimensionalLp : FiniteDimensional ℝ (Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
decls.doc: **`L²(λ^K)` is finite-dimensional** — the sentence of Step 4 that `OperatorFinite.exists_resolvent` waits on.

decls.name: exists_diffusionOp
decls.statement: theorem exists_diffusionOp (hrow : RowOnChain S (some K)) : ∃ R : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow + L.piL2) * R = 1 ∧ R * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow + L.piL2) = 1 ∧ (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) * (R - L.piL2) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ (R - L.piL2) * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ L.piL2 * (R - L.piL2) = 0 ∧ (R - L.piL2) * L.piL2 = 0
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_operator`(2), instantiated.** On the truncation `Id − P⋆ + Π` is invertible and the diffusion operator `S := (Id − P⋆ + Π)^{-1} − Π` satisfies `eq:doubling_resolvent`.

decls.name: exists_bhat
decls.statement: theorem exists_bhat (hrow : RowOnChain S (some K)) : ∃ Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) * Sop = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ L.piL2 * Sop = 0 ∧ Sop * L.piL2 = 0 ∧ ∀ F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, ‖F - L.piL2 F‖ ≤ ‖Sop‖ * ‖F - L.pstarL2 hrow F‖
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible` Step 4, and `cor:doubling_truncation` Step 1.** There is a diffusion operator `S` on `L²(λ^K)` satisfying `eq:doubling_resolvent`, and its norm `B̂_K` is a real number — which is `B̂_K < +∞`.

files.title: The exact per-cut identity

decls.name: inTail
decls.statement: def inTail : Option ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop
decls.doc: Membership of the tail set `A`: `[m, +∞)` on the loop closure, `[m, K]` on the truncation.

decls.statement: instance : ∀ (cap : Option ℕ) (m j : ℕ), Decidable (inTail cap m j) | none, m, j => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (m ≤ j)) | some K, m, j => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (m ≤ j ∧ j ≤ K)) variable {cap : Option ℕ} {m j : ℕ}

decls.name: inTail_of
decls.statement: theorem inTail_of (h : m ≤ j) (hx : OnChain cap (.lad j)) : inTail cap m j

decls.name: not_inTail_of_lt
decls.statement: theorem not_inTail_of_lt (h : j < m) : ¬ inTail cap m j

decls.name: tailInd
decls.statement: def tailInd (cap : Option ℕ) (m : ℕ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: `1_A`, the indicator of the tail set.

decls.name: tailInd_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem tailInd_sink : tailInd cap m .sink = 0

decls.name: tailInd_lad
decls.statement: theorem tailInd_lad (j : ℕ) : tailInd cap m (.lad j) = if inTail cap m j then 1 else 0

decls.name: tailInd_one
decls.statement: theorem tailInd_one (h : inTail cap m j) : tailInd cap m (.lad j) = 1

decls.name: tailInd_zero
decls.statement: theorem tailInd_zero (h : ¬ inTail cap m j) : tailInd cap m (.lad j) = 0

decls.name: tailInd_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem tailInd_nonneg (x : St) : 0 ≤ tailInd cap m x

decls.name: tailInd_le_one
decls.statement: theorem tailInd_le_one (x : St) : tailInd cap m x ≤ 1

decls.name: tailInd_bounded
decls.statement: theorem tailInd_bounded : ∃ C, ∀ x, |tailInd cap m x| ≤ C

decls.name: dirac
decls.statement: def dirac (j : ℕ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: The point mass at the ladder state `j`, as a function on `St`.

decls.name: dirac_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem dirac_sink (j : ℕ) : dirac j .sink = 0

decls.name: dirac_lad
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem dirac_lad (i j : ℕ) : dirac j (.lad i) = if i = j then 1 else 0

decls.name: cutFn
decls.statement: noncomputable def cutFn (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: The right-hand side of `eq:doubling_step1`: `(1 − ε(m)) 1_{\{m\}} − Σ_{x ∈ W(m)} ε(x) 1_{\{x\}}`.

decls.name: cutFn_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem cutFn_sink (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : cutFn S m .sink = 0

decls.name: sum_eps_dirac
decls.statement: theorem sum_eps_dirac (S : Setting) (m j : ℕ) : ∑ y ∈ window m, S.eps y * dirac y (.lad j) = if j ∈ window m then S.eps j else 0
decls.doc: The window sum collapses to a single term, by `Finset.sum_ite_eq`.

decls.name: sum_dirac_gen
decls.statement: theorem sum_dirac_gen (c : ℕ → ℝ) (m j : ℕ) : ∑ y ∈ window m, c y * dirac y (.lad j) = if j ∈ window m then c j else 0
decls.doc: The window sum collapses to a single term, for an arbitrary coefficient function.

decls.name: cutFn_lad
decls.statement: theorem cutFn_lad (S : Setting) (m j : ℕ) : cutFn S m (.lad j) = (1 - S.eps m) * (if j = m then 1 else 0) - (if j ∈ window m then S.eps j else 0)

decls.name: percut_id
decls.statement: theorem percut_id (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) {x : St} (hx : OnChain cap x) : tailInd cap m x - pstar S cap (tailInd cap m) x = cutFn S m x
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_step1`.** The flow-matching defect of the tail indicator is exactly a point mass of size `1 − ε(m)` at the cut, minus the doubling weights of the window below it.

files.title: The `L^p(λ)` mass of the per-cut defect

decls.name: Stat.mass
decls.statement: noncomputable def Stat.mass (L : Stat S cap) (p : ℝ) (f : St → ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The `p`-th power of the `L^p(λ)` norm, in plain `ℝ`.

decls.name: hasSum_dirac
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_dirac (j : ℕ) : HasSum (dirac j) 1

decls.name: not_mem_window_self
decls.statement: theorem not_mem_window_self (m : ℕ) : m ∉ window m
decls.doc: `m` is not in its own window.

decls.name: cutFn_at_cut
decls.statement: theorem cutFn_at_cut (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : cutFn S m (.lad m) = 1 - S.eps m

decls.name: cutFn_at_window
decls.statement: theorem cutFn_at_window (S : Setting) {m y : ℕ} (hy : y ∈ window m) : cutFn S m (.lad y) = -S.eps y

decls.name: cutFn_eq_zero
decls.statement: theorem cutFn_eq_zero (S : Setting) {m j : ℕ} (h1 : j ≠ m) (h2 : j ∉ window m) : cutFn S m (.lad j) = 0

decls.name: mass_cutFn
decls.statement: theorem mass_cutFn (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : L.mass p (cutFn S m) = L.lam (.lad m) * (1 - S.eps m) ^ p + ∑ y ∈ window m, L.lam (.lad y) * S.eps y ^ p
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_step2` / `eq:doubling_stepp`, the identity.** The `L^p(λ)` mass of the per-cut defect is a bare sum of point masses: `eq:doubling_step1` has disjoint supports.

decls.name: rpow_split
decls.statement: private theorem rpow_split {x p : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) : x ^ p = x ^ (p - 1) * x

decls.name: mass_cutFn_le_mid
decls.statement: theorem mass_cutFn_le_mid (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : L.mass p (cutFn S m) ≤ L.lam (.lad m) * (1 - S.eps m) * ((1 - S.eps m) ^ (p - 1) + S.epsMax ^ (p - 1))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_step2`, the middle term.** Cut balance collapses the window sum: the defect's `L^p(λ)` mass is at most `λ_m(1−ε(m))·((1−ε(m))^{p−1} + ε_max^{p−1})`, which at `p = 2` is the paper's `λ_m(1−ε(m))(1−ε(m)+ε_max)`.

decls.name: mass_cutFn_le_two
decls.statement: theorem mass_cutFn_le_two (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : L.mass p (cutFn S m) ≤ 2 * L.lam (.lad m)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_step2` / `eq:doubling_stepp`, the bound.** The defect's `L^p(λ)` mass is at most `2 λ_m` — twice the mass at the cut — for every `p ∈ [1, ∞)`, uniformly in `p`.

decls.name: Stat.tailMass
decls.statement: noncomputable def Stat.tailMass (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `L(m) = λ([m,∞))` on the loop closure, `λ^K([m,K])` on the truncation — the tail mass.

decls.name: Stat.hasSum_tailMass
decls.statement: theorem Stat.hasSum_tailMass (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) : HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * tailInd cap m x) (L.tailMass m)

decls.name: Stat.tailMass_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem Stat.tailMass_nonneg (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) : 0 ≤ L.tailMass m

decls.name: Stat.hasSum_one
decls.statement: theorem Stat.hasSum_one (L : Stat S cap) : HasSum L.lam 1

decls.name: Stat.hasSum_coTail
decls.statement: theorem Stat.hasSum_coTail (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) : HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * (1 - tailInd cap m x)) (1 - L.tailMass m)
decls.doc: The complement carries `1 − L(m)`.

decls.name: Stat.tailMass_le_one
decls.statement: theorem Stat.tailMass_le_one (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) : L.tailMass m ≤ 1

decls.name: Stat.centredTail
decls.statement: noncomputable def Stat.centredTail (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: `f_m := 1_A − L(m)`, the **centred tail indicator** of `def:doubling_setting`.

decls.name: Stat.tsum_centredTail
decls.statement: theorem Stat.tsum_centredTail (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) : ∑' x, L.lam x * L.centredTail m x = 0
decls.doc: **`Π f_m = 0`.** Centring is exactly subtracting the `λ`-mean.

decls.name: centredTail_defect
decls.statement: theorem centredTail_defect (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) {x : St} (hx : OnChain cap x) : L.centredTail m x - pstar S cap (L.centredTail m) x = cutFn S m x
decls.doc: **The defect of `f_m` is the defect of `1_A`.** Centring changes nothing: `P⋆` fixes the constants (`pstar_const`), so the constant is a `0`-flow.

decls.name: Stat.mass_centredTail
decls.statement: theorem Stat.mass_centredTail (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : L.mass p (L.centredTail m) = L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m) ^ p + (1 - L.tailMass m) * L.tailMass m ^ p
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_stepp`, second line.** `‖f_m‖^p_{L^p(λ)} = L(1−L)^p + (1−L)L^p`.

decls.name: Stat.mass_centredTail_ge
decls.statement: theorem Stat.mass_centredTail_ge (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m) ^ p ≤ L.mass p (L.centredTail m)
decls.doc: The denominator of `eq:doubling_step3`, bounded below: `‖f_m‖^p ≥ L(1−L)^p`.

decls.name: Stat.mass_congr_onChain
decls.statement: theorem Stat.mass_congr_onChain (L : Stat S cap) (p : ℝ) {f g : St → ℝ} (h : ∀ x, OnChain cap x → f x = g x) : L.mass p f = L.mass p g
decls.doc: Masses only see the chain: `λ` vanishes off it, so two functions agreeing on the chain have the same `L^p(λ)` mass.

decls.name: Stat.mass_centredTail_defect
decls.statement: theorem Stat.mass_centredTail_defect (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) (p : ℝ) : L.mass p (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S cap (L.centredTail m) x) = L.mass p (cutFn S m)
decls.doc: The `L^p(λ)` mass of `(Id − P⋆)f_m` is that of the per-cut defect.

decls.name: Stat.mass_defect_le
decls.statement: theorem Stat.mass_defect_le (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : L.mass p (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S cap (L.centredTail m) x) ≤ 2 * L.lam (.lad m)
decls.doc: **The numerator of `eq:doubling_step3`.** `‖(Id − P⋆)f_m‖^p_{L^p(λ)} ≤ 2 λ_m`, for every `p ∈ [1,∞)` and on either chain.

decls.name: Stat.mass_two_centredTail
decls.statement: theorem Stat.mass_two_centredTail (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) : L.mass 2 (L.centredTail m) = L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m)
decls.doc: **`‖f_m‖²_{L²(λ)} = L(1−L)`**, exactly — the denominator of `eq:doubling_step3`.

decls.name: Stat.rayleigh_two_le
decls.statement: theorem Stat.rayleigh_two_le (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) (hpos : 0 < L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m)) : L.mass 2 (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S cap (L.centredTail m) x) / L.mass 2 (L.centredTail m) ≤ 2 * L.lam (.lad m) / (L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_step3`, squared.** The squared Rayleigh quotient of `f_m` is at most `2λ_m / (L(1−L))`: the defect is controlled by the mass at the *cut*, the function by the mass of the whole *tail*.

decls.name: Stat.lam_le_tailMass
decls.statement: theorem Stat.lam_le_tailMass (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hm : inTail cap m m) : L.lam (.lad m) ≤ L.tailMass m
decls.doc: `λ_m ≤ L(m)`: the cut itself lies in the tail.

decls.name: Stat.lam_one_le_coTailMass
decls.statement: theorem Stat.lam_one_le_coTailMass (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hm1 : 1 < m) : L.lam (.lad 1) ≤ 1 - L.tailMass m
decls.doc: `λ_1 ≤ 1 − L(m)`: the state `1` lies outside the tail, since `m > d ≥ 1`.

decls.name: Stat.tailMass_mul_coTail_pos
decls.statement: theorem Stat.tailMass_mul_coTail_pos (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) : 0 < L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m)
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_percut` Step 1.** `0 < λ_m ≤ L(m) ≤ 1 − λ_1 < 1`, so `‖f_m‖² = L(1−L) > 0` and the Rayleigh quotient of `eq:doubling_step3` is well posed.

decls.name: Stat.rayleigh_two_le'
decls.statement: theorem Stat.rayleigh_two_le' (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) : L.mass 2 (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S cap (L.centredTail m) x) / L.mass 2 (L.centredTail m) ≤ 2 * L.lam (.lad m) / (L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_step3`**, with the positivity hypothesis discharged by Step 1.

files.title: The loop closure carries no invariant probability when the doubling flux is supercritical

decls.name: Icc_one_eq_Ioc_zero
decls.statement: theorem Icc_one_eq_Ioc_zero (b : ℕ) : Finset.Icc 1 b = Finset.Ioc 0 b

decls.name: Icc_succ_eq_Ioc
decls.statement: theorem Icc_succ_eq_Ioc (a b : ℕ) : Finset.Icc (a + 1) b = Finset.Ioc a b

decls.name: window_swap_shift
decls.statement: theorem window_swap_shift (M N : ℕ) : ∀ (m j : ℕ), (m ∈ Finset.Icc (M + 1) N ∧ j ∈ window m) ↔ (m ∈ Finset.Icc (max M j + 1) (min N (2 * j)) ∧ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N)
decls.doc: The index swap: `m ∈ (M,N]` and `j ∈ W(m)` iff `m ∈ (max(M,j), min(N,2j)]` and `j ∈ {1,…,N}`.

decls.name: window_double_sum_shift
decls.statement: theorem window_double_sum_shift (M N : ℕ) (F : ℕ → ℝ) : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc (M + 1) N, ∑ j ∈ window m, F j = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ((min N (2 * j) - max M j : ℕ) : ℝ) * F j
decls.doc: **The double-counting step from a shifted foot.** The source index `j` is carried across exactly `min(N,2j) − max(M,j)` of the cuts `M+1, …, N`.

decls.name: cut_tail_ge
decls.statement: theorem cut_tail_ge (S : Setting) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ j, 0 ≤ lam j) {M T : ℕ} (hM1 : 1 ≤ M) (hMT : M ≤ T) (hcb : ∀ m, M < m → lam m * (1 - S.eps m) = ∑ j ∈ window m, lam j * S.eps j) (hthr : ∀ m, M < m → 1 ≤ ((m : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps m) : (M : ℝ) * (lam M * S.eps M) ≤ ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc (T + 1) (2 * T), lam m
decls.doc: **The block estimate.** Let `λ ≥ 0` satisfy the cut balance above `M` and let the drift coefficient `(m+1)ε(m)` be at least `1` above `M`.

decls.name: isEmpty_stat_of_supercritical
decls.statement: theorem isEmpty_stat_of_supercritical (S : Setting) {M : ℕ} (hM1 : 1 ≤ M) (hMd : S.d ≤ M) (hthr : ∀ m, M < m → 1 ≤ ((m : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps m) : IsEmpty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_phase`(2)–(3), in the form this library consumes.** If the drift coefficient `(m+1)ε(m)` is at least `1` past an index `M ≥ max(d,1)`, the loop-closed chain carries no invariant probability.

decls.name: isEmpty_stat_of_family_ge_one
decls.statement: theorem isEmpty_stat_of_family_ge_one {c : ℝ} (hc1 : 1 ≤ c) (S : Setting) (hS : S.eps = epsCS c 1) : IsEmpty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_phase`(3), the `1 ≤ c < 2` half.** At `s = 1` the drift coefficient is the constant `c`, so `c ≥ 1` already forbids an invariant probability — with no threshold to find.

decls.name: isEmpty_stat_of_family_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem isEmpty_stat_of_family_lt_one {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : s < 1) (S : Setting) (hS : S.eps = epsCS c s) : IsEmpty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_phase`(2), weakened to non-existence.** At `s < 1` the drift coefficient `c(m+1)^{1−s}` grows without bound, so it passes `1` at an explicit index and the loop closure carries no invariant probability.

files.title: The loop closure carries an invariant probability whenever the doubling flux is subcritical

decls.name: partial_sum_weighted_le
decls.statement: theorem partial_sum_weighted_le {lam g : ℕ → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ j, 0 ≤ lam j) (N : ℕ) (hrec : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → m ≤ N → lam m * (1 - S.eps m) ≤ ∑ j ∈ window m, lam j * S.eps j + g m) : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, lam m * (1 - ((m : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps m) ≤ ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, g m
decls.doc: **The partial-sum bound, before the family is substituted.** A non-negative sequence obeying the cut balance up to an excess `g` on `{1,…,N}` satisfies `Σ_{m≤N} λ_m(1 − (m+1)ε(m)) ≤ Σ_{m≤N} g_m`.

decls.name: partial_sum_le_of_threshold
decls.statement: theorem partial_sum_le_of_threshold {lam g : ℕ → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ j, 0 ≤ lam j) {θ : ℝ} (hθ0 : 0 ≤ θ) (m₀ : ℕ) (hthr : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → m₀ ≤ m → ((m : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps m ≤ θ) (hrec : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → lam m * (1 - S.eps m) ≤ ∑ j ∈ window m, lam j * S.eps j + g m) (N : ℕ) : (1 - θ) * ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, lam m ≤ (∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, g m) + ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m₀, lam m * (((m : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps m)
decls.doc: **The threshold form.** If `(m+1)ε(m) ≤ θ` past `m₀`, the partial sums of `λ` are bounded by the excess plus the finitely many terms below `m₀`, divided by `1 − θ`.

decls.name: statSeq_partial_sum_bounded
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_partial_sum_bounded {θ : ℝ} (hθ0 : 0 ≤ θ) (hθ1 : θ < 1) (m₀ : ℕ) (hthr : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → m₀ ≤ m → ((m : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps m ≤ θ) (N : ℕ) : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, statSeq S m ≤ (S.jbar + ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m₀, statSeq S m * (((m : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps m)) / (1 - θ)
decls.doc: **The uniform bound on the partial sums of `statSeq`.** At `θ = c`, `m₀ = 0` this is `statSeq_partial_sum_le`'s `j̄/(1−c)`.

decls.name: summable_statSeq_of_threshold
decls.statement: theorem summable_statSeq_of_threshold {θ : ℝ} (hθ0 : 0 ≤ θ) (hθ1 : θ < 1) (m₀ : ℕ) (hthr : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → m₀ ≤ m → ((m : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps m ≤ θ) : Summable (statSeq S)
decls.doc: **Summability under the threshold.** The one place `θ < 1` is spent.

decls.name: exists_stat_none_of_summable
decls.statement: theorem exists_stat_none_of_summable (S : Setting) (hsummable : Summable (statSeq S)) : Nonempty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: **The construction, given summability.** Everything but summability in `exists_stat_none` is independent of the family: `statSeq` solves the row-corrected cut balance at every `Setting`, `statSeq_point` is its pointwise form, and `inv_of_pointwise` promotes that to the integral invariance `Stat` asks for.

decls.name: exists_stat_of_threshold
decls.statement: theorem exists_stat_of_threshold (S : Setting) {θ : ℝ} (hθ0 : 0 ≤ θ) (hθ1 : θ < 1) (m₀ : ℕ) (hthr : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → m₀ ≤ m → ((m : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps m ≤ θ) : Nonempty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: **The threshold criterion.** A backward policy whose drift coefficient `(m+1)ε(m)` is eventually at most some `θ < 1` carries an invariant probability on the loop closure.

decls.name: exists_threshold_family
decls.statement: theorem exists_threshold_family {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 1 < s) : ∃ m₀ : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → m₀ ≤ m → ((m : ℝ) + 1) * epsCS c s m ≤ 1 / 2
decls.doc: **Step 3's `j₀`, made explicit.** At `s > 1` the drift coefficient falls below `½` past `m₀ ≥ (2c)^{1/(s−1)}` — the paper's "fix `j₀` with `c(j+1)^{1−s} − 1 ≤ −½` for `j > j₀`".

decls.name: exists_stat_of_family_gt_one
decls.statement: theorem exists_stat_of_family_gt_one {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 1 < s) (S : Setting) (hS : S.eps = epsCS c s) : Nonempty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_phase`(1), in the form this library consumes.** At `s > 1` the loop-closed chain carries an invariant probability, positive at every state.

decls.name: exists_stat_of_family_one
decls.statement: theorem exists_stat_of_family_one {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (S : Setting) (hS : S.eps = epsCS c 1) : Nonempty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: **Row (b) re-derived from the same threshold**, at `θ = c` and `m₀ = 0`: at `s = 1` the drift coefficient is the constant `c`.

files.title: Pointwise invariance implies the integral form

decls.name: stEquiv
decls.statement: def stEquiv : ℕ ≃ St
decls.doc: `ℕ ≃ St`: `0 ↦ s_f` and `k+1 ↦ lad k`.

decls.name: hasSum_st
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_st {g : St → ℝ} {A : ℝ} (h : HasSum (fun k : ℕ => g (.lad k)) A) : HasSum g (A + g .sink)
decls.doc: A summable family on the ladder extends to `St` by adding the value at the sink.

decls.name: inv_of_pointwise
decls.statement: theorem inv_of_pointwise (S : Setting) {mu : St → ℝ} (hnn : ∀ x, 0 ≤ mu x) (hsum : Summable (fun k : ℕ => mu (.lad k))) (hsink : mu .sink = mu (.lad 0)) (hpt : ∀ k : ℕ, mu (.lad k) = mu (.lad (k + 1)) * (1 - S.eps (k + 1)) + (if 1 ≤ k ∧ 2 ∣ k then mu (.lad (k / 2)) * S.eps (k / 2) else 0) + mu .sink * S.row k) (f : St → ℝ) (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : ∑' x, mu x * pstar S none f x = ∑' x, mu x * f x
decls.doc: **`Stat.of_pointwise`, on the loop closure.** A non-negative, ladder-summable measure on `St` satisfying the pointwise balance equations satisfies the integral invariance `∫P⋆f dμ = ∫f dμ` against every bounded `f` — which is the `inv` field of `Stat` and of `PreStat`.

files.title: `lem:doubling_product`: the weight of a descent is `1 + O(1/ℓ)` in expectation

decls.name: exp_neg_two_mul_le_one_sub
decls.statement: theorem exp_neg_two_mul_le_one_sub {y : ℝ} (hy0 : 0 ≤ y) (hy1 : y ≤ 1 / 2) : Real.exp (-(2 * y)) ≤ 1 - y
decls.doc: **`1 − y ≥ e^{−2y}` on `[0,½]`**, the paper's inequality in the last line of the proof of `lem:doubling_product`.

decls.name: prodW
decls.statement: noncomputable def prodW (D : Decay) (ℓ : ℕ) (b : ℕ → ℝ) (z : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The weighted product of a descent.** `prodW ℓ b z = E(∏_{n<N_ℓ}(1 + b(Y_n)) | Y₀ = z)`, as the recursion in the state that characterises it: the factor at the current state times the average of the same quantity after one step of the transition law `Decay.pk`, and `1` once the descent has fallen below `2ℓ`.

decls.name: prodW_of_lt
decls.statement: theorem prodW_of_lt {ℓ : ℕ} (b : ℕ → ℝ) {z : ℕ} (h : z < 2 * ℓ) : D.prodW ℓ b z = 1

decls.name: prodW_of_ge
decls.statement: theorem prodW_of_ge {ℓ : ℕ} (b : ℕ → ℝ) {z : ℕ} (h : ¬ z < 2 * ℓ) : D.prodW ℓ b z = (1 + b z) * ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j * D.prodW ℓ b j

decls.name: thr_of_two_level
decls.statement: theorem thr_of_two_level {ℓ y : ℕ} (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) (hy : 2 * ℓ ≤ y) : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)
decls.doc: Every state `≥ 2ℓ` clears the threshold `32cτ`, at a level `ℓ` with `32cτ ≤ 2ℓ`.

decls.name: prodW_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem prodW_nonneg {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) {b : ℕ → ℝ} (hb : ∀ y : ℕ, 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ 1 + b y) (z : ℕ) : 0 ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
decls.doc: The product of non-negative factors is non-negative: the paper's "the factors being positive".

decls.name: sojMean_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem sojMean_nonneg {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (z : ℕ) : 0 ≤ D.sojMean L z
decls.doc: `E(ς)` is non-negative, at every state.

decls.name: one_le_sojMean
decls.statement: theorem one_le_sojMean {L z : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hz : L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L) : 1 ≤ D.sojMean L z
decls.doc: `E(ς) ≥ 1` inside the block: one step is always taken there.

decls.name: prodW_block_le
decls.statement: theorem prodW_block_le {ℓ L : ℕ} (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hLℓ : 2 * ℓ ≤ L) {b : ℕ → ℝ} (hbnn : ∀ y : ℕ, 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ 1 + b y) {zeta A : ℝ} (hzeta : 0 ≤ zeta) (hup : ∀ y : ℕ, L ≤ y → y < 2 * L → 1 + b y ≤ zeta) (hbelow : ∀ w : ℕ, w < L → D.prodW ℓ b w ≤ A) : ∀ z : ℕ, z < 2 * L → D.prodW ℓ b z ≤ A * D.sojGF L zeta z
decls.doc: **The block step, upper half.** If `1 + b ≤ ζ` on `I = [L,2L)` and `Ψ ≤ A` below `L`, then `Ψ(z) ≤ A · E(ζ^ς | Y₀ = z)` for every `z < 2L`.

decls.name: prodW_block_ge
decls.statement: theorem prodW_block_ge {ℓ L : ℕ} (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hLℓ : 2 * ℓ ≤ L) {b : ℕ → ℝ} (hbnn : ∀ y : ℕ, 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ 1 + b y) {x A : ℝ} (hx1 : x ≤ 1) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hlow : ∀ y : ℕ, L ≤ y → y < 2 * L → 1 - x ≤ 1 + b y) (hbelow : ∀ w : ℕ, w < L → A ≤ D.prodW ℓ b w) : ∀ z : ℕ, z < 2 * L → A * (1 - x * D.sojMean L z) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
decls.doc: **The block step, lower half.** If `1 − x ≤ 1 + b` on `I = [L,2L)` and `A ≤ Ψ` below `L`, then `A · (1 − x·E(ς | Y₀ = z)) ≤ Ψ(z)` for every `z < 2L`.

decls.name: sixteen_lt_level
decls.statement: theorem sixteen_lt_level (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) : (16 : ℝ) < (ℓ : ℝ)
decls.doc: The level clears `16`: `2ℓ ≥ 32cτ > 32`, because `cτ = p_* + c > 1` (`one_lt_ctau`).

decls.name: gam_sq_lt_quarter
decls.statement: theorem gam_sq_lt_quarter : D.gam ^ 2 < 1 / 4

decls.name: one_add_b_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem one_add_b_nonneg (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) (hH0 : 0 ≤ H) (hH : H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ) / 6) (hbb : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / (y : ℝ)) : ∀ y : ℕ, 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ 1 + b y
decls.doc: **Every factor of the product is positive.** `|b| ≤ H/(2ℓ) ≤ γ²/12 < 1` above `2ℓ`, which is the paper's "every factor lies in `[½,3/2]`" in the only direction the recursion needs.

decls.name: abs_b_le_block
decls.statement: theorem abs_b_le_block (hH0 : 0 ≤ H) (hbb : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / (y : ℝ)) {L : ℕ} (hℓL : ℓ ≤ L) (hLpos : (0 : ℝ) < (L : ℝ)) {y : ℕ} (hy : L ≤ y) : |b y| ≤ H / (L : ℝ)
decls.doc: Above a block floor `L ≥ ℓ`, the bound `|b(y)| ≤ H/y` reads `|b(y)| ≤ H/L`.

decls.name: prodW_step_le
decls.statement: theorem prodW_step_le (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) (hH0 : 0 ≤ H) (hH : H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ) / 6) (hbb : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / (y : ℝ)) {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hLℓ : 2 * ℓ ≤ L) {A : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hbelow : ∀ w : ℕ, w < L → D.prodW ℓ b w ≤ A) : ∀ z : ℕ, z < 2 * L → D.prodW ℓ b z ≤ A * (1 + D.c5 * H / (L : ℝ))
decls.doc: **One block of the paper's induction, upper half.** `φ_i ≤ φ_{i−1}(1 + c₅H/L)` at `L = 2^i ℓ`: the block comparison `prodW_block_le` at `ζ = 1 + H/L`, followed by the third line of `eq:doubling_sojourn`.

decls.name: prodW_step_ge
decls.statement: theorem prodW_step_ge (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) (hH0 : 0 ≤ H) (hH : H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ) / 6) (hbb : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / (y : ℝ)) {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hLℓ : 2 * ℓ ≤ L) {A : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hbelow : ∀ w : ℕ, w < L → A ≤ D.prodW ℓ b w) : ∀ z : ℕ, z < 2 * L → A * (1 - 2 * H / (D.gam ^ 2 * (L : ℝ))) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
decls.doc: **One block of the paper's induction, lower half.** `φ̲_i ≥ φ̲_{i−1}(1 − 2H/(γ²L))` at `L = 2^i ℓ`: the block comparison `prodW_block_ge` at `x = H/L`, followed by the second line of `eq:doubling_sojourn`.

decls.name: prodW_level_le
decls.statement: theorem prodW_level_le (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) (hH0 : 0 ≤ H) (hH : H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ) / 6) (hbb : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / (y : ℝ)) : ∀ i z : ℕ, z < 2 ^ (i + 1) * ℓ → D.prodW ℓ b z ≤ Real.exp (D.c5 * H / (ℓ : ℝ) * (1 - 1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ i))
decls.doc: **The level invariant, upper half.** `Ψ(z) ≤ exp(c₅H/ℓ·(1 − 2^{−i}))` for every `z < 2^{i+1}ℓ` — the paper's `φ_i ≤ ∏_{r≤i}(1 + c₅H2^{−r}/ℓ)`, with the partial geometric sum kept, so that the induction on `i` is exact rather than asymptotic.

decls.name: prodW_level_ge
decls.statement: theorem prodW_level_ge (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) (hH0 : 0 ≤ H) (hH : H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ) / 6) (hbb : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / (y : ℝ)) : ∀ i z : ℕ, z < 2 ^ (i + 1) * ℓ → Real.exp (-(4 * H / (D.gam ^ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) * (1 - 1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ i))) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
decls.doc: **The level invariant, lower half.** `Ψ(z) ≥ exp(−4H/(γ²ℓ)·(1 − 2^{−i}))` for every `z < 2^{i+1}ℓ` — the paper's `φ̲_i ≥ e^{−4H/(γ²ℓ)}`, again with the partial sum kept.

decls.name: prodW_two_sided
decls.statement: theorem prodW_two_sided (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) (hH0 : 0 ≤ H) (hH : H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ) / 6) (hbb : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / (y : ℝ)) (z : ℕ) : Real.exp (-(D.c5 * H / (ℓ : ℝ))) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z ∧ D.prodW ℓ b z ≤ Real.exp (D.c5 * H / (ℓ : ℝ))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_product`.** `e^{−c₅H/ℓ} ≤ E(∏_{n<N_ℓ}(1+b(Y_n)) | Y₀ = z) ≤ e^{c₅H/ℓ}`.

decls.name: prodW_two_sided_paper
decls.statement: theorem prodW_two_sided_paper {d : ℕ} (hℓ : D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ) (hH0 : 0 ≤ H) (hH : H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ) / 6) (hbb : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / (y : ℝ)) {m : ℕ} (_hm : 2 * ℓ ≤ m) : Real.exp (-(D.c5 * H / (ℓ : ℝ))) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b m ∧ D.prodW ℓ b m ≤ Real.exp (D.c5 * H / (ℓ : ℝ))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_product`, in the paper's own form**: at a level `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂` and a starting state `m ≥ 2ℓ`.

decls.name: prodW_R0_eq_descOne
decls.statement: theorem prodW_R0_eq_descOne {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) {bb : ℕ → ℝ} (hbb : ∀ y : ℕ, bb y = D.R0 y - 1) (z : ℕ) : D.prodW ℓ bb z = D.descOne ℓ z
decls.doc: The two recursions coincide at `b := R₀ − 1`: `(1 + (R₀(z) − 1))·(w_z(j)/R₀(z)) = w_z(j)`, so `prodW ℓ (R₀ − 1) = descOne ℓ`.

decls.name: m0
decls.statement: noncomputable def m0 (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) : ℕ
decls.doc: **`m₀` of `theo:doubling_decay`**, `max(ℓ₂, ⌈6c₄/γ²⌉)`: the level at which `eq:doubling_product` may be run at `b := R₀ − 1` and `H := c₄`, i.e.

decls.name: ell2_le_m0
decls.statement: theorem ell2_le_m0 (d : ℕ) : D.ell2 d ≤ D.m0 d

decls.name: lt_m0
decls.statement: theorem lt_m0 (d : ℕ) : d < D.m0 d

decls.name: descOne_two_sided
decls.statement: theorem descOne_two_sided {d ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : D.m0 d ≤ ℓ) (y : ℕ) : Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))) ≤ D.descOne ℓ y ∧ D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_product` at `b := R₀ − 1`, `H := c₄`.** The expected weight of a descent is `1 + O(1/ℓ)`, two-sidedly: `e^{−c₅c₄/ℓ} ≤ E(Z_ℓ | Y₀ = y) ≤ e^{c₅c₄/ℓ}` with `c₄ = 16cτ`.

decls.name: decay_block_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem decay_block_of_cutBal {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞} (h : D.CutBal d lam M₁) (hℓ : D.m0 d ≤ ℓ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : ∀ j, ℓ ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) {m : ℕ} (hm : ℓ ≤ m) (hM : (m : ℕ∞) ≤ M₁) : a * Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))) ≤ D.uu lam m ∧ D.uu lam m ≤ b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_block`, unconditional.** One block of the rescaled profile bounds every index above it, within `e^{±c₅c₄/ℓ}` — `theo:doubling_decay`(1), with `min`/`max` over `[ℓ,2ℓ)` replaced by any pair bracketing the profile there, which is what `Decay.decay_block` takes and what its two uses supply.

decls.name: decay_two_sided_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem decay_two_sided_of_cutBal {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hpos : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) (hℓ : D.m0 d ≤ ℓ) : ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j ∧ lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_decay`(2), unconditional.** Every positive sequence satisfying the cut balance above `d` obeys `c₁ j^{−p_*} ≤ λ_j ≤ c₂ j^{−p_*}` for every `j ≥ 1`, with no hypothesis left beyond the cut balance and positivity: `eq:doubling_product` has discharged `hlo`/`hhi`.

decls.name: uu_bounded_explicit
decls.statement: theorem uu_bounded_explicit {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hℓ : D.m0 d ≤ ℓ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → a * Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))) ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_decay` in the `u` variable, with the constants written out.** If the rescaled profile lies in `[a, b]` on the initial block `1 ≤ j < 2ℓ`, `ℓ ≥ m₀`, then on the whole ladder it lies in `[a e^{−c₅c₄/ℓ}, b e^{c₅c₄/ℓ}]`, `c₄ = 16cτ`.

decls.name: decay_two_sided_explicit
decls.statement: theorem decay_two_sided_explicit {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hℓ : D.m0 d ≤ ℓ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → a * Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))) * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j ∧ lam j ≤ b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ)) * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_decay` with the constants written out** — `theo:doubling_decay`(2) and its dependence clause.

files.title: `eq:doubling_R0`: the total window weight is `1 + O(1/m)`, effectively

decls.name: rpow_sub_one_eq
decls.statement: theorem rpow_sub_one_eq {t q : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) : t ^ (q - 1) = t ^ q / t

decls.name: window_eq
decls.statement: theorem window_eq (m : ℕ) : window m = Finset.Ico ((m + 1) / 2) m
decls.doc: The foot of the window, `⌈m/2⌉`.

decls.name: foot_le
decls.statement: theorem foot_le (m : ℕ) : ((m : ℝ)) / 2 ≤ (((m + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ)

decls.name: le_foot
decls.statement: theorem le_foot (m : ℕ) : (((m + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((m : ℝ) + 1) / 2

decls.name: one_le_foot
decls.statement: theorem one_le_foot {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : 1 ≤ (m + 1) / 2

decls.name: foot_le_self
decls.statement: theorem foot_le_self {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : (m + 1) / 2 ≤ m

decls.name: R0_eq
decls.statement: theorem R0_eq {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : D.R0 m = D.c / (1 - D.eps m) * ((m : ℝ) ^ D.p * ∑ j ∈ window m, (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) / ((j : ℝ) + 1))
decls.doc: `R₀(m)` in the form the comparison uses: a constant times `m^p` times a window sum.

decls.name: term_le
decls.statement: theorem term_le {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) / ((j : ℝ) + 1) ≤ (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p - 1)
decls.doc: Term by term: `j^{−p}/(j+1) ≤ j^{−p−1}`.

decls.name: le_term
decls.doc: Term by term: `j^{−p−1} − j^{−p−2} ≤ j^{−p}/(j+1)`, since `(j−1)(j+1) ≤ j²`.

decls.name: windowSum_le
decls.statement: theorem windowSum_le {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : ∑ j ∈ window m, (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) / ((j : ℝ) + 1) ≤ ∑ j ∈ window m, (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p - 1)
decls.doc: The window sum, above.

decls.name: windowSum_ge
decls.statement: theorem windowSum_ge {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : (∑ j ∈ window m, (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p - 1)) - ∑ j ∈ window m, (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p - 1 - 1) ≤ ∑ j ∈ window m, (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: The window sum, below.

decls.name: half_rpow
decls.statement: theorem half_rpow (hm : 1 ≤ m) : ((m : ℝ) / 2) ^ (-D.p) = D.tau * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)

decls.name: foot_rpow_le
decls.statement: theorem foot_rpow_le (hm : 1 ≤ m) : (((m + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ D.tau * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)
decls.doc: `a^{−p} ≤ τ m^{−p}`, since `a ≥ m/2`.

decls.name: le_foot_rpow
decls.statement: theorem le_foot_rpow (hm : 1 ≤ m) : D.tau * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) * (1 - D.p / (m : ℝ)) ≤ (((m + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)

decls.name: R0_sub_one_le
decls.statement: theorem R0_sub_one_le (hm : 1 ≤ m) : |D.R0 m - 1| ≤ 16 * D.c * D.tau / (m : ℝ)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_R0`, second half, effectivized.** `|R₀(m) − 1| ≤ 16cτ/m` at every `m ≥ 1`.

decls.name: R0_between
decls.statement: theorem R0_between (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmb : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (m : ℝ)) : 1 / 2 ≤ D.R0 m ∧ D.R0 m ≤ 2
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_R0`, first half.** `½ ≤ R₀(m) ≤ 2` once `m ≥ 32cτ`.

files.title: The clipped ramp: the exponent `p = ∞`

decls.name: rampFn
decls.statement: noncomputable def rampFn (N : ℕ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: `r_N := min(V, N)`, the clipped ramp of `lem:doubling_ramp`.

decls.name: rampFn_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem rampFn_sink (N : ℕ) : rampFn N .sink = 0

decls.name: rampFn_lad
decls.statement: theorem rampFn_lad (N j : ℕ) : rampFn N (.lad j) = min (j : ℝ) (N : ℝ)

decls.name: rampFn_lad_le
decls.statement: theorem rampFn_lad_le (N j : ℕ) (h : j ≤ N) : rampFn N (.lad j) = (j : ℝ)

decls.name: rampFn_lad_ge
decls.statement: theorem rampFn_lad_ge (N j : ℕ) (h : N ≤ j) : rampFn N (.lad j) = (N : ℝ)

decls.name: rampFn_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem rampFn_nonneg (N : ℕ) (x : St) : 0 ≤ rampFn N x

decls.name: rampFn_le
decls.statement: theorem rampFn_le (N : ℕ) (x : St) : rampFn N x ≤ (N : ℝ)

decls.name: rampFn_bounded
decls.statement: theorem rampFn_bounded (N : ℕ) : ∃ C, ∀ x, |rampFn N x| ≤ C

decls.name: ramp_defect_src
decls.statement: theorem ramp_defect_src (N : ℕ) : rampFn N (.lad 0) - pstar S none (rampFn N) (.lad 0) = 0
decls.doc: At the source the ramp and its image both vanish.

decls.name: ramp_defect_sink
decls.statement: theorem ramp_defect_sink (hN : S.d ≤ N) : rampFn N .sink - pstar S none (rampFn N) .sink = -S.jbar
decls.doc: At the sink the defect is `−j̄`: the target row has mean `j̄` and `r_N = V` on `{1,…,d}`.

decls.name: ramp_defect_below
decls.statement: theorem ramp_defect_below {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (h2m : 2 * m ≤ N) : rampFn N (.lad m) - pstar S none (rampFn N) (.lad m) = 1 - S.eps m * ((m : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: Below the clip: the defect is `1 − ε(m)(m+1)`.

decls.name: ramp_defect_straddle
decls.statement: theorem ramp_defect_straddle {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmN : m ≤ N) (h2m : N < 2 * m) : rampFn N (.lad m) - pstar S none (rampFn N) (.lad m) = 1 - S.eps m * ((N : ℝ) - (m : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: Straddling the clip: the defect is `1 − ε(m)(N−m+1)`, and `2m > N` keeps `N−m+1 ≤ m+1`.

decls.name: ramp_defect_above
decls.statement: theorem ramp_defect_above {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmN : N < m) : rampFn N (.lad m) - pstar S none (rampFn N) (.lad m) = 0
decls.doc: Above the clip every image carries the value `N`, so the defect vanishes.

decls.name: ramp_defect_bounded
decls.statement: theorem ramp_defect_bounded {γ : ℝ} (hγ : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → ((j : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps j ≤ γ) (hN : S.d ≤ N) (x : St) : |rampFn N x - pstar S none (rampFn N) x| ≤ max 1 (max γ S.jbar)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_ramp`, second line.** The defect of the clipped ramp is bounded by `max(1, γ, j̄)`, uniformly in `N`.

decls.name: rampMean
decls.statement: noncomputable def rampMean (N : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `Π r_N`, the `λ`-mean of the clipped ramp.

decls.name: rampMean_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem rampMean_nonneg (N : ℕ) : 0 ≤ L.rampMean N

decls.name: rampMean_le
decls.statement: theorem rampMean_le (N : ℕ) : L.rampMean N ≤ (N : ℝ)

decls.name: centredRamp
decls.statement: noncomputable def centredRamp (N : ℕ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: `r̃_N := r_N − Π r_N`, the centred clipped ramp.

decls.name: centredRamp_bounded
decls.statement: theorem centredRamp_bounded (N : ℕ) : ∃ C, ∀ x, |L.centredRamp N x| ≤ C

decls.name: tsum_centredRamp
decls.statement: theorem tsum_centredRamp (N : ℕ) : ∑' x, L.lam x * L.centredRamp N x = 0

decls.name: centredRamp_defect
decls.statement: theorem centredRamp_defect (N : ℕ) (x : St) : L.centredRamp N x - pstar S none (L.centredRamp N) x = rampFn N x - pstar S none (rampFn N) x
decls.doc: Centring leaves the defect unchanged: `P⋆` fixes the constants.

decls.name: exists_centredRamp_ge
decls.statement: theorem exists_centredRamp_ge (N : ℕ) : ∃ x : St, (N : ℝ) / 2 ≤ |L.centredRamp N x|
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_ramp`, first line.** The centred ramp attains `N/2` in absolute value: the two values `r_N(s₀) = 0` and `r_N(N) = N` are both attained, so one of `Π r_N` and `N − Π r_N` is at least `N/2`.

decls.name: no_bounded_inverse_infty
decls.statement: theorem no_bounded_inverse_infty {γ : ℝ} (hγ : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → ((j : ℝ) + 1) * S.eps j ≤ γ) : ¬ ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ (f : St → ℝ) (M D : ℝ), (∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) → (∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) → (∃ x, M ≤ |f x|) → (∀ x, |f x - pstar S none f x| ≤ D) → M ≤ B * D
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_ramp`, the conclusion.** No constant `B` bounds an attained lower bound of `‖f‖_∞` by a uniform upper bound of `‖(Id−P⋆)f‖_∞` over the **bounded** mean-zero `f`: the clipped ramps drive the `L^∞` Rayleigh quotient to zero.

decls.name: gamma_family
decls.statement: theorem gamma_family {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 1 ≤ s) (j : ℕ) (hj : 1 ≤ j) : ((j : ℝ) + 1) * epsCS c s j ≤ c * 2 ^ (1 - s)
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_ramp`, last sentence.** For the family, `γ = c·2^{1−s}` bounds `(j+1)ε(j)` exactly when `s ≥ 1`; the bound is stated, the "exactly when" being the observation that `(j+1)ε_{c,s}(j) = c(j+1)^{1−s}` is unbounded for `s < 1`.

files.title: The family `ε_{c,s}` and its standing range

decls.name: epsCS
decls.statement: noncomputable def epsCS (c s : ℝ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `ε_{c,s}(j) = c/(j+1)^s` of `eq:doubling_family`.

decls.name: base_pos
decls.statement: theorem base_pos (j : ℕ) : (0 : ℝ) < (j : ℝ) + 1

decls.name: epsCS_pos
decls.statement: theorem epsCS_pos {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (s : ℝ) (j : ℕ) : 0 < epsCS c s j
decls.doc: `ε_{c,s} > 0` — the doubling edge is present at every ladder state.

decls.name: epsCS_antitone
decls.statement: theorem epsCS_antitone {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 0 ≤ s) : Antitone (epsCS c s)
decls.doc: `ε_{c,s}` is non-increasing on `{1,2,3,…}`: the doubling probability decays along the ladder.

decls.name: epsCS_one
decls.statement: theorem epsCS_one (c s : ℝ) : epsCS c s 1 = c * 2 ^ (-s)
decls.doc: The supremum of the family, `ε_{c,s}(1) = c·2^{-s}`.

decls.name: epsCS_le_one_val
decls.statement: theorem epsCS_le_one_val {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 0 ≤ s) {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : epsCS c s j ≤ c * 2 ^ (-s)
decls.doc: Every value of the family on the ladder is at most `ε_{c,s}(1) = c·2^{-s}`.

decls.name: epsCS_one_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem epsCS_one_lt_one {c s : ℝ} (hcs : c < 2 ^ s) : c * 2 ^ (-s) < 1
decls.doc: `c < 2^s` is exactly what makes `ε_{c,s}(1) < 1`, hence the decrement edge out of the state `1` carry the positive probability `1 − c·2^{-s}`.

decls.name: one_sub_epsCS_one_pos
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_epsCS_one_pos {c s : ℝ} (hcs : c < 2 ^ s) : 0 < 1 - c * 2 ^ (-s)
decls.doc: The decrement edge out of the state `1` carries positive probability.

decls.name: Setting.ofFamily
decls.statement: noncomputable def Setting.ofFamily (c s : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hcs : c < 2 ^ s) (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (row : ℕ → ℝ) (hrow : ∀ j, 0 ≤ row j) (hsupp : ∀ ⦃j⦄, row j ≠ 0 → 1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ d) (hsum : ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, row j = 1) : Setting
decls.doc: The family, packaged as a `Setting`: `lem:doubling_range` is exactly the proof obligation that `ε_{c,s}` on the standing range satisfies the standing hypotheses, with `ε_max = c·2^{-s}`.

decls.name: Setting.ofFamily_eps
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem Setting.ofFamily_eps (c s : ℝ) (hc hs hcs) (d hd row hrow hsupp hsum) : (Setting.ofFamily c s hc hs hcs d hd row hrow hsupp hsum).eps = epsCS c s

files.title: The one-step ratio inequalities

decls.name: dirac_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem dirac_nonneg (j : ℕ) (x : St) : 0 ≤ dirac j x

decls.name: dirac_bounded
decls.statement: theorem dirac_bounded (j : ℕ) : ∃ C, ∀ x, |dirac j x| ≤ C

decls.name: Stat.hasSum_flux
decls.statement: theorem Stat.hasSum_flux (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) : HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * pstar S cap (dirac j) x) (L.lam (.lad j))
decls.doc: **Pointwise balance, from the integral form.** `λ_j` is the total one-step flux into `j`.

decls.name: Stat.flux_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem Stat.flux_nonneg (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) (x : St) : 0 ≤ L.lam x * pstar S cap (dirac j) x
decls.doc: Every one-step flux term is non-negative, so a single one may be kept and the rest discarded.

decls.name: pstar_dirac_double
decls.statement: theorem pstar_dirac_double {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) (hD : HasDouble cap j) : pstar S cap (dirac (2 * j)) (.lad j) = S.eps j
decls.doc: The doubling edge out of `j` carries `ε(j)` into `2j`.

decls.name: one_sub_eps_le_pstar_dirac_pred
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_eps_le_pstar_dirac_pred {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : 1 - S.eps m ≤ pstar S cap (dirac (m - 1)) (.lad m)
decls.doc: The decrement edge out of `m` carries at least `1 − ε(m)` into `m − 1`, with equality when the doubling edge survives and value `1` when it has been truncated away.

decls.name: Stat.lam_double_ge
decls.statement: theorem Stat.lam_double_ge (L : Stat S cap) {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) (hD : HasDouble cap j) : L.lam (.lad j) * S.eps j ≤ L.lam (.lad (2 * j))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_ratios`, first half.** `λ_{2j} ≥ λ_j ε(j)`: the doubling edge out of `j` deposits at least its own share at `2j`, whatever else arrives there.

decls.name: Stat.lam_le_prev
decls.statement: theorem Stat.lam_le_prev (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : L.lam (.lad m) * (1 - S.eps m) ≤ L.lam (.lad (m - 1))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_ratios`, second half.** `λ_m (1 − ε(m)) ≤ λ_{m−1}`.

files.title: From the `L²(λ)` Rayleigh inequality to the mass layer
variables: variable {S : Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap)

decls.name: memLp_two_of_bounded
decls.statement: theorem memLp_two_of_bounded {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : MemLp f 2 L.mu
decls.doc: A bounded function is in `L²(λ)`: `λ` is a probability.

decls.name: norm_sq_eq_mass_of_ae
decls.statement: theorem norm_sq_eq_mass_of_ae {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} {g : St → ℝ} (h : ⇑F =ᵐ[L.mu] g) (hg : MemLp g 2 L.mu) : ‖F‖ ^ 2 = L.mass 2 g
decls.doc: The `L²` norm squared of a class is the `mass` of any of its representatives, at every `cap`.

decls.name: tsum_lam_mul_congr_ae
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_mul_congr_ae {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} {g : St → ℝ} (h : ⇑F =ᵐ[L.mu] g) : ∑' x, L.lam x * (F : St → ℝ) x = ∑' x, L.lam x * g x
decls.doc: The `λ`-mean of a class is the `λ`-mean of any of its representatives, at every `cap`.

decls.name: coeFn_sub_pstarL2_toLp
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_sub_pstarL2_toLp (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : MemLp f 2 L.mu) : ⇑(hf.toLp f - L.pstarL2 hrow (hf.toLp f)) =ᵐ[L.mu] fun x => f x - pstar S cap f x
decls.doc: The defect class of the class of `f` is the class of the pointwise defect.

decls.name: rayleigh_of_leftInverse
decls.statement: theorem rayleigh_of_leftInverse (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} (hS : Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ‖F - L.piL2 F‖ ≤ ‖Sop‖ * ‖F - L.pstarL2 hrow F‖
decls.doc: A bounded left inverse `S` of `Id − P⋆` on `L²(λ)`, `S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π`, bounds the mean-zero part of every class by `‖S‖` times its defect.

decls.name: mass_le_of_rayleighL2
decls.statement: theorem mass_le_of_rayleighL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {B : ℝ} (hB : ∀ F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, ‖F - L.piL2 F‖ ≤ B * ‖F - L.pstarL2 hrow F‖) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) (hmean : ∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) : L.mass 2 f ≤ B ^ 2 * L.mass 2 (fun x => f x - pstar S cap f x)
decls.doc: **The bridge.** If `‖F − ΠF‖ ≤ B‖F − P⋆F‖` on `L²(λ)`, then every bounded mean-zero `f` has `mass 2 f ≤ B² · mass 2 ((Id − P⋆)f)`.

decls.name: mass_le_of_leftInverse
decls.statement: theorem mass_le_of_leftInverse (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} (hS : Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) (hmean : ∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) : L.mass 2 f ≤ ‖Sop‖ ^ 2 * L.mass 2 (fun x => f x - pstar S cap f x)
decls.doc: The bridge, fed by a left inverse: `mass 2 f ≤ ‖S‖² · mass 2 ((Id − P⋆)f)`.

files.title: The doubling graph: state space, backward policy, and invariant sequences
variables: variable {S : Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} {f g : St → ℝ}
variable {S : Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap)

decls.name: St
decls.statement: inductive St
decls.doc: The states of the doubling graph `eq:counterexample_graph`.

decls.name: src
decls.statement: @[match_pattern] abbrev src : St
decls.doc: The source `s₀`, which is the ladder index `0`.

decls.statement: instance : Countable St
decls.doc: `St` is countable: `lad j ↦ j + 1` and `sink ↦ 0` is injective into `ℕ`.

decls.statement: instance : Inhabited St

decls.name: HasDouble
decls.statement: def HasDouble : Option ℕ → ℕ → Prop
decls.doc: Whether the doubling edge out of the ladder state `j` is present.

decls.statement: instance : ∀ (cap : Option ℕ) (j : ℕ), Decidable (HasDouble cap j) | none, _ => .isTrue trivial | some K, j => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (2 * j ≤ K))

decls.name: hasDouble_none
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hasDouble_none (j : ℕ) : HasDouble none j

decls.name: hasDouble_some
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hasDouble_some (K j : ℕ) : HasDouble (some K) j ↔ 2 * j ≤ K

decls.name: hasDouble_mono
decls.statement: theorem hasDouble_mono {cap : Option ℕ} {m j : ℕ} (h : HasDouble cap m) (hj : j ≤ m) : HasDouble cap j
decls.doc: The doubling edge survives downward: if it is present at `m` it is present at every `j ≤ m`.

decls.name: OnChain
decls.statement: def OnChain : Option ℕ → St → Prop
decls.doc: The states of the chain in play.

decls.statement: instance : ∀ (cap : Option ℕ) (x : St), Decidable (OnChain cap x) | none, _ => .isTrue trivial | some K, .lad j => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (j ≤ K)) | some _, .sink => .isTrue trivial

decls.name: onChain_none
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem onChain_none (x : St) : OnChain none x

decls.name: onChain_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem onChain_sink (cap : Option ℕ) : OnChain cap .sink

decls.name: onChain_some_lad
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem onChain_some_lad (K j : ℕ) : OnChain (some K) (.lad j) ↔ j ≤ K

decls.name: onChain_double
decls.statement: theorem onChain_double {cap : Option ℕ} {j : ℕ} (h : HasDouble cap j) : OnChain cap (.lad (2 * j))
decls.doc: Where a surviving doubling edge lands is on the chain: on the truncation that is exactly the content of `HasDouble`, `2j ≤ K`.

decls.name: onChain_lad_of_hasDouble
decls.statement: theorem onChain_lad_of_hasDouble {cap : Option ℕ} {m j : ℕ} (h : HasDouble cap m) (hj : j ≤ m) : OnChain cap (.lad j)
decls.doc: A ladder state at or below a state carrying its doubling edge is on the chain.

decls.name: window
decls.statement: def window (m : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
decls.doc: The cut window `W(m) = {⌈m/2⌉, …, m−1}` of `eq:doubling_window`.

decls.name: mem_window
decls.statement: theorem mem_window {m j : ℕ} : j ∈ window m ↔ (m + 1) / 2 ≤ j ∧ j < m

decls.name: window_lt
decls.statement: theorem window_lt {m j : ℕ} (h : j ∈ window m) : j < m

decls.name: Setting
decls.statement: structure Setting
decls.doc: The standing hypotheses of `def:doubling_setting`, minus the family.

decls.name: jbar
decls.statement: noncomputable def jbar : ℝ
decls.doc: `j̄`, the mean of the target row (`def:doubling_setting`).

decls.name: epsMax_pos
decls.statement: theorem epsMax_pos : 0 < S.epsMax

decls.name: eps_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem eps_lt_one ⦃j : ℕ⦄ (hj : 1 ≤ j) : S.eps j < 1

decls.name: one_sub_eps_pos
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_eps_pos ⦃j : ℕ⦄ (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 < 1 - S.eps j

decls.name: pstar
decls.statement: noncomputable def pstar (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (f : St → ℝ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: The function action `(P⋆ f)(x) = E(f(X₁) | X₀ = x)` of the backward kernel, in closed form.

decls.name: pstar_src
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem pstar_src : pstar S cap f .src = f .sink

decls.name: pstar_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem pstar_sink : pstar S cap f .sink = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d, S.row k * f (.lad k)

decls.name: pstar_lad_succ
decls.statement: theorem pstar_lad_succ (j : ℕ) : pstar S cap f (.lad (j + 1)) = if HasDouble cap (j + 1) then S.eps (j + 1) * f (.lad (2 * (j + 1))) + (1 - S.eps (j + 1)) * f (.lad j) else f (.lad j)

decls.name: pstar_lad_of_hasDouble
decls.statement: theorem pstar_lad_of_hasDouble {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) (h : HasDouble cap j) : pstar S cap f (.lad j) = S.eps j * f (.lad (2 * j)) + (1 - S.eps j) * f (.lad (j - 1))
decls.doc: The doubling case of `pstar`, stated at a ladder index `j ≥ 1` rather than at `j + 1`.

decls.name: pstar_lad_of_not_hasDouble
decls.statement: theorem pstar_lad_of_not_hasDouble {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) (h : ¬ HasDouble cap j) : pstar S cap f (.lad j) = f (.lad (j - 1))
decls.doc: The truncated case of `pstar`: with the doubling edge deleted, the decrement carries `1`.

decls.name: pstar_add
decls.statement: theorem pstar_add : pstar S cap (f + g) = pstar S cap f + pstar S cap g

decls.name: pstar_smul
decls.statement: theorem pstar_smul (c : ℝ) : pstar S cap (c • f) = c • pstar S cap f

decls.name: pstar_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem pstar_nonneg (hf : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (x : St) : 0 ≤ pstar S cap f x
decls.doc: `P⋆` preserves non-negativity: it is an average over the one-step law.

decls.name: pstar_bounded
decls.statement: theorem pstar_bounded {C : ℝ} (hC : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) (x : St) : |pstar S cap f x| ≤ C
decls.doc: `P⋆` is a contraction of the sup norm: it is an average, so it cannot enlarge the range.

decls.name: pstar_const
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem pstar_const (c : ℝ) : pstar S cap (fun _ => c) = fun _ => c
decls.doc: `P⋆` fixes the constants: the rows are probabilities.

decls.name: Stat
decls.statement: structure Stat (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ)
decls.doc: An invariant probability of the chain in play — `λ` of `def:doubling_setting`.

decls.name: summable_mul
decls.statement: theorem summable_mul {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : Summable (fun x => L.lam x * f x)
decls.doc: `λ · f` is summable whenever `f` is bounded — the workhorse behind every `tsum` manipulation in the norm estimates.

decls.name: tsum_sub_pstar
decls.statement: theorem tsum_sub_pstar {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : ∑' x, L.lam x * (f x - pstar S cap f x) = 0
decls.doc: The invariance identity, rearranged: the `λ`-integral of the flow-matching defect `(Id − P⋆)f` vanishes for every bounded `f`.

files.title: `theo:doubling_sharp`: the rescaled profile converges, and its limit is determined
variables: variable {d L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ c₃ : ℝ}

decls.name: cutBal_unique
decls.statement: theorem cutBal_unique {d : ℕ} {lam lam' : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (h' : D.CutBal d lam' ⊤) (hagree : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → lam j = lam' j) : ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → lam m = lam' m
decls.doc: **Fifth bullet of the proof of `theo:doubling_sharp`.** Two sequences satisfying `eq:doubling_cut` at every `m > d` and agreeing on `λ_1,…,λ_d` agree everywhere; so `c`, `d` and the boundary data determine the whole sequence, and with it the limit `C`.

decls.name: descP_diff_eq
decls.statement: theorem descP_diff_eq {ℓ : ℕ} (u : ℕ → ℝ) {y y' : ℕ} (hy : ℓ ≤ y) (hy' : ℓ ≤ y') : D.descP ℓ u y - D.descP ℓ u y' = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ), u k * (D.exitLaw ℓ y k - D.exitLaw ℓ y' k)
decls.doc: The difference of two descent averages, as one sum against the difference of the exit laws.

decls.name: descP_uu_diff_le
decls.statement: theorem descP_uu_diff_le (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 20 ≤ ℓ) (hℓτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (ℓ : ℝ)) (i : ℕ) {m m' : ℕ} (hm : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m) (hm' : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m') : |D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) m - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) m'| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i
decls.doc: **The coupling step.** Two descent averages of the profile, started above `2^iℓ`, differ by at most `c₂(1−ω)^i`.

decls.name: uu_sub_descP_le
decls.statement: theorem uu_sub_descP_le (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hLd : d < 2 * L) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hc₂ : 0 ≤ c₂) (hweight : ∀ ℓ y : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : L ≤ ℓ) (y : ℕ) : |D.uu lam y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ
decls.doc: **The weight step.** The profile differs from its own descent average by at most `c₂c₃/ℓ`.

decls.name: uu_diff_le
decls.statement: theorem uu_diff_le (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hLd : d < 2 * L) (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hLτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hweight : ∀ ℓ y : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : L ≤ ℓ) (i : ℕ) {m m' : ℕ} (hm : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m) (hm' : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m') : |D.uu lam m - D.uu lam m'| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)
decls.doc: **The two bullets of the proof of `theo:doubling_sharp`, merged.** At every level `ℓ ≥ L` and every `i`, two indices above `2^iℓ` have profiles differing by at most `c₂(1−ω)^i + 2c₂c₃/ℓ` — the paper's `3c₂c₃/ℓ`, improved to `2`.

decls.name: sharp_limit
decls.statement: theorem sharp_limit (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hLd : d < 2 * L) (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hLτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hweight : ∀ ℓ y : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ) : ∃ C : ℝ, Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => D.uu lam m) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧ c₁ ≤ C ∧ C ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ ℓ i m : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sharp`.** The rescaled profile `u_m = λ_m m^{p_*}` converges; its limit lies in `[c₁,c₂]`; and the convergence carries the explicit error `c₂(1−ω)^i + 2c₂c₃/ℓ` at every level `ℓ ≥ L` and every `i` with `2^iℓ ≤ m`.

files.title: `theo:doubling_sharp`, unconditional

decls.name: uu_bounded_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem uu_bounded_of_cutBal {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hpos : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) (hℓ : D.m0 d ≤ ℓ) : ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_decay`(2) in the `u` variable, unconditional.** The same preamble as `Product.decay_two_sided_of_cutBal`, stopped one step earlier: it is the rescaled profile, not the sequence, that `Sharp.lean` takes bounds on.

decls.name: sharp_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem sharp_of_cutBal {d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hpos : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) : ∃ C c₁ c₂ c₆ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ C ∧ C ≤ c₂ ∧ 0 < c₆ ∧ (∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) ∧ Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p - C| ≤ c₆ * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_sharp`, with no hypothesis beyond the cut balance and positivity.** `eq:doubling_sharp` is the convergence, `eq:doubling_rate` the bound with `ϑ = Decay.vartheta`, and `c₁ ≤ C ≤ c₂` records the limit inside the decay window that `theo:doubling_decay`(2) produces.

decls.name: levelL
decls.statement: noncomputable def levelL (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) : ℕ
decls.doc: **The level of the sharp block**, `L = max(ℓ₃, 20, d+1, m₀(d), ⌈32cτ⌉)`: past it every hypothesis of `Sharp.sharp_limit` and `Decay.weight_bound` holds.

decls.name: c6
decls.statement: noncomputable def c6 (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) (c₂ : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`c₆` of `eq:doubling_rate`, written out**: `c₂(4^α + 2c₃) + c₂ m₃^ϑ` with `m₃ = max(1, ⌈L^{1/ϑ}⌉)`, `L = levelL d` and `c₂` the upper decay constant.

decls.name: sharp_explicit
decls.statement: theorem sharp_explicit {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hℓ : D.m0 d ≤ ℓ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) : ∃ C : ℝ, a * Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))) ≤ C ∧ C ≤ b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ)) ∧ Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p - C| ≤ D.c6 d (b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))) * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_sharp` with every constant written out.** If the rescaled profile lies in `[a, b]` on the initial block `1 ≤ j < 2ℓ`, `ℓ ≥ m₀`, `a > 0`, then the limit `C` lies in `[a e^{−c₅c₄/ℓ}, b e^{c₅c₄/ℓ}]`, `c₄ = 16cτ`, and `|λ_m m^{p_*} − C| ≤ c₆ m^{−ϑ}` at every `m ≥ 1` with `c₆ = c6 d (b e^{c₅c₄/ℓ})` — a formula in `c`, `d` and the initial block, which is the paper's dependence clause "`c₆` depends on `c`, `d`, `λ_1..λ_{2m₀}` alone" made precise.

files.title: `eq:doubling_rate`: the sharp asymptotic carries a polynomial rate
variables: variable {d L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ c₃ C : ℝ}

decls.name: alph
decls.statement: noncomputable def alph : ℝ
decls.doc: `α := log₂(1/(1−ω))`, the paper's exponent parameter.

decls.name: vartheta
decls.statement: noncomputable def vartheta : ℝ
decls.doc: `ϑ := α/(1+α)`, the rate exponent of `eq:doubling_rate`.

decls.name: one_sub_omeg_pos
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_omeg_pos : 0 < 1 - D.omeg

decls.name: one_sub_omeg_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_omeg_lt_one : 1 - D.omeg < 1

decls.name: alph_pos
decls.statement: theorem alph_pos : 0 < D.alph

decls.name: two_rpow_neg_alph
decls.statement: theorem two_rpow_neg_alph : (2 : ℝ) ^ (-D.alph) = 1 - D.omeg

decls.name: vartheta_pos
decls.statement: theorem vartheta_pos : 0 < D.vartheta

decls.name: vartheta_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem vartheta_lt_one : D.vartheta < 1

decls.name: alph_mul_one_sub
decls.statement: theorem alph_mul_one_sub : D.alph * (1 - D.vartheta) = D.vartheta
decls.doc: `α(1 − ϑ) = ϑ`, the identity the rate turns on.

decls.name: rate_of_large
decls.statement: theorem rate_of_large (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hc₂ : 0 < c₂) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hCbound : ∀ ℓ i m : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)) {m : ℕ} (hm1 : 1 ≤ m) (hmL : (L : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) ^ D.vartheta) : |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (4 ^ D.alph + 2 * c₃) * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **The rate at a large index.** At every `m` with `L ≤ m^ϑ`, the level `ℓ := ⌈m^ϑ⌉` and the index `i := ⌊log₂(m/ℓ)⌋` turn `Sharp.sharp_limit`'s error into `c₂(4^α + 2c₃) m^{−ϑ}`.

decls.name: sharp_rate_explicit
decls.statement: theorem sharp_rate_explicit (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hC1 : c₁ ≤ C) (hC2 : C ≤ c₂) (hCbound : ∀ ℓ i m : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)) : ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ (c₂ * (4 ^ D.alph + 2 * c₃) + c₂ * ((max 1 ⌈(L : ℝ) ^ (1 / D.vartheta)⌉₊ : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ D.vartheta) * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_rate`, with the constant written out.** With `ϑ = α/(1+α)`, `α = log₂(1/(1−ω))` and `m₃ = max(1, ⌈L^{1/ϑ}⌉)`, `|λ_m m^{p_*} − C| ≤ (c₂(4^α + 2c₃) + c₂ m₃^ϑ) m^{−ϑ}` at every `m ≥ 1`.

decls.name: sharp_rate
decls.statement: theorem sharp_rate (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hC1 : c₁ ≤ C) (hC2 : C ≤ c₂) (hCbound : ∀ ℓ i m : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)) : ∃ c₆ : ℝ, 0 < c₆ ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₆ * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_rate`.** There is `c₆ > 0` with `|λ_m m^{p_*} − C| ≤ c₆ m^{−ϑ}` at every `m ≥ 1`: the existential reading of `sharp_rate_explicit`.

decls.name: sharp
decls.statement: theorem sharp (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hLd : d < 2 * L) (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hLτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hweight : ∀ ℓ y : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ) : ∃ C c₆ : ℝ, 0 < c₆ ∧ c₁ ≤ C ∧ C ≤ c₂ ∧ Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p - C| ≤ c₆ * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_sharp`, assembled.** The rescaled profile `λ_m m^{p_*}` converges to a limit `C ∈ [c₁,c₂]` — this is `eq:doubling_sharp` — and the convergence carries the polynomial rate `eq:doubling_rate` with the paper's exponent `ϑ = α/(1+α)`, `α = log₂(1/(1−ω))`.

files.title: `lem:doubling_escape`, Step 2: the sojourn in a dyadic block

decls.name: pk
decls.statement: noncomputable def pk (z j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The transition law of `lem:doubling_descent`.** `P(Y₁ = j | Y₀ = z) = w_z(j)/R₀(z)` for `j ∈ W(z)`.

decls.name: half_le_R0
decls.statement: theorem half_le_R0 (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) : 1 / 2 ≤ D.R0 z
decls.doc: `R₀(z) ≥ ½` above the threshold: `eq:doubling_R0`, first half.

decls.name: pk_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem pk_nonneg (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) {j : ℕ} (hj : j ∈ window z) : 0 ≤ D.pk z j

decls.name: sum_pk
decls.statement: theorem sum_pk (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) : ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j = 1
decls.doc: The transition law is a probability on `W(z)`: `Σ_{j ∈ W(z)} w_z(j)/R₀(z) = 1`.

decls.name: escape_pk
decls.statement: theorem escape_pk (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) : D.gam ≤ ∑ j ∈ halveIco z, D.pk z j
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_escape` as a mass.** `Σ_{j ≤ y/√2} P(Y₁ = j | Y₀ = y) ≥ γ`.

decls.name: halveIco_subset
decls.statement: theorem halveIco_subset (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) : halveIco z ⊆ window z

decls.name: indB
decls.statement: noncomputable def indB (L z : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The indicator of the block `I = [L, 2L)`; `I_i(ℓ)` at `L = 2^i ℓ`.

decls.name: indB_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem indB_nonneg (L z : ℕ) : 0 ≤ indB L z

decls.name: indB_le_one
decls.statement: theorem indB_le_one (L z : ℕ) : indB L z ≤ 1

decls.name: indB_eq_zero
decls.statement: theorem indB_eq_zero {L z : ℕ} (h : z < L) : indB L z = 0

decls.name: halve_halve_lt
decls.statement: theorem halve_halve_lt {L z j k : ℕ} (hzthr : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) (hjthr : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (j : ℝ)) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) (hj : j ∈ halveIco z) (hk : k ∈ halveIco j) : k < L
decls.doc: **Two halvings leave the block.** If `j ≤ z/√2`, `k ≤ j/√2` and `z < 2L`, then `k < L`.

decls.name: inner_le
decls.statement: theorem inner_le {L j : ℕ} (hjthr : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (j : ℝ)) (hout : ∀ k ∈ halveIco j, k < L) : ∑ k ∈ window j, D.pk j k * indB L k ≤ 1 - D.gam
decls.doc: **One step out of the block, from an already halved state.** If every halving of `j` leaves the block, then the chance of staying in it at the next step is at most `1 − γ`.

decls.name: two_step
decls.statement: theorem two_step {L z : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hz1 : L ≤ z) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) : ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j * (indB L j * ∑ k ∈ window j, D.pk j k * indB L k) ≤ 1 - D.gam ^ 2
decls.doc: **The two-step estimate.** `P(Y₂ ∈ I | Y₀ = z) ≤ 1 − γ²` for every `z ∈ I = [L, 2L)`.

decls.name: surv
decls.statement: noncomputable def surv (D : Decay) (L : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
decls.doc: **`P(ς > r | Y₀ = z)`**, where `ς` is the exit time from `I = [L, 2L)`, as the recursion in the number of steps that characterises it: `{ς > r} = {Y₀, …, Y_r ∈ I}`.

decls.name: surv_zero
decls.statement: theorem surv_zero (L z : ℕ) : D.surv L 0 z = indB L z

decls.name: surv_succ
decls.statement: theorem surv_succ (L r z : ℕ) : D.surv L (r + 1) z = indB L z * ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j * D.surv L r j

decls.name: surv_of_out
decls.statement: theorem surv_of_out {L z : ℕ} (h : ¬ (L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L)) (r : ℕ) : D.surv L r z = 0

decls.name: surv_eq_zero_of_lt
decls.statement: theorem surv_eq_zero_of_lt {L : ℕ} : ∀ (r z : ℕ), z < L + r → D.surv L r z = 0
decls.doc: The descent falls by at least one at each step, so it cannot stay in a block of width `L` for `L` steps: `surv L r z = 0` as soon as `z < L + r`.

decls.name: surv_two_pow
decls.statement: theorem surv_two_pow {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) : ∀ (r z : ℕ), D.surv L (2 * r) z ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r * indB L z
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`, first line.** `P(ς > 2r | Y₀ = y) ≤ (1 − γ²)^r`, and — the sharper form the induction needs — the bound is carried by the block indicator.

decls.name: surv_le_pow
decls.statement: theorem surv_le_pow {L z : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hz1 : L ≤ z) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) (r : ℕ) : D.surv L (2 * r) z ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`, first line, as stated in the paper.**

decls.name: geom_sum_le_inv
