decls.statement: theorem geom_sum_le_inv {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x < 1) (n : ℕ) : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, x ^ i ≤ 1 / (1 - x)

decls.name: surv_antitone
decls.statement: theorem surv_antitone {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) : ∀ (r z : ℕ), D.surv L (r + 1) z ≤ D.surv L r z
decls.doc: `P(ς > r)` is non-increasing in `r`.

decls.name: surv_two_pow_le
decls.statement: theorem surv_two_pow_le {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (m z : ℕ) : D.surv L (2 * m) z ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ m
decls.doc: `P(ς > 2m | Y₀ = z) ≤ (1−γ²)^m` at every state, the indicator dropped.

decls.name: surv_partial_sum
decls.statement: theorem surv_partial_sum {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (z : ℕ) : ∀ R : ℕ, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * R), D.surv L n z ≤ 2 * ∑ r ∈ Finset.range R, (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r
decls.doc: Consecutive terms of the tail sum, paired: this is the paper's `ς̃ = ⌈ς/2⌉`.

decls.name: Decay.sojMean
decls.statement: noncomputable def Decay.sojMean (D : Decay) (L : ℕ) (z : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`E(ς | Y₀ = z)`**, the expected sojourn in `I = [L,2L)`, as the recursion that characterises it: leave at once outside the block, else one step plus the expectation after it.

decls.name: Decay.sojGF
decls.statement: noncomputable def Decay.sojGF (D : Decay) (L : ℕ) (zeta : ℝ) (z : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`E(ζ^ς | Y₀ = z)`**, as the recursion that characterises it.

decls.name: c5
decls.statement: noncomputable def c5 : ℝ
decls.doc: **`c₅ := 6/γ²`** of `lem:doubling_escape`.

decls.name: sojMean_of_out
decls.statement: theorem sojMean_of_out {L z : ℕ} (h : ¬ (L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L)) : D.sojMean L z = 0

decls.name: sojMean_of_in
decls.statement: theorem sojMean_of_in {L z : ℕ} (h : L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L) : D.sojMean L z = 1 + ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j * D.sojMean L j

decls.name: sojMean_eq_sum
decls.statement: theorem sojMean_eq_sum {L : ℕ} : ∀ (z N : ℕ), z < L + N → D.sojMean L z = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, D.surv L n z
decls.doc: **The tail formula.** `E(ς) = Σ_{n<N} P(ς > n)` for every `N` past the block width — proved from the two recursions, not assumed.

decls.name: sojMean_le
decls.statement: theorem sojMean_le {L z : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) : D.sojMean L z ≤ 2 / D.gam ^ 2
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`, second line.** `E(ς | Y₀ = y) ≤ 2/γ²`.

decls.name: sojGF_of_out
decls.statement: theorem sojGF_of_out {L : ℕ} {zeta : ℝ} {z : ℕ} (h : ¬ (L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L)) : D.sojGF L zeta z = 1

decls.name: sojGF_of_in
decls.statement: theorem sojGF_of_in {L : ℕ} {zeta : ℝ} {z : ℕ} (h : L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L) : D.sojGF L zeta z = zeta * ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j * D.sojGF L zeta j

decls.name: sojGF_eq_sum
decls.statement: theorem sojGF_eq_sum {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (zeta : ℝ) : ∀ (z N : ℕ), z < L + N → D.sojGF L zeta z = 1 + (zeta - 1) * ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, zeta ^ n * D.surv L n z
decls.doc: **The paper's expansion `ζ^ς = 1 + (ζ−1) Σ_{n<ς} ζⁿ`, in expectation.**

decls.name: surv_partial_zeta
decls.statement: theorem surv_partial_zeta {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (z : ℕ) {zeta : ℝ} (hz : 1 ≤ zeta) : ∀ R : ℕ, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * R), zeta ^ n * D.surv L n z ≤ (1 + zeta) * ∑ r ∈ Finset.range R, (zeta ^ 2 * (1 - D.gam ^ 2)) ^ r
decls.doc: The `ζ`-weighted tail sum, paired two by two.

decls.name: sojGF_le
decls.statement: theorem sojGF_le {L z : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) {zeta : ℝ} (h1 : 1 ≤ zeta) (h2 : zeta ≤ 1 + D.gam ^ 2 / 6) : D.sojGF L zeta z ≤ 1 + D.c5 * (zeta - 1)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`, third line.** `E(ζ^ς | Y₀ = y) ≤ 1 + c₅(ζ−1)` for `1 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 + γ²/6`, with `c₅ = 6/γ²`.

decls.name: thr_of_block
decls.statement: theorem thr_of_block {d ℓ i : ℕ} (hℓ : D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ((2 ^ i * ℓ : ℕ) : ℝ)
decls.doc: The threshold holds on `I_i(ℓ)` for `i ≥ 1` and `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂`, since `2^i ℓ ≥ 2ℓ ≥ 32cτ`.

decls.name: sojourn_block
decls.statement: theorem sojourn_block {d ℓ i : ℕ} (hℓ : D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) {y : ℕ} (hy : y ∈ block i ℓ) : (∀ r : ℕ, D.surv (2 ^ i * ℓ) (2 * r) y ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r) ∧ D.sojMean (2 ^ i * ℓ) y ≤ 2 / D.gam ^ 2 ∧ ∀ zeta : ℝ, 1 ≤ zeta → zeta ≤ 1 + D.gam ^ 2 / 6 → D.sojGF (2 ^ i * ℓ) zeta y ≤ 1 + D.c5 * (zeta - 1)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`.** All three bounds, on the paper's own block `I_i(ℓ)` at `i ≥ 1` and `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂`, for the exit time `ς` from that block.

files.title: The loop closure carries an invariant probability at `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1`

decls.name: rowTail
decls.statement: noncomputable def rowTail (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `R(m) = Σ_{k ≥ m} P̂_B(s_f → k)`, the mass the target row sends at or above `m`.

decls.name: rowTail_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem rowTail_nonneg (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : 0 ≤ rowTail S m

decls.name: rowTail_one
decls.statement: theorem rowTail_one : rowTail S 1 = 1

decls.name: rowTail_sub
decls.statement: theorem rowTail_sub (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : rowTail S m - rowTail S (m + 1) = S.row m

decls.name: rowTail_swap
decls.statement: theorem rowTail_swap (S : Setting) (N : ℕ) : ∀ (m k : ℕ), (m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ k ∈ Finset.Icc m S.d) ↔ (m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (min N k) ∧ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d)

decls.name: sum_rowTail_le
decls.statement: theorem sum_rowTail_le (N : ℕ) : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, rowTail S m ≤ S.jbar
decls.doc: The source term contributes at most the mean `j̄` of the target row, however far the cuts are summed: each `k` is counted `min(N, k) ≤ k` times.

decls.name: statSeq
decls.statement: noncomputable def statSeq (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The invariant sequence of the loop closure: the solution of the cut balance with the target row as source term, normalised by `λ(s₀) = 1`.

decls.name: statSeq_zero
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem statSeq_zero : statSeq S 0 = 1

decls.name: statSeq_eq
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_eq {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : statSeq S m = ((∑ j ∈ window m, statSeq S j * S.eps j) + rowTail S m) / (1 - S.eps m)

decls.name: statSeq_cut
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_cut {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : statSeq S m * (1 - S.eps m) = (∑ j ∈ window m, statSeq S j * S.eps j) + rowTail S m
decls.doc: **The cut balance with the row correction.** This is `eq:doubling_cut` at every `m ≥ 1`, not only at `m > d`; the extra term is the mass the target row sends at or above `m`, and it is what makes the cut identity hold below `d` as well.

decls.name: statSeq_pos
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_pos (S : Setting) : ∀ m : ℕ, 0 < statSeq S m

decls.name: statSeq_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_nonneg (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : 0 ≤ statSeq S m

decls.name: statSeq_partial_sum_le
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_partial_sum_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (N : ℕ) : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, statSeq S m ≤ S.jbar / (1 - c)
decls.doc: **Summability with the paper's constant.** `Σ_{m=1}^{N} λ_m ≤ j̄/(1−c)` at every `N` — the same number as `σ̄ ≤ j̄/(1−c)` in `lem:doubling_supersolution`, obtained from the cut balance alone.

decls.name: summable_statSeq
decls.statement: theorem summable_statSeq {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) : Summable (statSeq S)

decls.name: window_succ_sum
decls.statement: theorem window_succ_sum {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (F : ℕ → ℝ) : (∑ j ∈ window (k + 1), F j) + (if 2 ∣ k then F (k / 2) else 0) = (∑ j ∈ window k, F j) + F k
decls.doc: The window moves by one: passing from the cut at `k` to the cut at `k+1` adds the state `k` and, when `k` is even, drops the state `k/2`.

decls.name: statSeq_point
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_point (S : Setting) (k : ℕ) : statSeq S k = statSeq S (k + 1) * (1 - S.eps (k + 1)) + (if 1 ≤ k ∧ 2 ∣ k then statSeq S (k / 2) * S.eps (k / 2) else 0) + S.row k
decls.doc: **The pointwise invariance equation on the ladder.** Mass at `k` comes from the decrement out of `k+1`, from the doubling out of `k/2` when `k` is even and positive, and from the target row.

decls.name: statMeas
decls.statement: noncomputable def statMeas (S : Setting) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: The unnormalised invariant measure on `St`: `statSeq` along the ladder, `1` at the sink.

decls.name: statMeas_lad
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem statMeas_lad (j : ℕ) : statMeas S (.lad j) = statSeq S j

decls.name: statMeas_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem statMeas_sink : statMeas S .sink = 1

decls.name: statMeas_pos
decls.statement: theorem statMeas_pos (S : Setting) (x : St) : 0 < statMeas S x

decls.name: exists_stat_none
decls.statement: theorem exists_stat_none {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) : Nonempty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_phase`(3), the `0 < c < 1` half, in the form this library consumes.** The loop-closed chain at `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1` carries an invariant probability, positive at every state.

decls.name: exists_stat_of_family
decls.statement: theorem exists_stat_of_family {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (S : Setting) (hS : S.eps = epsCS c 1) : Nonempty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: The same statement with `ε` given as the family `ε_{c,1}` rather than pointwise: the form `GFNBoundsScaffold.Doubling.exists_stat_of_lt_one` states.

files.title: The cut balance is summable at `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1`

decls.name: window_swap
decls.statement: theorem window_swap (N : ℕ) : ∀ (m j : ℕ), (m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ j ∈ window m) ↔ (m ∈ Finset.Icc (j + 1) (min N (2 * j)) ∧ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N)
decls.doc: `j` lies in the window of `m` with `1 ≤ m ≤ N` exactly when `j + 1 ≤ m ≤ min(N, 2j)` and `1 ≤ j ≤ N`: the index swap behind `window_double_sum`.

decls.name: window_double_sum
decls.statement: theorem window_double_sum (N : ℕ) (F : ℕ → ℝ) : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∑ j ∈ window m, F j = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ((min N (2 * j) - j : ℕ) : ℝ) * F j
decls.doc: **The double-counting step.** Each ladder index `j` is carried across a cut by exactly `min(N, 2j) − j` of the windows `W(1), …, W(N)`.

decls.name: partial_sum_le
decls.statement: theorem partial_sum_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) {lam g : ℕ → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ j, 0 ≤ lam j) (N : ℕ) (hrec : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → m ≤ N → lam m * (1 - S.eps m) ≤ ∑ j ∈ window m, lam j * S.eps j + g m) : (1 - c) * ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, lam m ≤ ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, g m
decls.doc: **The partial-sum bound.** At `s = 1`, a non-negative sequence obeying the cut balance up to an excess `g` on `{1,…,N}` has `(1 − c) Σ_{m≤N} λ_m ≤ Σ_{m≤N} g_m`.

decls.name: cutBalance_partial_sum_le
decls.statement: theorem cutBalance_partial_sum_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ j, 0 ≤ lam j) (hcb : CutBalanceSeq S lam ⊤) (N : ℕ) : (1 - c) * ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, lam m ≤ ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d, lam m
decls.doc: The instance for `CutBalanceSeq`: the excess is carried by the boundary data alone, the recursion being an equality above `d`.

decls.name: summable_of_cutBalanceSeq
decls.statement: theorem summable_of_cutBalanceSeq {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ j, 0 ≤ lam j) (hcb : CutBalanceSeq S lam ⊤) : Summable lam
decls.doc: **The conclusion.** At `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1`, every non-negative solution of the cut balance is summable, with the explicit bound `Σ_{j≥1} λ_j ≤ (Σ_{j≤d} λ_j)/(1−c)`.

files.title: The linear supersolution

decls.name: pstar_mono
decls.statement: theorem pstar_mono {f g : St → ℝ} (h : ∀ x, f x ≤ g x) (x : St) : pstar S cap f x ≤ pstar S cap g x
decls.doc: `P⋆` is monotone: it is an average over the one-step law.

decls.name: linSuper
decls.statement: noncomputable def linSuper (c : ℝ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: The linear supersolution `h(j) = j/(1−c)`, with `h(s₀) = h(s_f) = 0`.

decls.name: linSuper_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem linSuper_nonneg {c : ℝ} (hc1 : c < 1) (x : St) : 0 ≤ linSuper c x

decls.name: linSuper_lad
decls.statement: theorem linSuper_lad {c : ℝ} (j : ℕ) : linSuper c (.lad j) = (j : ℝ) / (1 - c)

decls.name: linSuper_eq
decls.statement: theorem linSuper_eq {c : ℝ} (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) : linSuper c (.lad m) = 1 + pstar S cap (linSuper c) (.lad m)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_super`, Step 1.** On the loop closure, and at every state of the truncation carrying its doubling edge, `h` solves the one-step equation exactly.

decls.name: linSuper_ge
decls.statement: theorem linSuper_ge {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hD : ¬ HasDouble cap m) : 1 + pstar S cap (linSuper c) (.lad m) ≤ linSuper c (.lad m)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_super`, Step 2.** Where the doubling edge has been truncated away, `h` is a strict supersolution: the decrement carries the whole mass and `1 ≤ 1/(1−c)`.

decls.name: hitExp
decls.statement: noncomputable def hitExp (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) : ℕ → St → ℝ
decls.doc: `E(σ ∧ n | X₀ = ·)`, defined by the recursion of Step 3: `u_0 = 0`, `u_n(s₀) = 0` and `u_{n+1}(j) = 1 + E(u_n(X₁) | X₀ = j)` at a ladder state `j ≥ 1`.

decls.name: hitExp_zero
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hitExp_zero (x : St) : hitExp S cap 0 x = 0

decls.name: hitExp_src
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hitExp_src (n : ℕ) : hitExp S cap n (.lad 0) = 0

decls.name: hitExp_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hitExp_sink (n : ℕ) : hitExp S cap n .sink = 0

decls.name: hitExp_succ_lad
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_succ_lad (n j : ℕ) : hitExp S cap (n + 1) (.lad (j + 1)) = 1 + pstar S cap (hitExp S cap n) (.lad (j + 1))

decls.name: hitExp_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_nonneg (n : ℕ) (x : St) : 0 ≤ hitExp S cap n x

decls.name: hitExp_le_linSuper
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_le_linSuper {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (n : ℕ) (x : St) : hitExp S cap n x ≤ linSuper c x
decls.doc: **Step 3.** A non-negative supersolution dominates the truncated hitting expectations.

decls.name: hitExp_mono
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_mono {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) (x : St) : hitExp S cap n x ≤ hitExp S cap m x
decls.doc: The truncated hitting expectations increase in `n` — `σ ∧ n ↑ σ`.

decls.name: hitExp_iSup_le
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_iSup_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (x : St) : ⨆ n, hitExp S cap n x ≤ linSuper c x
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_supersolution`, the conclusion.** `E(σ | X₀ = j) ≤ j/(1−c) < +∞` on both chains: the supremum of the truncated hitting expectations is bounded by the supersolution.

decls.name: sigmaBar_le
decls.statement: theorem sigmaBar_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (n : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d, S.row k * hitExp S cap n (.lad k) ≤ S.jbar / (1 - c)
decls.doc: **`σ̄ ≤ j̄/(1−c)`.** Averaging the bound over the target row, whose mean is `j̄`.

files.title: The tail of the invariant measure

decls.name: rpow_ge_tangent
decls.statement: theorem rpow_ge_tangent {q u : ℝ} (hq : q ≤ 0) (hu : 0 < u) : 1 + q * (u - 1) ≤ u ^ q
decls.doc: The tangent-line inequality for a non-positive exponent: `u^q ≥ 1 + q(u−1)`.

decls.name: incr_le
decls.statement: theorem incr_le {t : ℝ} (hp : 1 < p) (ht : 0 < t) : t ^ (1 - p) - (t + 1) ^ (1 - p) ≤ (p - 1) * t ^ (-p)
decls.doc: **The upper increment.** `j^{1−p} − (j+1)^{1−p} ≤ (p−1) j^{−p}` for `j ≥ 1`, `p > 1`.

decls.name: summable_rpow_neg
decls.statement: theorem summable_rpow_neg (hp : 1 < p) : Summable fun j : ℕ => (j : ℝ) ^ (-p)
decls.doc: `j ↦ j^{−p}` is summable for `p > 1`.

decls.name: powerTail
decls.statement: noncomputable def powerTail (p : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `Σ_{j ≥ m} j^{−p}`, the tail of the pure power.

decls.name: hasSum_powerTail
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_powerTail (hp : 1 < p) (m : ℕ) : HasSum (fun k : ℕ => ((k + m : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-p)) (powerTail p m)

decls.name: powerTail_succ
decls.statement: theorem powerTail_succ (hp : 1 < p) (m : ℕ) : powerTail p m = (m : ℝ) ^ (-p) + powerTail p (m + 1)

decls.name: tendsto_shift_rpow
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_shift_rpow (hp : 1 < p) (m : ℕ) : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((n + m : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (1 - p)) atTop (𝓝 0)
decls.doc: The vanishing of the telescoped remainder: `(m+n)^{1−p} → 0`.

decls.name: powerTail_ge
decls.statement: theorem powerTail_ge (hp : 1 < p) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : (m : ℝ) ^ (1 - p) / (p - 1) ≤ powerTail p m
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_powertail`, lower half.** `m^{1−p}/(p−1) ≤ Σ_{j≥m} j^{−p}`.

decls.name: powerTail_le
decls.statement: theorem powerTail_le (hp : 1 < p) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : powerTail p m ≤ (m : ℝ) ^ (-p) + (m : ℝ) ^ (1 - p) / (p - 1)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_powertail`, upper half.** `Σ_{j≥m} j^{−p} ≤ m^{−p} + m^{1−p}/(p−1)`.

decls.name: tailSeq
decls.statement: noncomputable def tailSeq (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `L(m) = Σ_{j ≥ m} λ_j`, the tail of the sequence.

decls.name: tail_bounds
decls.statement: theorem tail_bounds {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : c₁ * ((m : ℝ) ^ (1 - D.p) / (D.p - 1)) ≤ tailSeq lam m ∧ tailSeq lam m ≤ c₂ * ((m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) + (m : ℝ) ^ (1 - D.p) / (D.p - 1))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tailratio`, both pairs.** With `c₁ j^{−p} ≤ λ_j ≤ c₂ j^{−p}` on `j ≥ 1`, the tail and the ratio of the tail to the mass at the cut are pinned to a power and to `m`.

decls.name: tail_ratio_ge
decls.statement: theorem tail_ratio_ge {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : c₁ * (m : ℝ) * lam m ≤ c₂ * (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tailratio`, second pair, lower half.** `c₁ m λ_m ≤ c₂(p−1) L(m)`, the denominator-free form of `L(m)/λ_m ≥ c₁ m/(c₂(p−1))`.

decls.name: tail_ratio_le
decls.statement: theorem tail_ratio_le {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : c₁ * (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m ≤ c₂ * D.p * (m : ℝ) * lam m
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tailratio`, second pair, upper half.** `c₁(p−1) L(m) ≤ c₂ p m λ_m`, the denominator-free form of `L(m)/λ_m ≤ c₂ p m/(c₁(p−1))`: the tail bound `tail_bounds` divided by `λ_m ≥ c₁ m^{−p}`, with `(p−1) + m ≤ p m` for `m ≥ 1`.

decls.name: tendsto_tailSeq_zero
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_tailSeq_zero {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) : Tendsto (tailSeq lam) atTop (𝓝 0)
decls.doc: **`cor:doubling_tail`, "in particular `L(m) → 0`"**, for the sequence: squeezed between `0` and `c₂(m^{−p} + m^{1−p}/(p−1)) → 0`.

decls.name: tendsto_tail_ratio_atTop
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_tail_ratio_atTop {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => tailSeq lam m / lam m) atTop atTop
decls.doc: **`cor:doubling_tail`, "in particular `L(m)/λ_m → +∞`"**, for the sequence: the ratio dominates `c₁ m/(c₂(p−1))` (`tail_ratio_ge`).

decls.name: tail_sharp
decls.statement: theorem tail_sharp {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {C t : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) {m₀ m : ℕ} (hm : m₀ ≤ m) (hm1 : 1 ≤ m) (hclose : ∀ j : ℕ, m₀ ≤ j → |lam j * (j : ℝ) ^ D.p - C| ≤ t) : |(D.p - 1) * (m : ℝ) ^ (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m - C| ≤ t * (1 + (D.p - 1) / (m : ℝ)) + |C| * ((D.p - 1) / (m : ℝ))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tail_sharp`, first line, in explicit form.** If the rescaled profile is within `t` of `C` past `m₀`, then `(p_*−1) m^{p_*−1} L(m)` is within `t(1 + (p_*−1)/m) + |C|(p_*−1)/m` of `C` at every `m ≥ m₀`.

decls.name: tendsto_tail_sharp
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_tail_sharp {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {C : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hlim : Tendsto (fun j : ℕ => lam j * (j : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C)) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (D.p - 1) * (m : ℝ) ^ (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m) atTop (𝓝 C)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tail_sharp`, first line, as a limit.** If the rescaled profile `λ_j j^{p_*}` converges to `C`, then `(p_*−1) m^{p_*−1} L(m) → C`, i.e.

decls.name: tendsto_tail_ratio_sharp
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_tail_ratio_sharp {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {C : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hC : 0 < C) (hpos : ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → 0 < lam m) (hlim : Tendsto (fun j : ℕ => lam j * (j : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C)) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m / ((m : ℝ) * lam m)) atTop (𝓝 1)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tail_sharp`, second line.** If `λ_j j^{p_*} → C > 0` then `(p_*−1) L(m)/(m λ_m) → 1`, i.e.

files.title: Total variation as a finite sum, and the Doeblin contraction

decls.name: tvOn
decls.statement: noncomputable def tvOn (F : Finset ℕ) (μ ν : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **Total variation, ½-convention.** `tvOn F μ ν = ½ ∑_{k ∈ F} |μ k − ν k|`.

decls.name: tvOn_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_nonneg (F : Finset ℕ) (μ ν : ℕ → ℝ) : 0 ≤ tvOn F μ ν

decls.name: tvOn_self
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_self (F : Finset ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℝ) : tvOn F μ μ = 0

decls.name: tvOn_comm
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_comm (F : Finset ℕ) (μ ν : ℕ → ℝ) : tvOn F μ ν = tvOn F ν μ

decls.name: sum_abs_eq
decls.statement: theorem sum_abs_eq (F : Finset ℕ) (μ ν : ℕ → ℝ) : ∑ k ∈ F, |μ k - ν k| = 2 * tvOn F μ ν
decls.doc: The sum form: `∑_{k ∈ F} |μ k − ν k| = 2 · tvOn F μ ν`, the ½-convention read backwards.

decls.name: tvOn_le_one
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_le_one {F : Finset ℕ} {μ ν : ℕ → ℝ} (hμ : ∀ k ∈ F, 0 ≤ μ k) (hν : ∀ k ∈ F, 0 ≤ ν k) (hμs : ∑ k ∈ F, μ k = 1) (hνs : ∑ k ∈ F, ν k = 1) : tvOn F μ ν ≤ 1
decls.doc: Two probabilities carried by `F` are at total variation at most `1`.

decls.name: abs_sum_sub_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_sum_sub_le {F : Finset ℕ} {π π' f : ℕ → ℝ} {lo hi : ℝ} (hF : F.Nonempty) (hf : ∀ k ∈ F, lo ≤ f k ∧ f k ≤ hi) (hmass : ∑ k ∈ F, π k = ∑ k ∈ F, π' k) : |∑ k ∈ F, f k * (π k - π' k)| ≤ (hi - lo) * tvOn F π π'
decls.doc: **The displayed inequality of `theo:doubling_sharp`, first bullet.** `|∫ f d(π − π')| ≤ (sup f − inf f) · TV(π ‖ π')`, for `f` ranged between `lo` and `hi` on `F` and `π, π'` of equal mass.

decls.name: mix
decls.statement: noncomputable def mix (G : Finset ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (P : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ
decls.doc: The mixture `∑_{z ∈ G} μ(z) π_z`, as a function on the states.

decls.name: mix_apply
decls.statement: theorem mix_apply (G : Finset ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (P : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : mix G μ P k = ∑ z ∈ G, μ z * P z k

decls.name: tvOn_mix_le
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_mix_le {F G : Finset ℕ} {μ μ' ν : ℕ → ℝ} {P : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ} {ω B : ℝ} (hω1 : ω < 1) (hν : ∀ z ∈ G, ν z ≤ μ z) (hν' : ∀ z ∈ G, ν z ≤ μ' z) (hνsum : ∑ z ∈ G, ν z = ω) (hμsum : ∑ z ∈ G, μ z = 1) (hμ'sum : ∑ z ∈ G, μ' z = 1) (hB : ∀ z ∈ G, ∀ z' ∈ G, tvOn F (P z) (P z') ≤ B) : tvOn F (mix G μ P) (mix G μ' P) ≤ (1 - ω) * B
decls.doc: **The Doeblin contraction.** Two probabilities on a finite `G` that both dominate one non-negative `ν` of mass `ω < 1` mix a family of laws to within `(1 − ω)` times the family's own diameter in total variation.

decls.name: geom_iterate
decls.statement: theorem geom_iterate {Δ : ℕ → ℝ} {ω : ℝ} (hω1 : ω < 1) (h0 : Δ 0 ≤ 1) (hstep : ∀ i, Δ (i + 1) ≤ (1 - ω) * Δ i) : ∀ i, Δ i ≤ (1 - ω) ^ i
decls.doc: The geometric iteration of `lem:doubling_coupling`, as pure arithmetic: a family of diameters that contracts by `(1 − ω)` at each step and starts at most `1` is at most `(1 − ω)^i`.

files.title: The truncation, and a proved `√K`

decls.name: percut_K
decls.statement: theorem percut_K {B : ℝ} {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble (some K) m) (hB : ∀ f : St → ℝ, (∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) → (∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) → L.mass 2 f ≤ B * L.mass 2 (fun x => f x - pstar S (some K) f x)) : L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m) ≤ 2 * L.lam (.lad m) * B
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_percut_K`, squared and cleared.** Every constant bounding the `L²(λ^K)` Rayleigh quotient is at least `L_K(m)(1−L_K(m)) / (2λ^K_m)`.

decls.name: finset_sum_le_tailMass
decls.statement: theorem finset_sum_le_tailMass {m b : ℕ} (hbK : b ≤ K) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc m b, L.lam (.lad j) ≤ L.tailMass m
decls.doc: A finite block of the ladder below the cap is part of the tail.

decls.name: tail_lower
decls.statement: theorem tail_lower (D : Decay) {Cm Cp : ℝ} (hC : 0 < Cm) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (h2mK : 2 * m ≤ K) (hlo : ∀ j : ℕ, m ≤ j → j ≤ 2 * m → Cm * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (.lad j)) (hhi : L.lam (.lad m) ≤ Cp * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) : Cm / (Cp * (2 : ℝ) ^ D.p) * (m : ℝ) * L.lam (.lad m) ≤ L.tailMass m
decls.doc: **Step 5.** `L_K(m) ≥ (Cm/(Cp 2^{p_*})) · m · λ^K_m`: the tail is `m` times the mass at the cut, up to the ratio of the two decay constants.

decls.name: hitInt_le
decls.statement: theorem hitInt_le {c : ℝ} (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (hc0 : 0 < c) (n : ℕ) : L.hitInt n ≤ (K : ℝ) / (1 - c)
decls.doc: On the truncation the supersolution is bounded by `K/(1−c)`, which is what makes the hitting integrals converge.

decls.name: sqrtK
decls.statement: theorem sqrtK (D : Decay) {c B Cm Cp : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (hC : 0 < Cm) (hKd : 4 * (S.d + 1) ≤ K) (hK8 : 8 ≤ K) (hlo : ∀ j : ℕ, K / 4 ≤ j → j ≤ 2 * (K / 4) → Cm * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (.lad j)) (hhi : L.lam (.lad (K / 4)) ≤ Cp * ((K / 4 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) (hB : ∀ f : St → ℝ, (∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) → (∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) → L.mass 2 f ≤ B * L.mass 2 (fun x => f x - pstar S (some K) f x)) : Cm / (Cp * (2 : ℝ) ^ D.p * 16 * (2 + S.jbar / (1 - c))) * (K : ℝ) ≤ B
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sqrtK`, squared.** Every constant bounding the `L²(λ^K)` Rayleigh quotient is at least `c₈² K`, with `c₈² = Cm / (Cp · 2^{p_*+4} · (2 + j̄/(1−c)))` — the paper's constant, since `Cp/Cm = c₉`.

decls.name: lam_ge_prev
decls.statement: theorem lam_ge_prev (L : Stat S (some K)) {i : ℕ} (hdi : S.d < i) (hD : HasDouble (some K) i) (hi2 : 2 ≤ i) : L.lam (.lad (i - 1)) * S.eps (i - 1) ≤ L.lam (.lad i)
decls.doc: **The step down, from the cut balance.** `λ_{i−1} ε(i−1) ≤ λ_i`: keeping only the term `y = i−1` of `eq:doubling_cut` at `i`, which is legitimate because `i−1 ∈ W(i)` for `i ≥ 2`.

decls.name: lam_chain_up
decls.statement: theorem lam_chain_up (L : Stat S (some K)) {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) (n : ℕ) : L.lam (.lad (j + n)) ≤ L.lam (.lad j) * ((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹) ^ n
decls.doc: Going up the ladder: `λ_{j+n} ≤ λ_j ρ^n` with `ρ = (1 − ε_max)^{-1}`.

decls.name: lam_chain_down
decls.statement: theorem lam_chain_down (L : Stat S (some K)) {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 ≤ η) {j : ℕ} : ∀ n : ℕ, (∀ i, j ≤ i → i < j + n → S.d < i + 1 ∧ HasDouble (some K) (i + 1) ∧ 1 ≤ i ∧ η ≤ S.eps i) → L.lam (.lad j) * η ^ n ≤ L.lam (.lad (j + n))
decls.doc: Going up the ladder from below: `λ_j η^n ≤ λ_{j+n}` when `η` is a lower bound for `ε` on the range crossed.

decls.name: block_ratio
decls.statement: theorem block_ratio (D : Decay) (L : Stat S (some K)) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = D.eps j) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓd : S.d < ℓ) (hℓ1 : 1 ≤ ℓ) (h4ℓK : 4 * ℓ ≤ K) {j j' : ℕ} (hj : ℓ ≤ j) (hj2 : j < 2 * ℓ) (hj' : ℓ ≤ j') (hj'2 : j' < 2 * ℓ) : L.lam (.lad j') ≤ (((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹) ^ ℓ + ((D.c / (2 * (ℓ : ℝ) + 1)) ^ ℓ)⁻¹) * L.lam (.lad j)
decls.doc: **The block ratio, free of `K`.** On `[ℓ, 2ℓ)` any two masses differ by at most `Q = ρ^ℓ + (η^ℓ)^{-1}`, with `ρ = (1−ε_max)^{-1}` and `η = c/(2ℓ+1)` — constants of `c` and `ℓ` alone.

decls.name: cutBalanceSeq_trunc
decls.statement: theorem cutBalanceSeq_trunc (L : Stat S (some K)) : CutBalanceSeq S (fun j => L.lam (.lad j)) ((K / 2 : ℕ) : ℕ∞)
decls.doc: The truncation's masses satisfy `eq:doubling_cut` up to `K/2`.

decls.name: decayK
decls.statement: theorem decayK (D : Decay) (L : Stat S (some K)) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = D.eps j) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓd : S.d < ℓ) (hℓ1 : 1 ≤ ℓ) (h4ℓK : 4 * ℓ ≤ K) {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ} (hZ1 : 0 < Z₁) (hZ2 : 0 < Z₂) (hZlo : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) (hZhi : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) : ∃ Cm Cp : ℝ, 0 < Cm ∧ Cp ≤ Z₂ / Z₁ * (2 : ℝ) ^ D.p * (((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹) ^ ℓ + ((D.c / (2 * (ℓ : ℝ) + 1)) ^ ℓ)⁻¹) ^ 2 * Cm ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, ℓ ≤ m → m ≤ K / 2 → Cm * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (.lad m) ∧ L.lam (.lad m) ≤ Cp * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_decayK`.** Two constants sandwiching `λ^K` on `[ℓ, K/2]`, with a ratio `C⁺/C⁻ ≤ (Z₂/Z₁) 2^{p_*} Q²` **free of `K`** — which is the `c₉` of the paper, since `Q` depends on `c` and `ℓ` alone and `Z₁, Z₂` on `c` and `d` alone.

files.title: The truncation carries a unique invariant probability

decls.name: chainFinset
decls.statement: def chainFinset (K : ℕ) : Finset St
decls.doc: The `K + 2` states `{s₀, 1, …, K, s_f}` of the truncation, as a `Finset`.

decls.name: mem_chainFinset
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem mem_chainFinset {x : St} : x ∈ chainFinset K ↔ OnChain (some K) x

decls.name: sink_mem_chainFinset
decls.statement: theorem sink_mem_chainFinset : (St.sink : St) ∈ chainFinset K

decls.name: chainFinset_nonempty
decls.statement: theorem chainFinset_nonempty : (chainFinset K).Nonempty

decls.name: pstar_congr_trunc
decls.statement: theorem pstar_congr_trunc (hdK : S.d ≤ K) {f g : St → ℝ} (h : ∀ z, OnChain (some K) z → f z = g z) {x : St} (hx : OnChain (some K) x) : pstar S (some K) f x = pstar S (some K) g x
decls.doc: The chain set is closed: `P⋆` at an on-chain state reads `f` only at on-chain states.

decls.name: pstar_finsetSum
decls.statement: theorem pstar_finsetSum {ι : Type*} {cap : Option ℕ} (s : Finset ι) (F : ι → St → ℝ) (x : St) : pstar S cap (fun z => ∑ i ∈ s, F i z) x = ∑ i ∈ s, pstar S cap (F i) x
decls.doc: `P⋆` commutes with a finite sum of functions.

decls.name: kern
decls.statement: noncomputable def kern (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (x y : St) : ℝ
decls.doc: The one-step transition probability `x → y`, *defined* as `P⋆` applied to the point mass at `y`.

decls.name: kern_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem kern_nonneg {cap : Option ℕ} (x y : St) : 0 ≤ kern S cap x y

decls.name: sum_kern
decls.statement: theorem sum_kern (hdK : S.d ≤ K) {x : St} (hx : OnChain (some K) x) : ∑ y ∈ chainFinset K, kern S (some K) x y = 1
decls.doc: The rows of the truncation sum to `1` over the chain set.

decls.name: pstar_eq_sum_kern
decls.statement: theorem pstar_eq_sum_kern (hdK : S.d ≤ K) (f : St → ℝ) {x : St} (hx : OnChain (some K) x) : pstar S (some K) f x = ∑ y ∈ chainFinset K, kern S (some K) x y * f y
decls.doc: **The representation.** At an on-chain state, `P⋆` is the finite matrix product.

decls.name: CVec
decls.statement: abbrev CVec (K : ℕ) : Type
decls.doc: Measures on the truncated chain: a finite-dimensional real vector space.

decls.name: densMap
decls.statement: noncomputable def densMap (S : Setting) (K : ℕ) : CVec K →ₗ[ℝ] CVec K
decls.doc: The **density** action `l ↦ lP` on the truncated chain, the transpose of `P⋆`.

decls.name: densMap_apply
decls.statement: theorem densMap_apply (l : CVec K) (y : ↥(chainFinset K)) : densMap S K l y = ∑ x : ↥(chainFinset K), l x * kern S (some K) (x : St) (y : St)

decls.name: sum_densMap
decls.statement: theorem sum_densMap (hdK : S.d ≤ K) (l : CVec K) : ∑ y : ↥(chainFinset K), densMap S K l y = ∑ x : ↥(chainFinset K), l x
decls.doc: The density action preserves total mass.

decls.name: exists_fixed
decls.statement: theorem exists_fixed (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : ∃ l : CVec K, l ≠ 0 ∧ densMap S K l = l
decls.doc: `Id − P` is not injective on the finite-dimensional space of measures: its range lies in the mass-zero hyperplane.

decls.name: exists_stationary
decls.statement: theorem exists_stationary (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : ∃ l : CVec K, (∀ y, 0 ≤ l y) ∧ (∑ y : ↥(chainFinset K), l y) = 1 ∧ densMap S K l = l
decls.doc: **The non-negative fixed vector.** `|l|` is a supersolution with the same total mass, hence a solution; normalizing gives a probability.

decls.name: extendCVec
decls.statement: noncomputable def extendCVec (K : ℕ) (l : CVec K) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: A measure on the chain set, read as a function on `St` vanishing off the chain.

decls.name: extendCVec_of_mem
decls.statement: theorem extendCVec_of_mem {l : CVec K} {x : St} (h : x ∈ chainFinset K) : extendCVec K l x = l ⟨x, h⟩

decls.name: extendCVec_of_not_mem
decls.statement: theorem extendCVec_of_not_mem {l : CVec K} {x : St} (h : x ∉ chainFinset K) : extendCVec K l x = 0

decls.name: sum_extendCVec
decls.statement: theorem sum_extendCVec (l : CVec K) (f : St → ℝ) : ∑ x ∈ chainFinset K, extendCVec K l x * f x = ∑ x : ↥(chainFinset K), l x * f (x : St)

decls.name: exists_preStat
decls.statement: theorem exists_preStat (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : Nonempty (PreStat S (some K))
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible`, Step 4 (existence).** The truncation at an even cap `K ≥ d` carries an invariant probability.

decls.name: exists_stat
decls.statement: theorem exists_stat (hK : Even K) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : Nonempty (Stat S (some K))
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible`, Step 4.** At an even cap `K ≥ d` the truncation carries an invariant probability, positive at every state of the chain.

decls.name: truncStat
decls.statement: noncomputable def truncStat (S : Setting) {K : ℕ} (hK : Even K) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : Stat S (some K)
decls.doc: The invariant probability `λ^K` of the truncation at an even cap `K ≥ d`.

decls.name: Stat.toPreStat
decls.statement: def Stat.toPreStat {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap) : PreStat S cap
decls.doc: Every `Stat` is a `PreStat`; positivity is the only extra field.

decls.name: Stat.hasSum_kern_flux
decls.statement: theorem Stat.hasSum_kern_flux {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap) (y : St) : HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * kern S cap x y) (L.lam y)
decls.doc: Total one-step flux into `y` is `λ(y)`.

decls.name: stat_unique
decls.statement: theorem stat_unique (hK : Even K) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) (L L' : Stat S (some K)) : L.lam = L'.lam
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible`, Step 4 (uniqueness).** At an even cap `K ≥ d` the truncation carries at most one invariant probability.

files.title: The diffusion operator is unbounded

decls.name: hasSum_tailShift
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_tailShift (m : ℕ) : HasSum (fun k : ℕ => L.lam (.lad (k + m))) (L.tailMass m)
decls.doc: The tail mass is the tail of a summable series over the ladder.

decls.name: summable_lad
decls.statement: theorem summable_lad : Summable (fun j : ℕ => L.lam (.lad j))

decls.name: tailMass_succ
decls.statement: theorem tailMass_succ (m : ℕ) : L.tailMass m = L.lam (.lad m) + L.tailMass (m + 1)
decls.doc: `λ_m = L(m) − L(m+1)`: the cut carries exactly the difference of two tails.

decls.name: tailMass_tendsto_zero
decls.statement: theorem tailMass_tendsto_zero : Tendsto L.tailMass atTop (𝓝 0)
decls.doc: The tail vanishes: `L(m) → 0`.

decls.name: tailMass_pos
decls.statement: theorem tailMass_pos (m : ℕ) : 0 < L.tailMass m

decls.name: coTail_pos
decls.statement: theorem coTail_pos {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 < m) : 0 < 1 - L.tailMass m
decls.doc: `1 − L(m) ≥ λ_1 > 0` for `m > 1`: the state `1` is outside the tail.

decls.name: GrowthCond
decls.statement: def GrowthCond (S : Setting) : Prop
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_star`.** `Σ_{i<D} log(1/ε(2^i)) = o(2^D)`.

decls.name: lam_pow_two_ge
decls.statement: theorem lam_pow_two_ge (D : ℕ) : L.lam (.lad 1) * ∏ i ∈ Finset.range D, S.eps (2 ^ i) ≤ L.lam (.lad (2 ^ D))
decls.doc: `λ_{2^D} ≥ λ_1 · ∏_{i<D} ε(2^i)`: iterate `eq:doubling_ratios` along the powers of two.

decls.name: exists_tailRatio_gt
decls.statement: theorem exists_tailRatio_gt (hstar : GrowthCond S) (Q : ℝ) (m₁ : ℕ) : ∃ m, m₁ ≤ m ∧ Q * L.lam (.lad m) < L.tailMass m
decls.doc: **Step 1 of `theo:doubling_unbounded`(2).** Under (★) the ratio `L(m)/λ_m` is unbounded above *every* cut: an exponentially decaying tail would force `Σ_{i<D} log(1/ε(2^i))` to grow like `2^D`, which (★) forbids.

decls.name: centredTail_bounded
decls.statement: theorem centredTail_bounded {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) : ∃ C, ∀ x, |L.centredTail m x| ≤ C
decls.doc: The centred tail indicator is bounded, hence a legitimate test function.

decls.name: mass_ratio_bound
decls.statement: theorem mass_ratio_bound {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hLpos : 0 < L.tailMass m) (hhalf : (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ 1 - L.tailMass m) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (hsmall : 2 * L.lam (.lad m) ≤ t * (L.tailMass m * (1 / 2) ^ p)) : L.mass p (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S cap (L.centredTail m) x) ≤ t * L.mass p (L.centredTail m)
decls.doc: The mass ratio at one cut: `mass p ((Id−P⋆)f_m) ≤ 2λ_m` against `mass p f_m ≥ L(m)·2^{-p}`.

decls.name: exists_small_mass_ratio
decls.statement: theorem exists_small_mass_ratio (hstar : GrowthCond S) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) : ∃ m, S.d < m ∧ L.mass p (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S none (L.centredTail m) x) ≤ t * L.mass p (L.centredTail m)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_inf`.** For every `t > 0` some centred tail indicator has flow-matching defect of mass at most `t` times its own mass: the infimum of the Rayleigh quotient over the mean-zero functions of unit norm is `0`.

decls.name: no_bounded_inverse
decls.statement: theorem no_bounded_inverse (hstar : GrowthCond S) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : ¬ ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ f : St → ℝ, (∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) → (∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) → L.mass p f ≤ B * L.mass p (fun x => f x - pstar S none f x)
decls.doc: **Step 3 of `theo:doubling_unbounded`(2).** No constant bounds the mass of a bounded mean-zero function by the mass of its flow-matching defect: in `L^p(λ)` terms, no bounded `S` satisfies `S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π`.

decls.name: growthCond_of_family
decls.statement: theorem growthCond_of_family {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (S : Setting) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = epsCS c s j) : GrowthCond S
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_unbounded`(1).** For `ε_{c,s}` the left side of (★) is `O(D²)`, hence `o(2^D)`: `Σ_{i<D} log(1/ε_{c,s}(2^i)) = Σ_{i<D} (s log(2^i+1) − log c)`.

decls.name: geometric_sum
decls.statement: theorem geometric_sum {a rho : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hrho : 0 < rho) (S : Setting) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = a * rho ^ j) (D : ℕ) : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range D, Real.log (1 / S.eps (2 ^ i)) = (D : ℝ) * Real.log (1 / a) + ((2 : ℝ) ^ D - 1) * Real.log (1 / rho)
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_geometric`, the identity.** For a geometrically decaying doubling probability `ε(j) = a ρ^j` the left side of (★) is `D log(1/a) + (2^D − 1) log(1/ρ)`.

decls.name: not_growthCond_geometric
decls.statement: theorem not_growthCond_geometric {a rho : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hrho : 0 < rho) (hrho1 : rho < 1) (S : Setting) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = a * rho ^ j) : ¬ GrowthCond S
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_geometric`.** (★) fails for `ε(j) = a ρ^j` with `ρ ∈ (0,1)`: the left side is of order `2^D`, not `o(2^D)`.

files.title: The diffusion operator is unbounded: the `p = 2` clauses

decls.name: no_diffusionOp
decls.statement: theorem no_diffusionOp (hstar : GrowthCond S) : ¬ ∃ Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 (rowOnChain_none S)) = 1 - L.piL2
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_unbounded`(2) at `p = 2`, the convention `B̂ = +∞`.** No bounded operator `S` on `L²(λ)` satisfies `S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π`.

decls.name: not_tendsto_partialSum
decls.statement: theorem not_tendsto_partialSum (hstar : GrowthCond S) : ¬ ∃ U : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, Tendsto (partialSum (L.pstarL2 (rowOnChain_none S)) L.piL2) atTop (𝓝 U)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_unbounded`(2) at `p = 2`: the series does not converge in operator norm.** The partial sums `Σ_{n<N}(P⋆ⁿ − Π)` have no limit in `L²(λ) →L L²(λ)`.

decls.name: not_summable_betaHat
decls.statement: theorem not_summable_betaHat (hstar : GrowthCond S) : ¬ Summable (L.betaHat (rowOnChain_none S))
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_unbounded`(2) at `p = 2`: `Σ β̂_n = +∞`.** The mixing coefficients `β̂_n = ‖Pⁿ − Π‖_{L²(λ)}` are not summable.

files.title: An `L²` pair with no exact `L²` outflow

decls.name: pstar_sub
decls.statement: theorem pstar_sub {f g : St → ℝ} : pstar S cap (f - g) = pstar S cap f - pstar S cap g

decls.name: tendsto_min_nat
decls.statement: private theorem tendsto_min_nat (a : ℝ) : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => min a (n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 a)

decls.name: tsum_pstar_eq_of_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem tsum_pstar_eq_of_nonneg {g : St → ℝ} (hg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) (hsum : Summable fun x => L.lam x * g x) : ∑' x, L.lam x * pstar S cap g x = ∑' x, L.lam x * g x
decls.doc: **Invariance against an unbounded non-negative function**, as an equality.

decls.name: tsum_pstar_eq
decls.statement: theorem tsum_pstar_eq {f : St → ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun x => L.lam x * |f x|) : ∑' x, L.lam x * pstar S cap f x = ∑' x, L.lam x * f x
decls.doc: **Invariance against a signed integrable function.** `λ` is `P⋆`-invariant against every `f` with `λ·|f|` summable: split into positive and negative parts.

decls.name: oneLp
decls.statement: noncomputable def oneLp : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu
decls.doc: The constant function `1` as an element of `L²(μ)`; `μ` is a probability.

decls.name: coeFn_oneLp
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_oneLp : ⇑L.oneLp =ᵐ[L.mu] (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))

decls.name: norm_oneLp
decls.statement: theorem norm_oneLp : ‖L.oneLp‖ = 1

decls.name: summable_lam_abs
decls.statement: theorem summable_lam_abs {f : St → ℝ} (hf : MemLp f 2 L.mu) : Summable fun x => L.lam x * |f x|
decls.doc: `λ·|f|` is summable at every `f ∈ L²(λ)`: `λ` is a probability.

decls.name: integral_eq_tsum
decls.statement: theorem integral_eq_tsum {f : St → ℝ} (hf : MemLp f 2 L.mu) : ∫ x, f x ∂L.mu = ∑' x, L.lam x * f x
decls.doc: The `μ`-integral is the `λ`-weighted sum.

decls.name: inner_oneLp
decls.statement: theorem inner_oneLp (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⟪L.oneLp, F⟫_ℝ = ∑' x, L.lam x * F x
decls.doc: **`Π`, read as an inner product.** `⟪1, F⟫ = ∫ F dλ`.

decls.name: inner_oneLp_pstarLp
decls.statement: theorem inner_oneLp_pstarLp (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⟪L.oneLp, L.pstarLp F⟫_ℝ = ⟪L.oneLp, F⟫_ℝ
decls.doc: **`P⋆` preserves the mean on `L²`.** This is `λ`-invariance, tested against a square-integrable function.

decls.name: pstarLp_oneLp
decls.statement: theorem pstarLp_oneLp (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : L.pstarLp L.oneLp = L.oneLp

decls.name: fixed_of_mem_orthogonal_range
decls.statement: theorem fixed_of_mem_orthogonal_range {Q : E →L[ℝ] E} (hQ : ‖Q‖ ≤ 1) {g : E} (hg : g ∈ (LinearMap.range (((1 : E →L[ℝ] E) - Q : E →L[ℝ] E) : E →ₗ[ℝ] E))ᗮ) : Q g = g
decls.doc: **The step `lem:doubling_fixed_points` takes from `P⋆` to `P`.** For a contraction `Q` of a Hilbert space, a vector orthogonal to the range of `Id − Q` is a fixed point of `Q` — the paper's `ker(Id − Q*) ⊆ ker(Id − Q)`, in the form that needs no adjoint.

decls.name: exists_lower_bound_of_bijective
decls.statement: theorem exists_lower_bound_of_bijective {A : E →L[ℝ] E} (hker : LinearMap.ker (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) = ⊥) (hran : LinearMap.range (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) = ⊤) : ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ f : E, ‖f‖ ≤ K * ‖A f‖
decls.doc: **The open mapping theorem, in the form the proof uses.** A bijective bounded operator of a Hilbert space is bounded below.

decls.name: defect
decls.statement: noncomputable def defect : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu
decls.doc: **`Id − P⋆`** as a bounded operator of `L²(λ)`, on the loop closure.

decls.name: defect_apply
decls.statement: theorem defect_apply (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.defect F = F - L.pstarLp F

decls.name: kerPi
decls.statement: noncomputable def kerPi : Submodule ℝ (Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
decls.doc: **`ker Π`**, the classes of `L²(λ)` of zero `λ`-mean.

decls.name: defectRange
decls.statement: noncomputable def defectRange : Submodule ℝ (Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)

decls.name: mem_kerPi_iff
decls.statement: theorem mem_kerPi_iff {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} : F ∈ L.kerPi ↔ ∑' x, L.lam x * F x = 0
decls.doc: `ker Π` is what its name says: `F` has zero mean.

decls.name: defectRange_le_kerPi
decls.statement: theorem defectRange_le_kerPi : L.defectRange ≤ L.kerPi
decls.doc: The defect of any class has zero mean: `Π(Id − P⋆) = 0`.

decls.name: eq_smul_oneLp_of_fixed
decls.statement: theorem eq_smul_oneLp_of_fixed {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} (hF : L.pstarLp F = F) : F = (F : St → ℝ) (.lad 0) • L.oneLp
decls.doc: A fixed point of `P⋆` in `L²(λ)` is a constant class: `lem:doubling_fixed_points`, `P⋆` half, transported to `Lp`.

decls.name: oneLp_mem_orthogonal
decls.statement: theorem oneLp_mem_orthogonal : L.oneLp ∈ L.defectRangeᗮ
decls.doc: `1` is orthogonal to every defect.

decls.name: orthogonal_defectRange
decls.statement: theorem orthogonal_defectRange : L.defectRangeᗮ = ℝ ∙ L.oneLp
decls.doc: **The orthogonal complement of the range of `Id − P⋆` is the line of constants.**

decls.name: topologicalClosure_defectRange
decls.statement: theorem topologicalClosure_defectRange : L.defectRange.topologicalClosure = L.kerPi
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_unsolvable`(1), the dense half.** The closure of `(Id − P⋆)L²(λ)` is `ker Π`.

decls.name: coeFn_defect
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_defect (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⇑(L.defect F) =ᵐ[L.mu] fun x => (F : St → ℝ) x - pstar S none (F : St → ℝ) x

decls.name: coeFn_defect_toLp
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_defect_toLp {f : St → ℝ} (hf : MemLp f 2 L.mu) : ⇑(L.defect (hf.toLp f)) =ᵐ[L.mu] fun x => f x - pstar S none f x

decls.name: norm_sq_eq_mass
decls.statement: theorem norm_sq_eq_mass {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} {g : St → ℝ} (h : ⇑F =ᵐ[L.mu] g) (hg : MemLp g 2 L.mu) : ‖F‖ ^ 2 = L.mass 2 g
decls.doc: The `L²` norm squared of a class is the `mass` of any of its representatives.

decls.name: tsum_lam_congr_ae
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_congr_ae {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} {g : St → ℝ} (h : ⇑F =ᵐ[L.mu] g) : ∑' x, L.lam x * (F : St → ℝ) x = ∑' x, L.lam x * g x
decls.doc: The `λ`-mean of a class is the `λ`-mean of any of its representatives.

decls.name: memLp_centredTail
decls.statement: theorem memLp_centredTail (m : ℕ) : MemLp (L.centredTail m) 2 L.mu

decls.name: exists_small_defect
decls.statement: theorem exists_small_defect (hstar : GrowthCond S) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) : ∃ F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, F ∈ L.kerPi ∧ F ≠ 0 ∧ ‖L.defect F‖ ^ 2 ≤ t * ‖F‖ ^ 2
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_inf` at `p = 2`, in `L²(λ)`.** For every `t > 0` some non-zero mean-zero class has `‖(Id − P⋆)F‖² ≤ t‖F‖²`.

decls.name: eq_zero_of_mem_kerPi_of_fixed
decls.statement: theorem eq_zero_of_mem_kerPi_of_fixed {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} (hmem : F ∈ L.kerPi) (hfix : L.pstarLp F = F) : F = 0

decls.name: sub_mean_mem_kerPi
decls.statement: theorem sub_mean_mem_kerPi (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : F - ⟪L.oneLp, F⟫_ℝ • L.oneLp ∈ L.kerPi

decls.name: defect_oneLp
decls.statement: theorem defect_oneLp : L.defect L.oneLp = 0

decls.name: defect_sub_mean
decls.statement: theorem defect_sub_mean (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.defect (F - ⟪L.oneLp, F⟫_ℝ • L.oneLp) = L.defect F

decls.name: defectRange_ne_kerPi
decls.statement: theorem defectRange_ne_kerPi (hstar : GrowthCond S) : L.defectRange ≠ L.kerPi
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_unsolvable`(1), the proper half.** `(Id − P⋆)L²(λ)` is not all of `ker Π`: were it, the open mapping theorem would bound `Id − P⋆` below on `ker Π`, against `eq:doubling_inf`.

decls.name: exists_unsolvable_pair
decls.statement: theorem exists_unsolvable_pair (hstar : GrowthCond S) : ∃ fi fe : St → ℝ, (∀ x, 0 ≤ fi x) ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ fe x) ∧ MemLp fi 2 L.mu ∧ MemLp fe 2 L.mu ∧ ∑' x, L.lam x * fi x = 1 ∧ ∑' x, L.lam x * fe x = 1 ∧ ¬ ∃ f : St → ℝ, MemLp f 2 L.mu ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂L.mu, f x - pstar S none f x = fi x - fe x
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_unsolvable`(2).** There are probability densities `f_init, f_term ∈ L²(λ)` whose difference is not a flow-matching defect: no `f ∈ L²(λ)` has `(Id − P⋆)f = f_init − f_term`.

decls.name: doubling_unsolvable
decls.statement: theorem doubling_unsolvable (L : Stat S none) (hstar : GrowthCond S) : (L.defectRange ≤ L.kerPi ∧ L.defectRange.topologicalClosure = L.kerPi ∧ L.defectRange ≠ L.kerPi) ∧ ∃ fi fe : St → ℝ, (∀ x, 0 ≤ fi x) ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ fe x) ∧ MemLp fi 2 L.mu ∧ MemLp fe 2 L.mu ∧ ∑' x, L.lam x * fi x = 1 ∧ ∑' x, L.lam x * fe x = 1 ∧ ¬ ∃ f : St → ℝ, MemLp f 2 L.mu ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂L.mu, f x - pstar S none f x = fi x - fe x
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_unsolvable`.** Under `eq:doubling_star`, on the positive recurrent loop closure: *(1)* `(Id − P⋆)L²(λ)` is a dense proper linear subspace of `ker Π`; *(2)* some pair of probability densities of `L²(λ)` has its difference outside it, so the exact `L²` flow-matching problem it poses has no solution.

files.title: `lem:doubling_weight`: the weight of a descent deviates from `1` by `O(1/ℓ)` in mean

decls.name: exp_sub_one_le_two_mul
decls.statement: theorem exp_sub_one_le_two_mul {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x ≤ 1) : Real.exp x - 1 ≤ 2 * x
decls.doc: **`e^x − 1 ≤ 2x` on `[0,1]`**, the paper's last inequality in the proof of `lem:doubling_weight`.

decls.name: weight_step
decls.statement: theorem weight_step {r beta B SW SP SQ : ℝ} (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hrnn : 0 ≤ r) (hrb : |r - 1| ≤ beta) (h1 : |SW - SP| ≤ B * (SQ - 1)) (h2 : |SP| ≤ B) (h3 : 1 ≤ SQ) : |r * SW - SP| ≤ B * ((1 + beta) * SQ - 1)
decls.doc: **The induction step of `lem:doubling_weight`, as arithmetic.** With `r` the total window weight, `β` a bound for `|r − 1|`, `SW`, `SP` the one-step averages of the two transforms and `SQ ≥ 1` the one-step average of the product transform, the step of the recursion propagates the bound `B·(SQ − 1)` to `B·((1+β)·SQ − 1)`.

decls.name: kern_eq_pk
decls.statement: theorem kern_eq_pk (z j : ℕ) : D.kern z j = D.pk z j
decls.doc: The one-step law of `DescentLaw.lean` and the one of `Sojourn.lean` are the same function.

decls.name: one_le_prodW
decls.statement: theorem one_le_prodW {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) {b : ℕ → ℝ} (hb : ∀ y : ℕ, 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ b y) (z : ℕ) : 1 ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
decls.doc: The product transform is at least `1` when its factors are: `prodW ℓ b ≥ 1` for `b ≥ 0` above `2ℓ`.

decls.name: abs_descP_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_descP_le {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) {B : ℝ} {g : ℕ → ℝ} (hg : ∀ j, |g j| ≤ B) (y : ℕ) : |D.descP ℓ g y| ≤ B
decls.doc: The normalised transform of a function bounded by `B` is bounded by `B`: it is an average.

decls.name: abs_descW_sub_descP_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_descW_sub_descP_le {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * (ℓ : ℝ)) {b : ℕ → ℝ} (hbR : ∀ y : ℕ, 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.R0 y - 1| ≤ b y) {B : ℝ} {g : ℕ → ℝ} (hg : ∀ j, |g j| ≤ B) : ∀ y : ℕ, |D.descW ℓ g y - D.descP ℓ g y| ≤ B * (D.prodW ℓ b y - 1)
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_weight`, in the form the sharp block consumes.** The unnormalised and the normalised descent transforms of a function bounded by `B` differ by at most `B·(prodW − 1)`, where `prodW` is the product transform at any `b` dominating `|R₀ − 1|` above `2ℓ`.

decls.name: ell3
decls.statement: noncomputable def ell3 (D : Decay) : ℕ
decls.doc: **`ℓ₃`, made effective.** `ℓ₃ := max(1, ⌈16cτ⌉, ⌈96cτ/γ²⌉)`: the first requirement is `32cτ ≤ 2ℓ`, under which `eq:doubling_R0` and the one-step law are available; the second is `c₄ ≤ γ²ℓ/6`, the hypothesis of `eq:doubling_product` at `H := c₄`, and simultaneously `c₅c₄/ℓ ≤ 1`, which is what `e^x − 1 ≤ 2x` needs.

decls.name: one_le_ell3
decls.statement: theorem one_le_ell3 : 1 ≤ D.ell3

decls.name: c3
decls.statement: noncomputable def c3 (D : Decay) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`c₃`, made effective.** `c₃ := 32c₅c₄/4 = 32c₅cτ = 192cτ/γ²`.

decls.name: c5_pos
decls.statement: theorem c5_pos : 0 < D.c5

decls.name: c3_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem c3_nonneg : 0 ≤ D.c3

decls.name: weight_bound
decls.statement: theorem weight_bound {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : D.ell3 ≤ ℓ) {B : ℝ} {g : ℕ → ℝ} (hg : ∀ j, |g j| ≤ B) (y : ℕ) : |D.descW ℓ g y - D.descP ℓ g y| ≤ B * D.c3 / (ℓ : ℝ)
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_weight`**, with both constants explicit: at every level `ℓ ≥ ℓ₃`, every function `g` bounded by `B` and every state `y`, `|descW ℓ g y − descP ℓ g y| ≤ B c₃/ℓ`, `c₃ = 32c₅cτ`, `ℓ₃ = max(1, ⌈16cτ⌉, ⌈96cτ/γ²⌉)`.

files.title: Sums of a power over a window, by telescoping

decls.name: incr_le'
decls.statement: theorem incr_le' {r t : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (ht : 0 < t) : t ^ (-r) - (t + 1) ^ (-r) ≤ r * t ^ (-r - 1)

decls.name: le_incr'
decls.statement: theorem le_incr' {r t : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (ht : 0 < t) : r * (t + 1) ^ (-r - 1) ≤ t ^ (-r) - (t + 1) ^ (-r)

decls.name: telescope_Ico
decls.statement: theorem telescope_Ico (f : ℕ → ℝ) {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico a b, (f j - f (j + 1)) = f a - f b
decls.doc: Telescoping over `Ico a b`.

decls.name: sum_window_ge
decls.statement: theorem sum_window_ge {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {a b : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) : ((a : ℝ) ^ (-r) - (b : ℝ) ^ (-r)) / r ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico a b, (j : ℝ) ^ (-r - 1)

decls.name: sum_window_le
decls.statement: theorem sum_window_le {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {a b : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico a b, (j : ℝ) ^ (-r - 1) ≤ (a : ℝ) ^ (-r - 1) + ((a : ℝ) ^ (-r) - (b : ℝ) ^ (-r)) / r

files.title: No bound on the sampling error can hold for a divergence-based FM loss: the cyclic counter-example

decls.name: cycV
decls.statement: abbrev cycV (M : ℕ)
decls.doc: The vertices of the cyclic graph `C_N`, `N = M + 2`: `none` is `s₀`, `some none` is `s_f`, and `some (some i)` is the internal state `x_{i+1}`.

decls.name: srcC
decls.statement: def srcC (M : ℕ) : cycV M
decls.doc: The source `s₀`.

decls.name: snkC
decls.statement: def snkC (M : ℕ) : cycV M
decls.doc: The sink `s_f`.

decls.name: xC
decls.statement: def xC (M : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 2)) : cycV M
decls.doc: The internal state `x_{i+1}`; `xC M 0` is the paper's `x₁` and `xC M 1` its `x₂`.

decls.name: xC_inj
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem xC_inj {i j : Fin (M + 2)} : xC M i = xC M j ↔ i = j

decls.name: xC_injective
decls.statement: theorem xC_injective (M : ℕ) : Function.Injective (xC M)

decls.name: xC_ne_srcC
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem xC_ne_srcC (i : Fin (M + 2)) : xC M i ≠ srcC M

decls.name: xC_ne_snkC
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem xC_ne_snkC (i : Fin (M + 2)) : xC M i ≠ snkC M

decls.name: srcC_ne_xC
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem srcC_ne_xC (i : Fin (M + 2)) : srcC M ≠ xC M i

decls.name: snkC_ne_xC
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem snkC_ne_xC (i : Fin (M + 2)) : snkC M ≠ xC M i

decls.name: srcC_ne_snkC
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem srcC_ne_snkC : srcC M ≠ snkC M

decls.name: snkC_ne_srcC
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem snkC_ne_srcC : snkC M ≠ srcC M

decls.name: cycV_cases
decls.statement: theorem cycV_cases {p : cycV M → Prop} (hs : p (srcC M)) (ht : p (snkC M)) (hx : ∀ i, p (xC M i)) : ∀ v, p v
decls.doc: Case analysis on a vertex, in the paper's names.

decls.name: sum_cycV
decls.statement: theorem sum_cycV (f : cycV M → ℝ) : ∑ v, f v = f (srcC M) + (f (snkC M) + ∑ i, f (xC M i))
decls.doc: Every sum over the vertices splits into the two marks and the `N` internal states.

decls.name: cycEdge
decls.statement: def cycEdge (M : ℕ) (u v : cycV M) : Prop
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the graph `𝒞_N`** (`proofs.tex:387`): the initial edge `s₀ → x₁`, a terminal edge `xᵢ → s_f` for every `i`, and the cycle edges `xᵢ → x_{i+1 mod N}`.

decls.name: cycGraph
decls.statement: def cycGraph (M : ℕ) : MarkedGraph (cycV M)
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the marked graph `𝒞_N`**: `s₀` receives no edge (the three edge families all end at an internal state or at `s_f`) and `s_f` emits none.

decls.name: cycGraph_src
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem cycGraph_src : (cycGraph M).src = srcC M

decls.name: cycGraph_snk
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem cycGraph_snk : (cycGraph M).snk = snkC M

decls.name: cycGraph_edge_iff
decls.statement: theorem cycGraph_edge_iff {u v : cycV M} : (cycGraph M).Edge u v ↔ cycEdge M u v

decls.name: internal_eq
decls.statement: theorem internal_eq (M : ℕ) : (cycGraph M).internal = Finset.univ.map ⟨xC M, xC_injective M⟩
decls.doc: The internal state space `𝒮 = 𝒱 ∖ {s₀, s_f}` is exactly the `N` states `x₁,…,x_N`.

decls.name: sum_internal
decls.statement: theorem sum_internal (f : cycV M → ℝ) : ∑ x ∈ (cycGraph M).internal, f x = ∑ i, f (xC M i)
decls.doc: A sum over `𝒮` is a sum over the `N` internal indices.

decls.name: mem_internal_iff
decls.statement: theorem mem_internal_iff {v : cycV M} : v ∈ (cycGraph M).internal ↔ ∃ i, v = xC M i
decls.doc: Membership in `𝒮`, in the paper's names.

decls.name: card_internal
decls.statement: theorem card_internal (M : ℕ) : (cycGraph M).internal.card = M + 2
decls.doc: **`#𝒞_N = N`**: the graph has exactly `N = M + 2` internal states, which is what the supremum of `theo:no_bound_divergence` ranges over.

decls.name: unitEdge
decls.statement: def unitEdge [DecidableEq V] (a b : V) : V → V → ℝ
decls.doc: The edgeflow carrying mass `1` on the single transition `a → b` and nothing elsewhere.

decls.name: unitEdge_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem unitEdge_nonneg (a b u v : V) : 0 ≤ unitEdge a b u v

decls.name: unitEdge_eq_zero_of_ne
decls.statement: theorem unitEdge_eq_zero_of_ne {a b u v : V} (h : ¬ (u = a ∧ v = b)) : unitEdge a b u v = 0

decls.name: unitEdge_of_ne_zero
decls.statement: theorem unitEdge_of_ne_zero {a b u v : V} (h : unitEdge a b u v ≠ 0) : u = a ∧ v = b

decls.name: edgeInflow_unitEdge
decls.statement: theorem edgeInflow_unitEdge (a b v : V) : edgeInflow (unitEdge a b) v = if v = b then 1 else 0

decls.name: edgeOutflow_unitEdge
decls.statement: theorem edgeOutflow_unitEdge (a b u : V) : edgeOutflow (unitEdge a b) u = if u = a then 1 else 0

decls.name: edgeInflow_add
decls.statement: theorem edgeInflow_add (F G : V → V → ℝ) (v : V) : edgeInflow (F + G) v = edgeInflow F v + edgeInflow G v

decls.name: edgeOutflow_add
decls.statement: theorem edgeOutflow_add (F G : V → V → ℝ) (u : V) : edgeOutflow (F + G) u = edgeOutflow F u + edgeOutflow G u

decls.name: unitEdge_eq_zero_of_ne_left
decls.statement: theorem unitEdge_eq_zero_of_ne_left {a b u : V} (h : u ≠ a) (v : V) : unitEdge a b u v = 0

decls.name: unitEdge_eq_zero_of_ne_right
decls.statement: theorem unitEdge_eq_zero_of_ne_right {a b v : V} (h : v ≠ b) (u : V) : unitEdge a b u v = 0

decls.name: unitEdge_left
decls.statement: theorem unitEdge_left (a b v : V) : unitEdge a b a v = if v = b then 1 else 0

decls.name: unitEdge_right
decls.statement: theorem unitEdge_right (a b u : V) : unitEdge a b u b = if u = a then 1 else 0

decls.name: Fhat
decls.statement: noncomputable def Fhat (M : ℕ) : cycV M → cycV M → ℝ
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the flow `F̂`** (`proofs.tex:388`): the unit-mass flow routed `s₀ → x₁ → x₂ → s_f`.

decls.name: Fhat_apply
decls.statement: theorem Fhat_apply (u v : cycV M) : Fhat M u v = unitEdge (srcC M) (xC M 0) u v + unitEdge (xC M 0) (xC M 1) u v + unitEdge (xC M 1) (snkC M) u v

decls.name: gammaC
decls.statement: noncomputable def gammaC (M : ℕ) : cycV M → cycV M → ℝ
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the unit circulation `γ`** (`proofs.tex:388`): `γ = 1` on each cycle edge `xᵢ → x_{i+1}`, `0` elsewhere.

decls.name: gammaC_apply
decls.statement: theorem gammaC_apply (u v : cycV M) : gammaC M u v = ∑ i, unitEdge (xC M i) (xC M (i + 1)) u v

decls.name: Fhat_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem Fhat_nonneg (u v : cycV M) : 0 ≤ Fhat M u v

decls.name: gammaC_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem gammaC_nonneg (u v : cycV M) : 0 ≤ gammaC M u v

decls.name: gammaC_srcC
decls.statement: theorem gammaC_srcC (u : cycV M) : gammaC M u (srcC M) = 0

decls.name: gammaC_snkC
decls.statement: theorem gammaC_snkC (u : cycV M) : gammaC M u (snkC M) = 0

decls.name: Fhat_srcC
decls.statement: theorem Fhat_srcC (u : cycV M) : Fhat M u (srcC M) = 0

decls.name: Fhat_snkC
decls.statement: theorem Fhat_snkC (u : cycV M) : Fhat M u (snkC M) = if u = xC M 1 then 1 else 0

decls.name: edgeInflow_Fhat
decls.statement: theorem edgeInflow_Fhat (v : cycV M) : edgeInflow (Fhat M) v = (if v = xC M 0 then 1 else 0) + (if v = xC M 1 then 1 else 0) + (if v = snkC M then 1 else 0)

decls.name: edgeOutflow_Fhat
decls.statement: theorem edgeOutflow_Fhat (u : cycV M) : edgeOutflow (Fhat M) u = (if u = srcC M then 1 else 0) + (if u = xC M 0 then 1 else 0) + (if u = xC M 1 then 1 else 0)

decls.name: edgeInflow_gammaC
decls.statement: theorem edgeInflow_gammaC (v : cycV M) : edgeInflow (gammaC M) v = ∑ i, (if v = xC M (i + 1) then (1 : ℝ) else 0)

decls.name: edgeOutflow_gammaC
decls.statement: theorem edgeOutflow_gammaC (u : cycV M) : edgeOutflow (gammaC M) u = ∑ i, (if u = xC M i then (1 : ℝ) else 0)

decls.name: edgeInflow_gammaC_x
decls.statement: theorem edgeInflow_gammaC_x (j : Fin (M + 2)) : edgeInflow (gammaC M) (xC M j) = 1

decls.name: edgeOutflow_gammaC_x
decls.statement: theorem edgeOutflow_gammaC_x (i : Fin (M + 2)) : edgeOutflow (gammaC M) (xC M i) = 1

decls.name: edgeInflow_gammaC_srcC
decls.statement: theorem edgeInflow_gammaC_srcC : edgeInflow (gammaC M) (srcC M) = 0

decls.name: edgeInflow_gammaC_snkC
decls.statement: theorem edgeInflow_gammaC_snkC : edgeInflow (gammaC M) (snkC M) = 0

decls.name: edgeOutflow_gammaC_srcC
decls.statement: theorem edgeOutflow_gammaC_srcC : edgeOutflow (gammaC M) (srcC M) = 0

decls.name: edgeOutflow_gammaC_snkC
decls.statement: theorem edgeOutflow_gammaC_snkC : edgeOutflow (gammaC M) (snkC M) = 0

decls.name: isCirculation_gammaC
decls.statement: theorem isCirculation_gammaC (M : ℕ) : IsCirculation (gammaC M)
decls.doc: **`γ` is a `0`-flow** (`proofs.tex:388`): every internal state gains `1` and loses `1`, and the cycle touches neither mark.

decls.name: gammaMC
decls.statement: noncomputable def gammaMC (M : ℕ) : MarkedCirculation (cycGraph M)
decls.doc: **`γ` as the `MarkedCirculation` of `GFNBounds.Graph`** — the hypothesis bundle `prop:frozen_unstable_full` consumes of its own `1_γ`, here discharged rather than assumed.

decls.name: Fk
decls.statement: noncomputable def Fk (M : ℕ) (k : ℝ) : cycV M → cycV M → ℝ
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the family `F_k := F̂ + kγ`** (`proofs.tex:388`).

decls.name: edgeInflow_Fk
decls.statement: theorem edgeInflow_Fk (k : ℝ) (v : cycV M) : edgeInflow (Fk M k) v = edgeInflow (Fhat M) v + k * edgeInflow (gammaC M) v

decls.name: edgeOutflow_Fk
decls.statement: theorem edgeOutflow_Fk (k : ℝ) (u : cycV M) : edgeOutflow (Fk M k) u = edgeOutflow (Fhat M) u + k * edgeOutflow (gammaC M) u

decls.name: Fk_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem Fk_nonneg {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) (u v : cycV M) : 0 ≤ Fk M k u v

decls.name: Fk_srcC
decls.statement: theorem Fk_srcC (k : ℝ) (u : cycV M) : Fk M k u (srcC M) = 0

decls.name: Fk_snkC
decls.statement: theorem Fk_snkC (k : ℝ) (u : cycV M) : Fk M k u (snkC M) = if u = xC M 1 then 1 else 0

decls.name: Fk_supp
decls.statement: theorem Fk_supp {k : ℝ} {u v : cycV M} (h : Fk M k u v ≠ 0) : (cycGraph M).Edge u v
decls.doc: Every transition `F_k` charges is an edge of `𝒞_N`: `F̂` rides on the initial edge, one cycle edge and one terminal edge, and `γ` on the cycle.

decls.name: Fk_flowMatching
decls.statement: theorem Fk_flowMatching (k : ℝ) : ∀ x ∈ (cycGraph M).internal, edgeInflow (Fk M k) x = edgeOutflow (Fk M k) x
decls.doc: **`F_k` is flow-matching for every `k`** (`proofs.tex:388`): the circulation adds `k` to the inflow and `k` to the outflow of every internal state, so the constraint `equ:FM_const` at `𝒮` — which on a marked graph is conservation at the internal states — is untouched.

decls.name: zero_ne_one_fin
decls.statement: theorem zero_ne_one_fin (M : ℕ) : (0 : Fin (M + 2)) ≠ 1

decls.name: sum_fin_ite_zero
decls.statement: theorem sum_fin_ite_zero (A B : ℝ) : ∑ i : Fin (M + 2), (if i = 0 then A else B) = A + ((M : ℝ) + 1) * B

decls.name: sum_fin_ite_two
decls.statement: theorem sum_fin_ite_two (A B C : ℝ) : ∑ i : Fin (M + 2), (if i = 0 then A else if i = 1 then B else C) = A + B + (M : ℝ) * C

decls.name: targetC
decls.statement: noncomputable def targetC (M : ℕ) (delta : ℝ) : cycV M → ℝ
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the target** (`proofs.tex:387`): `target(x₁) = 1 − δ` and `target(xᵢ) = δ/(N−1)` for `i ≥ 2`, with `N − 1 = M + 1`.

decls.name: targetC_srcC
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem targetC_srcC (delta : ℝ) : targetC M delta (srcC M) = 0

decls.name: targetC_snkC
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem targetC_snkC (delta : ℝ) : targetC M delta (snkC M) = 0

decls.name: targetC_x
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem targetC_x (delta : ℝ) (i : Fin (M + 2)) : targetC M delta (xC M i) = if i = 0 then 1 - delta else delta / ((M : ℝ) + 1)

decls.name: sum_targetC
decls.statement: theorem sum_targetC (delta : ℝ) : ∑ v, targetC M delta v = 1
decls.doc: **The target is a probability measure on `𝒮`**: `(1 − δ) + (N − 1)·δ/(N − 1) = 1`.

decls.name: fmRatio
decls.statement: noncomputable def fmRatio (G : MarkedGraph V) (target : V → ℝ) (F : V → V → ℝ) (x : V) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the ratio of the two sides of `equ:FM_const`** (`proofs.tex:393`): `ρ(x) = (F_init + f_←)(x)/(target + f_→)(x)`, with the **target** in the denominator in place of the flow's own terminal flow.

decls.name: fmLossTarget
decls.statement: noncomputable def fmLossTarget (G : MarkedGraph V) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (nu target : V → ℝ) (F : V → V → ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, a divergence-based FM loss** (`proofs.tex:393`): `𝓛(F) = ∫ g(ρ) dν_train`, the integral over the internal states of a generator `g` of the ratio of the two sides of the flow-matching constraint.

decls.name: aC
decls.statement: noncomputable def aC (M : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 2)) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The numerators `aᵢ` of `proofs.tex:395`**: `a₁ = a₂ = 1`, `aᵢ = 0` for `i ≥ 3`.

decls.name: bC
decls.statement: noncomputable def bC (M : ℕ) (delta : ℝ) (i : Fin (M + 2)) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The denominators `bᵢ` of `proofs.tex:395`**: `b₁ = 2 − δ`, `bᵢ = δ/(N−1)` for `i ≥ 2`.

decls.name: sum_internal_row
decls.statement: theorem sum_internal_row (F : cycV M → cycV M → ℝ) (u : cycV M) : ∑ v ∈ (cycGraph M).internal, F u v = edgeOutflow F u - F u (srcC M) - F u (snkC M)

decls.name: indicator_add
decls.statement: theorem indicator_add (j : Fin (M + 2)) : (if j = 0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0) + (if j = 1 then (1 : ℝ) else 0) = aC M j
decls.doc: `aᵢ` is the sum of the two indicators `F̂` contributes to the inflow at `xᵢ`.

decls.name: edgeInflow_Fk_x
decls.statement: theorem edgeInflow_Fk_x (k : ℝ) (j : Fin (M + 2)) : edgeInflow (Fk M k) (xC M j) = aC M j + k
decls.doc: **The numerator of `ρ_k` at an internal state**: `(F_init + f^k_←)(xᵢ) = aᵢ + k`.

decls.name: foutC_Fk_x
decls.statement: theorem foutC_Fk_x (k : ℝ) (j : Fin (M + 2)) : ∑ v ∈ (cycGraph M).internal, Fk M k (xC M j) v = (if j = 0 then 1 else 0) + k
decls.doc: **The outflow half of the denominator**: `f^k_→(xᵢ) = 1_{i=1} + k`, the circulation adding `k` at every internal state.

decls.name: fmRatio_Fk
decls.statement: theorem fmRatio_Fk (k delta : ℝ) (j : Fin (M + 2)) : fmRatio (cycGraph M) (targetC M delta) (Fk M k) (xC M j) = (aC M j + k) / (bC M delta j + k)
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the closed form of the ratio** (`proofs.tex:395`): `ρ_k(xᵢ) = (aᵢ + k)/(bᵢ + k)`, with `a₁ = a₂ = 1`, `aᵢ = 0` for `i ≥ 3`, `b₁ = 2 − δ` and `bᵢ = δ/(N−1)` for `i ≥ 2`.

decls.name: tendsto_affine_ratio
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_affine_ratio (a b : ℝ) : Filter.Tendsto (fun k : ℝ => (a + k) / (b + k)) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)
decls.doc: **`ρ_k → 1`** (`proofs.tex:395`): a quotient of two affine functions of `k` with the same slope tends to `1`, whatever the intercepts — this is the scale invariance along `0`-flows.

decls.name: fmRatio_Fk_tendsto_one
decls.statement: theorem fmRatio_Fk_tendsto_one (delta : ℝ) (j : Fin (M + 2)) : Filter.Tendsto (fun k : ℝ => fmRatio (cycGraph M) (targetC M delta) (Fk M k) (xC M j)) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

decls.name: fmLossTarget_Fk_tendsto_zero
decls.statement: theorem fmLossTarget_Fk_tendsto_zero (g : ℝ → ℝ) (hg1 : g 1 = 0) (hgc : ContinuousAt g 1) (nu : cycV M → ℝ) (delta : ℝ) : Filter.Tendsto (fun k : ℝ => fmLossTarget (cycGraph M) g nu (targetC M delta) (Fk M k)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
decls.doc: **`𝓛(F_k) → 0`** (`proofs.tex:396`): a finite sum of terms `ν(x) g(ρ_k(x))`, each tending to `ν(x) g(1) = 0` by continuity of `g` at `1`.

decls.name: exists_Fk_loss_le
decls.statement: theorem exists_Fk_loss_le (g : ℝ → ℝ) (hg1 : g 1 = 0) (hgc : ContinuousAt g 1) (nu : cycV M → ℝ) (delta : ℝ) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) : ∃ k : ℝ, 0 ≤ k ∧ fmLossTarget (cycGraph M) g nu (targetC M delta) (Fk M k) ≤ eps
decls.doc: **`𝓛(F_k) ≤ ε` for `k` large** (`proofs.tex:396`).

decls.name: termLaw
decls.statement: noncomputable def termLaw (G : MarkedGraph V) (F : V → V → ℝ) : V → ℝ
decls.doc: The **normalized terminal flow** of an edgeflow, `F(·→s_f)/F(𝒮→s_f)`.

decls.name: tvFin
decls.statement: noncomputable def tvFin (p q : V → ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The `½`-convention total variation of `app:notation` between two densities on a finite state space, `TV(p‖q) = ½ ∑ |p − q|`.

decls.name: sum_termFlow_Fk
decls.statement: theorem sum_termFlow_Fk (k : ℝ) : ∑ y, Fk M k y (snkC M) = 1

decls.name: termLaw_Fk
decls.statement: theorem termLaw_Fk (k : ℝ) (x : cycV M) : termLaw (cycGraph M) (Fk M k) x = if x = xC M 1 then 1 else 0
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the terminal law is `δ_{x₂}` for every `k`** (`proofs.tex:388`): the circulation charges no terminal edge, so `F_k` and `F̂` have the same terminal flow `μ = δ_{x₂}`, of mass `1`.

decls.name: tvFin_termLaw_Fk
decls.statement: theorem tvFin_termLaw_Fk (k : ℝ) {delta : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ delta) (h1 : delta ≤ 1) : tvFin (termLaw (cycGraph M) (Fk M k)) (targetC M delta) = 1 - delta / ((M : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the total variation is `1 − δ/(N−1)`** (`proofs.tex:390`): `TV(δ_{x₂} ‖ target) = 1 − target(x₂)`.

decls.name: no_bound_divergence
decls.statement: theorem no_bound_divergence (M : ℕ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (hg1 : g 1 = 0) (hgc : ContinuousAt g 1) (nu : cycV M → ℝ) {delta eps : ℝ} (hd0 : 0 < delta) (hd1 : delta < 1) (heps : 0 < eps) : ∃ F : cycV M → cycV M → ℝ, (∀ u v, 0 ≤ F u v) ∧ (∀ u v, F u v ≠ 0 → (cycGraph M).Edge u v) ∧ (∀ x ∈ (cycGraph M).internal, edgeInflow F x = edgeOutflow F x) ∧ fmLossTarget (cycGraph M) g nu (targetC M delta) F ≤ eps ∧ tvFin (termLaw (cycGraph M) F) (targetC M delta) = 1 - delta / ((M : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`** — `cv_divergence.tex:7–19`, proof `proofs.tex:385–400` — on the cyclic graph `𝒞_N`, `N = M + 2`.

decls.name: no_bound_divergence_sup
decls.statement: theorem no_bound_divergence_sup (M : ℕ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (hg1 : g 1 = 0) (hgc : ContinuousAt g 1) (nu : cycV M → ℝ) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) {eta : ℝ} (heta : eta < 1) : ∃ (delta : ℝ) (F : cycV M → cycV M → ℝ), 0 < delta ∧ delta < 1 ∧ (∀ u v, 0 ≤ F u v) ∧ (∀ u v, F u v ≠ 0 → (cycGraph M).Edge u v) ∧ (∀ x ∈ (cycGraph M).internal, edgeInflow F x = edgeOutflow F x) ∧ fmLossTarget (cycGraph M) g nu (targetC M delta) F ≤ eps ∧ eta < tvFin (termLaw (cycGraph M) F) (targetC M delta)
decls.doc: **`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the `= 1` reading**: the supremum is not attained but is `1`, because `δ` is free.

decls.name: exists_cycle_of_size
decls.statement: theorem exists_cycle_of_size (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ≤ N) : ∃ M : ℕ, (cycGraph M).internal.card = N
decls.doc: **The supremum ranges over graphs of size `N`**: for every `N ≥ 2` the family above contains a graph with exactly `N` internal states, which is what `#𝒢 = N` asks.

decls.name: ratio_eq_fmRatio
decls.statement: theorem ratio_eq_fmRatio (G : MarkedGraph V) (target : V → ℝ) (F : V → V → ℝ) (hF : ∀ x, target x + (∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v) = 0 → ∀ y, F x y = 0) (y : V) : Balance.ratio (fun x y => F x y / (target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v)) (fun x => target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v) 1 y = fmRatio G target F y
decls.doc: **The ratio `ρ` is `GFNBounds.Balance`'s `r = d(μT)/dμ`** at `λ := target + f_→`, `u := 1` and the kernel `T(x→y) := F(x→y)/λ(x)` normalising each row of the flow.

decls.name: fmLossTarget_eq_loss
decls.statement: theorem fmLossTarget_eq_loss (G : MarkedGraph V) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (nu target : V → ℝ) (F : V → V → ℝ) (hF : ∀ x, target x + (∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v) = 0 → ∀ y, F x y = 0) : fmLossTarget G g nu target F = Balance.loss (fun x y => F x y / (target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v)) (fun x => target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v) (fun x => if x ∈ G.internal then nu x else 0) 1 g
decls.doc: **`fmLossTarget` is `GFNBounds.Balance.loss`**, not a new notion: the divergence FM loss of `theo:no_bound_divergence` is the library's `𝓛_{g,ν}(μ) = ∑_x ν(x) g(r(x))` at the kernel and reference measure above, with `ν` extended by `0` off the internal states.

decls.name: Fk_snk_row
decls.statement: theorem Fk_snk_row (k : ℝ) (y : cycV M) : Fk M k (snkC M) y = 0
decls.doc: `s_f` emits nothing under `F_k` — it emits nothing in `𝒞_N`.

decls.name: foutC_Fk_srcC
decls.statement: theorem foutC_Fk_srcC (k : ℝ) : ∑ v ∈ (cycGraph M).internal, Fk M k (srcC M) v = 1
decls.doc: `F_k` sends unit mass out of `s₀`, along the initial edge: `F_init(𝒮) = 1`.

decls.name: Fk_lam_ne_zero
decls.statement: theorem Fk_lam_ne_zero {k delta : ℝ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hd0 : 0 < delta) (hd1 : delta < 1) : ∀ x, targetC M delta x + (∑ v ∈ (cycGraph M).internal, Fk M k x v) = 0 → ∀ y, Fk M k x y = 0

decls.name: tvFin_eq_tvD_count
decls.statement: theorem tvFin_eq_tvD_count [MeasurableSpace V] [MeasurableSingletonClass V] (p q : V → ℝ) : tvFin p q = Core.tvD MeasureTheory.Measure.count p q
decls.doc: **`tvFin` is `GFNBounds.Core.tvD` against the counting measure** — the `½`-convention TV of `app:notation` read on a finite state space, so the value `1 − δ/(N−1)` above is the paper's `TV(s_τ ‖ target)` and not a separate notion.

files.title: A five-vertex cycle: the frozen policy and the inflation force never deadlock

decls.name: edgeB
decls.statement: def edgeB : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → Bool
decls.doc: The edges of the remark's graph: `s₀ → x₁`, the cycle `x₁ → x₂ → x₃ → x₁`, and `x₃ → s_f`.

decls.name: Edge
decls.statement: def Edge (x y : Fin 5) : Prop
decls.doc: The edge relation of the remark's graph, as a decidable `Prop`.

decls.statement: instance : DecidableRel Edge

decls.name: cyc
decls.statement: def cyc : MarkedGraph (Fin 5)
decls.doc: **`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the graph**: `𝒱 = {s₀,x₁,x₂,x₃,s_f}` with `s₀ → x₁`, the cycle `x₁ → x₂ → x₃ → x₁` and `x₃ → s_f`.

decls.name: pathConnected
decls.statement: theorem pathConnected : cyc.PathConnected
decls.doc: **`rem:cycle_no_stalemate` is path-connected** (`def:path_connected`), the hypothesis every result cited below carries.

decls.name: pbFun
decls.statement: noncomputable def pbFun (p : ℝ) : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℝ
decls.doc: **`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the frozen policy**: `π_←(x₁→x₃) = p`, `π_←(x₁→s₀) = 1−p`, and the three remaining rows deterministic — `π_←(x₂→x₁) = π_←(x₃→x₂) = π_←(s_f→x₃) = 1`.

decls.name: pol
decls.statement: noncomputable def pol {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) : BackwardPolicy cyc
decls.doc: **`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the frozen policy as a `BackwardPolicy`.** Of the three fields only non-negativity constrains `p`, and it asks for `0 ≤ p` and `p ≤ 1`; the row sum `(1−p) + p = 1` at `x₁` and the support condition are identities.

decls.name: positiveOnEdges
decls.statement: theorem positiveOnEdges {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) : (pol hp0 hp1).PositiveOnEdges
decls.doc: **`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the frozen policy is positive on the edges** — the hypothesis of `theo:universality_graphs` and of `prop:morozov_rate`.

decls.name: kern
decls.statement: noncomputable def kern (p : ℝ) : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℝ
decls.doc: The loop-closed kernel `π̂_←` of the remark, written out: the wrap row `π̂_←(s₀→s_f) = 1` (`def:loop_closure`) on top of `pbFun`.

decls.name: phat_eq
decls.statement: theorem phat_eq {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) : (pol hp0 hp1).phat = kern p
decls.doc: **`def:loop_closure` on this graph**: `π̂_←` is `kern p`.

decls.name: hitExp
decls.statement: noncomputable def hitExp (p : ℝ) : Fin 5 → ℝ
decls.doc: `E(σ ∣ X₀ = ·)`, the hitting time of `s₀` by the backward chain, in closed form: `0` at `s₀`, `(1+2p)/(1−p)` at `x₁`, `(2+p)/(1−p)` at `x₂`, `3/(1−p)` at `x₃` and `(4−p)/(1−p)` at `s_f`.

decls.name: isHitExp
decls.statement: theorem isHitExp {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) : (pol hp0 hp1).IsHitExp (hitExp p)
decls.doc: **`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the backward-trajectory length**: `hitExp p` solves the linear system `IsHitExp` of `prop:morozov_rate` — `u(s₀) = 0` and `u = 1 + Qu` off `s₀`.

decls.name: hitExp_unique
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_unique {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) {u : Fin 5 → ℝ} (hu : (pol hp0 hp1).IsHitExp u) : u = hitExp p
decls.doc: `hitExp p` is *the* solution: `prop:morozov_rate`'s system has at most one.

decls.name: hitExp_x1
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_x1 (p : ℝ) : hitExp p 1 = (1 + 2 * p) / (1 - p)
decls.doc: **The number the remark printed before its 2026-09-08 correction**, `(1+2p)/(1−p)`, is `E(σ ∣ X₀ = x₁)` — the expected hitting time of `s₀` from the far end of the cycle, not the backward-trajectory length.

decls.name: sigmaBar_eq
decls.statement: theorem sigmaBar_eq {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) : (pol hp0 hp1).sigmaBar (hitExp p) = 3 / (1 - p)
decls.doc: **`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 1, corrected.** The expected backward-trajectory length `σ̄ = E_{x ∼ π̂_←(s_f→·)} E(σ ∣ X₀ = x)` of `prop:morozov_rate` is `3/(1−p)`: the target row `π̂_←(s_f→·)` is the point mass at `x₃`, so `σ̄ = E(σ ∣ X₀ = x₃)`, and a backward excursion runs `x₃ → x₂ → x₁` and leaves to `s₀` with probability `1 − p` each lap.

decls.name: sigmaBar_ne_paper_value
decls.statement: theorem sigmaBar_ne_paper_value {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) : (pol hp0 hp1).sigmaBar (hitExp p) ≠ (1 + 2 * p) / (1 - p)
decls.doc: **The value the remark used to give for `σ̄` is not `σ̄`.** `3/(1−p) = (1+2p)/(1−p)` forces `p = 1`, which the hypothesis excludes, so the two disagree at *every* `p ∈ (0,1)`.

decls.name: sigmaBar_unbounded
decls.statement: theorem sigmaBar_unbounded (C : ℝ) : ∃ p : ℝ, 0 < p ∧ p < 1 ∧ C < 3 / (1 - p)
decls.doc: **`σ̄` is unbounded on `(0,1)`** — the certified half of the remark's closing clause "as `p → 1` the backward-length bound blows up".

decls.name: sigmaStar_eq
decls.statement: theorem sigmaStar_eq {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) : sigmaStar cyc (hitExp p) = (4 - p) / (1 - p)
decls.doc: `σ_* = max_x E(σ ∣ X₀ = x) = (4−p)/(1−p)`, attained at `s_f`.

decls.name: lam
decls.statement: noncomputable def lam (p : ℝ) : Fin 5 → ℝ
decls.doc: The invariant probability of the backward chain: `q = 1/(5−2p)` at each of `x₁, x₂, x₃` and `(1−p)q` at `s₀` and `s_f`.

decls.name: isInvProb
decls.statement: theorem isInvProb {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) : (pol hp0 hp1).IsInvProb (lam p)
decls.doc: **`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 2**: `lam p` is an invariant probability of the loop-closed backward chain.

decls.name: invProb_eq
decls.statement: theorem invProb_eq {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) {l : Fin 5 → ℝ} (hl : (pol hp0 hp1).IsInvProb l) : l = lam p
decls.doc: **`theo:universality_graphs`*(1)* on this graph**: `lam p` is *the* invariant probability.

decls.name: invProb_paper
decls.statement: theorem invProb_paper {p : ℝ} (hp1 : p < 1) : ∃ q : ℝ, 0 < q ∧ lam p 1 = q ∧ lam p 2 = q ∧ lam p 3 = q ∧ lam p 0 = (1 - p) * q ∧ lam p 4 = (1 - p) * q
decls.doc: **`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 2 in the remark's own words**: there is a `q > 0` with mass `q` at each of the three cycle states and `(1−p)q` at `s₀` and at `s_f`.

decls.name: green
decls.statement: noncomputable def green (p : ℝ) : Fin 5 → ℝ
decls.doc: The occupation measure `N` of `prop:morozov_rate`, killed at `s₀`: `g ≡ 1/(1−p)` on the cycle and `0` at the two marks.

decls.name: isGreen
decls.statement: theorem isGreen {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) : (pol hp0 hp1).IsGreen (green p)
decls.doc: **`green p` solves `prop:morozov_rate`'s renewal equation** `g(s₀) = 0`, `g = π̂_←(s_f→·) + gP̂` off `s₀`.

decls.name: two_add_sigmaBar_eq
